articles.title: Secretary Rubio has a tough time getting officials at G20 on the same page
articles.author: Michele Kelemen

paras.en: Secretary Rubio has a tough time getting officials at G20 on the same page
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is hosting the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, with a focus on economic and security challenges.
Tensions flared this weekend at a meeting chaired by Secretary of State Marco Rubio of the Group of 20 leading economies. NPR's Michele Kelemen reports from Atlanta.

MICHELE KELEMEN, BYLINE: There was no joint communiqué or even a family photo. Several foreign ministers did not want to be in a picture with Russia's Sergey Lavrov. So Rubio canceled plans for that, but he says countries did come together around some big themes, including freedom of navigation.

MARCO RUBIO: Safe passage of vessels in international waters is vital to the livelihood of the world. And we now live in a world where the Iranian regime actively and openly targets commercial vessels.
KELEMEN: He says the U.S. is open to diplomacy with Iran, but he wouldn't rule out a new round of attacks, even as the U.S. military tries to keep the Strait of Hormuz open.

RUBIO: Central Command in the United States has done a phenomenal job of protecting this shipping. And today, the amount of fuel getting through there is comparable with what was coming out before the conflict. But nonetheless, we've had to defend these ships from drones and missiles almost every single night.

KELEMEN: Other G20 countries are worried about the potential for a new escalation in the Middle East. Europeans are also nervous about U.S. sanctions relief to Russia. Germany's foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, is trying to highlight the positive, saying, while they may not agree on tactics, everyone shares the goal of getting Russia to the negotiating table to end the war in Ukraine.
JOHANN WADEPHUL: In the substance, we have the same position, not only in Europe, but together also with the United States of America. And for us, Marco Rubio was always a reliable partner.

KELEMEN: Rubio did meet briefly with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, who's been making light over the dispute over the family photo and defending Russia's war in Ukraine. Russia has long blamed the West for provoking Moscow. Poland's foreign minister, Radek Sikorski, has heard it all before.
RADEK SIKORSKI: Sergey Lavrov's repeated diatribes against Europe suggests to me that they've realized that Europe has cards.

KELEMEN: Europe, he says, has Russia's frozen assets, and it's buying weapons from the U.S. for Ukraine. Poland is lobbying to become a member of the G20 over Russia's objections. Sikorski says he used his time here to push for a ceasefire in the Black Sea.
SIKORSKI: So that both Ukrainian and Russian grain could make it through the Bosphorus to the people who need it in Egypt and elsewhere.

KELEMEN: Secretary Rubio says he wouldn't place bets on whether such a ceasefire is possible, but he says there was a lot of interest around the table to do that. He also defended the decision to host Lavrov in Atlanta and to invite Russian president Vladimir Putin to the G20 summit in Florida, though it's not clear Putin will come.

RUBIO: We have to be able to talk to the Russian side, and one of the ways to do that is to invite him to forums like this, where they're not just hearing from us, but potentially hearing from other countries that are there as well.

KELEMEN: Secretary Rubio also met briefly with his counterpart from Brazil, breaking the ice after right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro lost the elections and fled to the U.S. Rubio says President Trump made the decision to allow Bolsonaro into the country, but the U.S. government did not facilitate the travel.

Accuracy and availability of transcripts for NPR programming may vary. Transcript text may also be revised to correct errors or match updates to audio. Audio may be edited after its original broadcast or publication. The authoritative record of NPR’s programming is the audio record.

articles.title: BYU survives unranked Arizona State's second-half rally, stays unbeaten at home

paras.en: Eighth-ranked BYU pulled away after Arizona State rallied to tie the game at 17 late in the third quarter. Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier threw for 236 yards and a touchdown to help secure the 27-20 victory.

The Cougars blanked the Sun Devils in the fourth quarter. After a 45-yard field goal put BYU ahead for good, running back Sione Moa scored from 1 yard out to seal the victory with just over two minutes remaining.
Arizona State quarterback Jake Fette finished the late afternoon with 166 yards and two touchdowns, but the Sun Devils suffered their third road loss to a top-10 opponent this season.

Fette threw two third-quarter touchdown passes as Arizona State erased a 14-point deficit. The Sun Devils converted three third downs on their first scoring drive, which ended with Omarion Miller’s 20-yard touchdown catch. They then converted two fourth downs on the next drive before Anthony Miller Jr.’s 1-yard scoring reception tied the game at 17.
Adrian Wilson recovered a fumble by Kyler Kasper at the BYU 39-yard line, setting up Arizona State’s second touchdown drive. It was a turbulent start for Fette in his first career start.
He fumbled on the third play of Arizona State’s opening drive. Isaiah Glasker pounced on the ball at the Sun Devil 29, setting up BYU’s first touchdown.
Ironically, the Cougars scored following another fumble. Moa scooped up the ball after Bachmeier coughed it up inside the ASU 1 and scampered over the goal line to put BYU up 7-0.
Next week, BYU will travel to Salt Lake City for an in-state rivalry game against Utah, while Arizona State will host Colorado in Tempe.
Earlier Saturday, Colorado survived a scare from Kansas State to win in overtime and snap the Buffaloes’ losing streak.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Bill Belichick's UNC Tar Heels nearly upset top-ranked Miami before costly strip-sack

paras.en: Bill Belichick, the day his UNC Tar Heels were set to face the No. 1 Miami Hurricanes in Chapel Hill, was the center of more off-field noise regarding his relationship.

This time, though, it was reported the 74-year-old actually ended things with 25-year-old Jordon Hudson over a year ago, per TMZ. They remain "committed to their business partnerships" and "remain close friends."
Nonetheless, a game had to be played, and Belichick and UNC were certainly not thinking about his relationship status. They wanted to give Miami a run for their money.

The Tar Heels came close to upsetting the Hurricanes, but they ran out of gas in the fourth quarter in a 38-35 loss to move to 4-4 on the season. Miami stayed undefeated, improving to 8-0 on the year and 6-0 in ACC play.

No one expected Belichick's squad to be able to handle the Hurricanes, led by Mario Cristobal. But just as Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah continued his efficient play this season, Billy Edwards Jr. was matching him when the Tar Heels had the ball.
Edwards threw for 341 yards on 28-of-34 through the air with four touchdown passes, including a 16-yard strike to Jordan Shipp to take a 21-17 lead — UNC’s first of the game — in the third quarter.

From there, both teams were trading blows, and the lead, on the scoreboard. Miami responded with an 80-yard drive to retake their lead, 24-21, but UNC continued to fight on while crushing clock heading into the fourth quarter.

Edwards led a 16-play, 75-yard drive capped with a touchdown run by Demon June from one yard out. There was a lot of time left in this ballgame, which Miami knew despite some shock of what UNC was doing to them at home.

Mensah wasn’t fazed, though, as yet another touchdown drive came from the Hurricanes thanks to key catch-and-runs, including a 31-yard burst from star receiver Malachi Toney. Mark Fletcher Jr. regained the Miami lead with a two-yard run and 7:49 left on the clock.
The way this game was going, it seemed Belichick and UNC would have a chance if they were able to get the ball last. However, a grave error slammed the door shut on those chances.

Edwards was strip-sacked by Marquise Lightfoot, and Miami recovered at the UNC 37-yard line. That was the defensive stop needed to swing the tides of momentum, and Mensah didn’t thwart that opportunity.

Toney caught a nine-yard touchdown pass from his quarterback, and with a 10-point lead with 2:33 left to go, it was eventually the separation needed to leave Chapel Hill without Miami’s record being blemished. But it didn’t come without sweating until the end.

UNC would score on the ensuing possession to make things interesting, as Edwards threw for his fourth touchdown of the game with 1:38 left to play. Then, needing to recover an onside kick, the Tar Heels actually came away with it — until a yellow flag was seen on the turf. Offsides was called.
On the second try, UNC recovered again, but another flag negated it as a Tar Heels player hit the Miami player trying to recover the ball before crossing the necessary 10 yards.
The third try was finally recovered by the Hurricanes, and they ran the clock out.
Mensah threw for 274 yards and three scores, while rushing for 36 yards. Toney had two of those touchdowns, hauling in seven receptions for 75 yards. Fletcher also scored three total touchdowns.

articles.title: Ohio State's national title hopes are rightfully fading after USC delivers reality check in shocking upset

paras.en: If the Big Ten was resting their hopes on Ohio State being able to put together an offense capable of contending for a national championship, then Saturday night's 30-18 loss to USC was a reality check on the current situation.

Following the unfortunate loss of starting quarterback Julian Sayin to an elbow injury during the Indiana game two weeks ago, the fate of the Buckeyes season rested on the arms of Luke Fahey and freshman Taven St. Clair.

The nervousness around Columbus has been rampant since that day in Bloomington, and rightfully so given that Ryan Day had pinned his offensive hopes around the quarterback being able to disrupt opposing defenses with the Julian Sayin to Jeremiah Smith connection.

This pair opened up so many options for an offense that essentially forced opposing teams to decide on whether double-teaming the star wide receiver was worth the risk in losing a defender in the secondary.
Even with 484 yards of total offense against USC on Saturday night, it was the offensive line that struggled to protect quarterback Luke Fahey, while also not capitalizing inside the red zone.

You might ask whether one player is worth that much attention. To that, most college football fans would just implore you to "watch the tape" on the former Heisman Trophy leader coming out of the Indiana showdown that saw the Buckeyes leave Bloomington with a very important win.

Now, a few weeks later, there are rightful questions about this Ohio State team moving forward over the next month, along with where the Big Ten stands as we await the first CFP rankings of the 2026 season.

The answer to that question centered around the fact Ohio State had not scored a touchdown against USC through three quarters, and they looked like a squad who was lost on offense for a majority of this upset loss.
Does Ohio State look like a national title contender without Julian Sayin?
No, not right now after two weeks of preparation for the trip to Los Angeles.
If anything, the Buckeyes look like a team that would be on the brink of missing the playoff tonight if Indiana were to have somehow won that intense showdown.
So yes, Ohio State fans are clearly entering the panic mode of what could have been if Julian Sayin were to not have been injured.

Also, let's not forget the other unfortunate part of this problem for the Buckeyes. Entering the matchup with Indiana, Jeremiah Smith was the proverbial leader in the clubhouse for the Heisman Trophy. Now, he's going to need plenty of superman-like efforts to have his name called in New York City next month, without a quarterback capable enough to get him the ball downfield.

Sure, we know Smith is a man of high character and is more worried about the wins and losses. But, let's not act as though the situation isn’t a brutal dose of reality that his campaign might have ended in Bloomington.
Fittingly, it was Jeremiah Smith who scored Ohio State's first touchdown of the night with 2:12 remaining in the game on a five-yard out in the end zone.
As for Ohio State moving forward, there is nothing about their performance against USC that should give the CFP committee enough evidence to put them in the top-12 on Tuesday night.
We all remember when Florida State was left out of the national championship game after Jordan Travis went down with a knee injury, right?
No, we aren’t at that point just yet, but we're getting there. Over the next five weeks, Ohio State will face Northwestern, Oregon, Nebraska and Michigan.

Are we going to act as though this Buckeyes offense is good enough to avoid another loss? Sure, you can make that argument, but Oregon and Northwestern are talented enough to beat them in Columbus, and Nebraska is so awkward that it could have a lead heading into the fourth quarter.
The Buckeyes defense isn’t strong enough to carry them through the month of November, especially if this is what they are going to get from the offensive side of the ball.
And unfortunately, Jeremiah Smith and running back Bo Jackson can't do it all without a viable quarterback that oozes confidence.
Lincoln Riley finds himself on the winning side, with a tough stretch ahead
Give credit where it's due with this USC football team.

Coming off a loss to Wisconsin this week, with reasonable conversations surrounding his job status with the Trojans, the talk of Riley coaching somewhere else next season started picking up enough that he could not avoid the questions over the past five days.
Now, there is at least a path to the postseason, though it won't be an easy one.
After a week off, USC will play Indiana on the road, followed by a game against Maryland, before ending the season with a crosstown showdown with UCLA.
Can they run the table? Sure, if this is the type of performance we get over the next month.
But, even with the win over Ohio State, it's still hard to trust the Trojans. They’re going to have to prove it.

articles.title: Tusk defends overhaul of Poland’s constitutional court despite protests
articles.author: Jakub Krupa

paras.en: Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, has vowed to see through a contested overhaul of the country’s constitutional court, declaring that “in certain matters, there can be no compromise”.

In a prime-time television address on Saturday night, Tusk was defiant, despite overnight protests that saw riot police drafted to protect the court’s building, saying the shake-up was vital to restore a tribunal crippled by years of political disputes.
Paralysed for more than a decade, the court sat at the core of rule of law clashes between the rightwing Law and Justice (PiS) party and the EU during the party’s eight-year rule.

Since returning to office in 2023, the centre-right Tusk has sought to unwind those judicial changes, but his agenda has been frustrated by opposition-aligned presidents with extensive veto powers. Earlier this year, president Karol Nawrocki refused to swear in five judges approved by parliament.

The crisis flared again on Friday when a group of government-backed judges attempted to seize procedural control of the tribunal, suspending the PiS-appointed chief judge and deputy and prompting street protests.
Defending the action, Tusk said “there was never any doubt that the court in the form imposed by PiS was not a genuine court”, citing adverse rulings from European tribunals.
He compared the opposition outrage to “a thief snatching an elderly woman’s handbag, running off, and when he is caught, he screams that he is subjected to violence”.

Tusk said: “Let’s call things for what they are: for years, there have been organisations and politicians in Poland who seek to destroy democracy and the rule of law. It is no coincidence they find support among pro-Russian forces globally.”

He later highlighted that Russia’s former president Dmitry Medvedev had joined the opposition in an outcry over the changes, accusing Warsaw of “a constitutional coup” and “hounding the conservatives”. “And everything is clear,” Tusk said.

He also criticised opposition-aligned Nawrocki for joining the protests on Friday night and forcing his entry into the court’s building to intervene. “In a democratic state, no politician can enter a court to issue orders or intimidate judges – not even the president,” Tusk said. “We Poles have succeeded too well in building a strong state to surrender now.”
He said it was the government’s duty to ensure its security and the conditions necessary for the court to operate. “And I intend to fulfil that duty,” he said.
On Saturday, the European Commission urged Nawrocki to approve the new judges who were nominated by parliament, so the court could function in line with the constitution and EU law.
The confrontation sets the battle lines before next year’s parliamentary election, with polls pointing to a close race between Tusk’s broad coalition and the nationalist right.
However, experts remain divided over whether the government’s procedural gambit at the court is lawful.
Poland’s Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights said on Saturday the legal basis for the temporary suspension was “questionable”, warning it would “not contribute” to restoring the court.

The foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, conceded that the events outside the court were “not elegant”, but insisted: “The alternative was to concede an unconstitutional transformation of Poland into a presidential republic.”

Nawrocki held some cross-party political talks on Saturday, with no apparent breakthrough. His senior aide, Zbigniew Bogucki, responded to Tusk’s address, calling the prime minister “a pathological liar, who is setting Poland ablaze”.

articles.title: Police clash with masked rioters after largely peaceful protests across France
articles.author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent

paras.en: Clashes erupted in Paris, Marseille and other cities on Saturday after tens of thousands of demonstrators, some in Halloween fancy dress, marched across France in a third wave of protests over the cost of living and deteriorating public services.

The interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said about 150 planned demonstrations around the country had passed off peacefully, but police had encountered an “extraordinary” level of violence from some rioters as the rallies ended.

One riot police officer had been hit by a molotov cocktail in Paris, he said, describing the incident as an “attempted murder”. “We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight,” he added.

About 320,000 people – down from an estimated 410,000 last weekend – took part in rallies around the country, the interior ministry said, including 70,000 in Paris who marched along boulevards on the south-eastern outskirts, avoiding the city centre.

As evening approached and the largely peaceful demonstrations came to an end, police in several cities fired teargas and stun grenades to disperse crowds joined – as on the previous Saturday – by groups of masked rioters.
The interior ministry said late Saturday that police had arrested 565 people across the country. Four police officers and one gendarme were injured in Paris.

Nuñez said earlier this week that 70,000 police and gendarmes, including elite units, would be deployed in an effort to quell violence on the protests’ sidelines, warning that Saturday looked like “a very high risk” day.

The Paris protesters set off peacefully from the Porte de Bagnolet near the ring road, holding placards with slogans including “No need for teargas to make our future look bleak” and “Disguised as an angry citizen for Halloween”, as a helicopter flew overhead

On and around its destination, the Porte de Charenton, dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, and at least one incendiary device was thrown at security forces.

Police responded with teargas and baton charges. “A hardcore of several hundred rioters” had attacked police with projectiles, the Paris police prefecture said. Officers had “manoeuvred to restore public order”, it added.

In Lyon protesters threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire teargas, and in Toulouse police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people, mostly young demonstrators.

The marches brought together school students, who have been calling for better conditions for a month, trade unions and gilets jaune (yellow vests) protesters united in anger at the cost of living, widening inequalities and Emmanuel Macron’s government.

“The French economy is doing badly no matter what happens, because today we’re being run by a group of incompetents who juggle billions while families are struggling with a few cents,” said one protester on the Paris march, Jérôme Rodrigues. “That’s why we’re here, to keep shouting our demands louder and louder.”
A protester in Nantes, Camille Guérin, said: “We say no to the cost of living, no to the far right, yes to high school students’ demands, yes to giving citizens a voice.”

Saturday’s rallies came two weeks after widespread street violence and looting rocked numerous French cities during a first wave of mass protest on 17 October that became one of the worst days of civil unrest in the country’s recent history.

Student protesters vowed to stage new high school and university blockades on Tuesday and Thursday. “Then we will join the 5 November demonstration called by workers and trade unions,” said Sabrine Kharbach of the Union Étudiante, a student organisation.

Protests also took place elsewhere in Europe. In Germany, police fired water cannon to disperse protesters who hurled firework and other projectiles at the end of youth-led protests organised by a group called “Gen Z regelt!” (Gen Z will sort this).

Thousands of police were deployed across the country, with tensions rising as evening fell after mostly peaceful demonstrations for “for education, health, the climate and an affordable life” in dozens of cities.

In Frankfurt, Germany’s financial hub, at least two stores were looted as protests turned violent, with several more damaged and police trying to gain control of the situation, according to a Reuters witness. A march was also temporarily halted in the city after protesters set off fireworks.
In the western city of Cologne, police fired water cannon to disperse a crowd after saying protesters had targeted officers with fireworks.
In Berlin, protesters hurled bottles and eggs while protesters set barricades ablaze in Hamburg, and police were using pepper spray on demonstrators in some places, the newspaper Bild reported.
Fresh anti-government demonstrations also occurred in Albania’s capital, with protesters renewing their demands that prime minister Edi Rama resign.

Saturday’s demonstration began peacefully under rain outside the education ministry in Tirana, before dozens of masked youths started throwing paving stones and firebombs at police and set fire to rubbish bins.
Police were also on alert in Barcelona after an anonymous TikTok network called Blocus urged new gatherings, and in Italy after recent clashes with protesters in Milan, Turin and Bologna.

articles.title: Binance says 90% of losses from $6.3bn hack covered as FBI says North Korea behind attack
articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies

paras.en: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced 90% of the amount stolen after a record $6.3bn hack of its platform by a group the FBI identified as being backed by North Korea.

The remaining 10% of tokens are less liquid, meaning they may take longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday. Co-CEO Richard Teng said separately that the company was “committed to covering the remaining 10%” and that “users will not bear the financial impact of this incident”.
Binance suspended user withdrawals after the hack, but said in its latest update that it was on track to resume them on Sunday.
The announcement came as the FBI on Saturday confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.

TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.

“The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026,” the law enforcement agency said in a statement.

The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services.
It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets”.

Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it harder to trace and investigate.
Binance said it had set aside around $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses.
“Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said.

The money spent re-buying tokens came from using part of its $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users, a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some of its Futures Insurance Fund, and the company’s own corporate treasury, it said on X.
The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.
Bitcoin plunged nearly 5% after the news of the hack, while Ethereum dropped nearly 6% and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10%.

The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programmes – to find illicit means to capture revenue.

articles.title: These firms you've never heard of are feeding fears the AI bubble could burst

paras.en: A once-obscure corner of the AI ecosystem finds itself in the spotlight â and investors don't all like what they see.
paras.zh: 人工智能生态系统中一个曾经模糊不清的角落发现自己处于聚光灯下，投资者并不都喜欢他们所看到的。

paras.en: Names like CoreWeave and Nebius are familiar to the tech set in San Francisco and Silicon Valley.
paras.zh: 像CoreWeave和Nebius这样的名字对于旧金山和硅谷的科技公司来说很熟悉。

paras.en: These data centre companies, known as neocloud firms, run large warehouses packed with expensive computers, which they lease to major AI developers like Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta.
paras.zh: 这些数据中心公司被称为新云公司，运营着装满昂贵计算机的大型仓库，并将其出租给Anthropic、OpenAI和Meta等主要人工智能开发商。

paras.en: They're now the subject of one of Silicon Valley's most heated debates.
paras.zh: 他们现在是硅谷最激烈辩论的主题之一。

paras.en: Many question whether neocloud firms are financially sound and what their recent stumbles tell us about the state of the AI economy.
paras.zh: 许多人质疑新云公司的财务状况是否稳健，以及他们最近的失误告诉我们关于人工智能经济状况的信息。

paras.en: Analysts at Gartner predict by 2030, 80% of neocloud firms will "cease independent operations", while Forrester's experts expect at least three of them to be imminently acquired "as finances get shaky".
paras.zh: Gartner的分析师预测，到2030年， 80%的新云公司将“停止独立运营” ，而Forrester的专家预计， “由于财务状况不稳定” ，至少有三家公司将立即被收购。

paras.en: On Thursday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tried to downplay recent concerns about neocloud firms, calling them "a small component of the overall ecosystem, external" on CNBC.
paras.zh: 周四，财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)试图淡化最近对新云公司的担忧，称它们是CNBC “整个生态系统的一小部分，是外部的”。

paras.en: Neocloud firms often finance themselves by signing long-term lease contracts with major tech customers who need quick access to computing power.
paras.zh: 新云公司通常通过与需要快速访问计算能力的主要技术客户签订长期租赁合同来为自己融资。

paras.en: Firms can then borrow money using those contracts â plus the AI chips they purchase â as collateral, explained analyst Cory Johnson of "The Quiet Period" IPO research outfit.
paras.zh: 然后，公司可以使用这些合同（加上他们购买的人工智能芯片）作为抵押品借款， “安静时期” IPO研究机构的分析师科里·约翰逊（ Cory Johnson ）解释说。

paras.en: He said debt is common across neocloud firms because the hardware has to be paid for up front.
Take the industry leader: CoreWeave. It's a fraction of the size of some of the Big Tech companies it serves.
But Johnson believes lenders sometimes consider the creditworthiness of CoreWeave's customers, like Microsoft or Meta, more than the company's when they lend.
"This helps explain how CoreWeave accumulated $35.1bn (Â£26.3bn) in debt," he said.
Some jittery investors appear to be having second thoughts.
CoreWeave stock has lost a quarter of its value over the past month, and it's not alone.
Shares in other neocloud firms like Nebius, IREN, and Applied Digital have all shed about that much if not more during the same period.
Debt investors also appear spooked, and are demanding ever-higher returns from several firms in the sector.

CoreWeave's CEO Mike Intrator has said that the market is acting "irrationally" and has expressed confidence in its business model. Some of the world's most consequential companies are queuing up for CoreWeave's infrastructure and other AI services.
Several neocloud firms have their roots in the volatile crypto mining industry, made of companies that generate cryptocurrencies, like Bitcoin.
Crypto miners use some of the same kind of physical infrastructure that is used to develop AI.
CoreWeave was founded in 2017 with a focus on mining Ethereum.
IREN, Core Scientific and Applied Digital also started in crypto mining.
Their infrastructure left them well-positioned when AI exploded in 2022 with the introduction of OpenAI's ChatGPT.
One outlier is Nebius, which was known as Yandex NV when it was part of Russia's version of Google before splitting off and changing its name in 2024.
Now, the success of these firms hinges on the fate of major AI developers and hyperscalers â even larger data centre operators which neocloud firms often count as key customers.
"There is just an enormous amount of spending getting injected into the system," said Melissa Otto, head of Visible Alpha Research at S&P Global. "It's an arms race."
But the trade-off of their model is "greater financial risk" in the face of change, said Forrester VP and principal analyst Charlie Dai.
That includes any adjustments that their Big Tech customers might make to their spending plans.
This past week, when Microsoft and Google forecast less AI spending than Wall Street analysts had projected, shares in several neocloud firms tumbled.
Much is also riding on Anthropic and OpenAI, which are both expected to start selling shares to the public in the months ahead.
If AI proves to be a bubble â and bursts â neocloud firms "are definitely going to face collateral damage," said Bradley Tusk of Tusk Ventures.
The future of the neoclouds also depend on their ability to keep borrowing, which gets more expensive as interest rates rise.
In a recent social media post, Elon Musk suggested this challenge could lead more than 200 neoclouds to "see guppy-level death and consolidation", with the smallest firms being the most vulnerable.
"Some will make it through, but not many," he added.
For now, analysts at Yorkville Ives said demand for computing power still exceeds supply, adding that neoclouds are filling an important gap that larger data centre companies cannot fill.
But to some, the neocloud sector's recent wobbles are concerning.
Microsoft recently cancelled a deal with a British neocloud outfit called Nscale amid power supply issues which could last through to 2030.
Australia's Firmus just shelved plans to start selling shares to the public.
These developments come amid a public backlash against data centres and questions about how much value AI can add to worker productivity.
"There's reason to worry," said Johnson.

articles.title: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent

paras.en: Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday and clashes erupted with police there and in other German cities after largely peaceful mass protests over the cost of living.
paras.zh: 周六晚些时候，暴乱分子在法兰克福市中心抢劫了商店，并在那里和其他德国城市爆发了与警察的冲突，此前人们就生活费用问题进行了大规模的和平抗议。

paras.en: Besides Frankfurt - Germany's financial hub - there were incidents of violence in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg, with police saying they used water cannon to disperse protesters who targeted emergency workers with fireworks, stones and bottles.
paras.zh: 除了德国金融中心法兰克福外，柏林、科隆和汉堡也发生了暴力事件，警方称他们使用水炮驱散抗议者，他们用烟花、石头和瓶子袭击紧急救援人员。

paras.en: Thousands earlier joined the demonstrations organised by the campaign group Gen Z regelt - meaning "Gen Z takes charge" - to protest against underfunding in schools, the high cost of living, public spending cuts and military service.
paras.zh: 数千人早些时候加入了Z世代组织regelt （意为“Z世代负责” ）组织的示威活动，以抗议学校资金不足、高昂的生活成本、公共开支削减和兵役。

paras.en: The unrest in Germany follows similar youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on Saturday.
paras.zh: 德国的骚乱发生在法国类似的青年领导的大规模抗议活动之后，周六有超过32万人参加了示威活动。

paras.en: A large section of Frankfurt's main shopping street was closed off by police, AFP news agency reported. A police spokesperson said many arrests were made in the city.
paras.zh: 据法新社报道，法兰克福主要购物街的一大部分被警方封锁。警方发言人说，该市有许多人被捕。

paras.en: Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, roughly half of what the organisers had estimated on their website. German media say tens of thousands protested in German cities on Saturday.
paras.zh: 法兰克福、慕尼黑和柏林当局报告了多达18,000名抗议者，大约是组织者在其网站上估计的一半。德国媒体称，周六有数万人在德国城市举行抗议活动。

paras.en: Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said the demonstrations were "to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion".
paras.zh: Z世代发言人莉娜·弗里德里希（ Lina Friedrich ）表示，示威活动是为了“争取和平与自由，而不是为了战争和胁迫”。

paras.en: She said: "What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favour of a fairer distribution of the burden."
paras.zh: 她说： “对我们来说，最重要的是更好地支持卫生和教育系统。我们反对义务兵役，我们赞成更公平地分配负担。”

paras.en: While protests during the day were largely peaceful, the demonstrations turned violent as night fell.
paras.zh: 虽然白天的抗议活动基本上是和平的，但随着夜幕降临，示威活动变得暴力。

paras.en: In a post on X, Frankfurt police said that "violent riots" were occurring in the city centre. The windows of several shops had been smashed and molotov cocktails were thrown at emergency services, police said.
paras.zh: 法兰克福警方在X的帖子中表示，市中心正在发生“暴力骚乱”。警方称，几家商店的窗户被砸碎，燃烧弹被扔到紧急服务部门。

paras.en: In later updates, officials said the windows of a gun shop were smashed and that they had seized two weapons after arresting a suspect.
paras.zh: 在后来的更新中，官员们说，一家枪店的窗户被砸碎了，他们在逮捕了一名嫌疑人后缴获了两件武器。

paras.en: Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, of which Frankfurt is the biggest city, said that "around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists" had infiltrated the protest in the city. He added that it was "shameful" how the protests had ended.
paras.zh: 法兰克福是最大城市的黑森州内政部长罗曼·波塞克（ Roman Poseck ）表示， “大约100名明确识别的左翼极端分子”已经渗透到该市的抗议活动中。他补充说，抗议活动的结束是“可耻的”。

paras.en: Poseck said: "We all have those images from France in our minds â looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers... France must not be held up as a model in this regard."
paras.zh: 波塞克说： “我们脑海中都有那些来自法国的形象--抢劫、焚烧房屋、焚烧警车和袭击警察……在这方面，法国绝不能成为榜样。”

articles.title: Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?

paras.en: The race for a US Senate seat in Texas may prove crucial in determining which party controls Congress next year â a significant prize in its own right - but for both parties it represents so much more than that.
paras.zh: 在德克萨斯州竞选美国参议院席位可能对于确定哪个政党明年控制国会至关重要-这本身就是一个重要奖项-但对双方来说，它所代表的意义远不止于此。

paras.en: For the Democrats, their losing streak in statewide elections now stretches back more than three decades. In the second most populous state in America, liberals have been in the wilderness for a generation.
paras.zh: 对于民主党人来说，他们在全州选举中的连败现在可以追溯到三十多年前。在美国人口第二多的州，自由主义者已经在荒野中生活了一代人。

paras.en: But polls suggest their candidate, 37-year-old James Talarico, may be on the verge of breaking through and turning a Texas Senate seat blue for the first time since 1988.
paras.zh: 但民意调查显示，他们的候选人， 37岁的詹姆斯·塔拉里科（ James Talarico ）可能即将突破并自1988年以来首次将德克萨斯州参议院席位变成蓝色。

paras.en: That would be a dream scenario for Democrats - and a potential nightmare for Republicans.
paras.zh: 这将是民主党人的梦想，也是共和党人的潜在噩梦。

paras.en: "If the Democrats do pull it off, I think it's going to cause a lot of soul searching and a lot of psychological damage to the Republican Party in Texas and nationwide," said Brendan Steinhauser, a Texas-based Republican campaign strategist.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯州共和党竞选策略师布伦丹·斯坦豪泽（ Brendan Steinhauser ）表示： “如果民主党真的成功了，我认为这将给德克萨斯州和全国各地的共和党人带来很多灵魂探索和心理伤害。”

paras.en: These dramatic stakes help explain how this Senate race has rocketed to become the most expensive in US history, with total spending reaching more than half a billion dollars.
paras.zh: 这些戏剧性的赌注有助于解释这场参议院竞选如何成为美国历史上最昂贵的竞选，总支出超过5亿美元。

paras.en: For Talarico, it has been a remarkable rise for a candidate who in 2025 was a relatively unknown state-level Democrat.
paras.zh: 对于Talarico来说，对于2025年相对不知名的州级民主党候选人来说，这是一个显着的增长。

paras.en: At the Fiesta Center in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday night, the line to see the softly spoken former teacher, who studied to be a Christian minister before entering politics, stretched around the building and down the wide parking lot to a busy road.
paras.zh: 周二晚上，在德克萨斯州拉伯克的嘉年华中心，看到这位轻声细语的前教师在进入政界之前学习成为基督教牧师的队伍在建筑物周围延伸，沿着宽阔的停车场一直延伸到繁忙的道路上。

paras.en: In this dusty western plains town of about 250,000, which voted overwhelmingly for President Donald Trump two years ago, a visit from a major Democratic candidate on the eve of an election was unusual.
paras.zh: 在这个拥有约25万人口的尘土飞扬的西部平原小镇上，两年前唐纳德·特朗普（ Donald Trump ）以压倒性优势投票支持总统，在大选前夕，一位主要的民主党候选人的访问是不寻常的。

paras.en: "It's just so amazing to watch," said Aaron Gonzalez, the Democratic Party chair for Hockley County, which borders Lubbock. "This time is different."
paras.zh: “观看真是太神奇了，”与拉伯克接壤的霍克利县的民主党主席亚伦·冈萨雷斯说。“这次不一样。”

paras.en: When Talarico took the stage before an estimated 3,000 supporters â with another thousand listening on speakers outside - his pitch was a familiar one for many national Democrats this year, albeit with a Texas twist.
paras.zh: 当塔拉里科在大约3000名支持者面前上台时（另有1000名支持者在外面听演讲） ，他的演讲是今年许多全国民主党人熟悉的，尽管在德克萨斯州有所改变。

paras.en: He railed against a conservative political establishment that he said is insensitive to the economic hardship of average Americans. He condemned the corrosive influence of big money in politics. And he promised to advance a "comprehensive anti-corruption agenda" in the Senate.
paras.zh: 他抨击了一个保守的政治机构，他说这个机构对普通美国人的经济困难不敏感。他谴责大钱在政治上的腐蚀性影响。他承诺在参议院推进“全面的反腐败议程”。

paras.en: "Texans are ready for change," he said. "We are done with the extremism and the corruption. We're done with the politics of division, and we are ready for something new."
paras.zh: “德克萨斯人已经准备好改变，”他说。“我们已经结束了极端主义和腐败。我们已经完成了分裂的政治，我们已经准备好迎接新的事物。”

paras.en: The slogan for his final two weeks of campaigning â "clear eyes, full hearts, can't lose" â is taken from Friday Night Lights, a popular early 2000s TV show about a plucky small-town Texas high school football team.
paras.zh: 他最后两周竞选活动的口号- “清晰的眼睛，充实的心灵，不能失去” -取自周五夜灯节目，这是一部流行的21世纪初电视节目，讲述了德克萨斯州一个勇敢的小镇高中橄榄球队。

paras.en: His music playlist leans heavily on twangy Texas country music. He celebrates Texas breakfast tacos, quotes legendary Texas singer-songwriter Lyle Lovett and frequently mentions that his ties to the state go back eight generations.
paras.zh: 他的音乐播放列表在很大程度上依赖于得克萨斯州乡村音乐。他庆祝德克萨斯州的早餐玉米饼，引用德克萨斯州传奇创作歌手莱尔·洛维特（ Lyle Lovett ）的话，并经常提到他与该州的关系可以追溯到八代人。

paras.en: In the Lubbock audience, Andrew Robinson, a student from nearby Texas Tech University, liked what he heard. But the 26-year-old's optimism was tempered by an entire lifetime spent watching Democrats try, and fail, to get a toehold in the state.
paras.zh: 在拉伯克听众中，来自附近德克萨斯理工大学的学生安德鲁·罗宾逊（ Andrew Robinson ）喜欢他听到的内容。但这位26岁的年轻人的乐观情绪被一辈子看着民主党人试图在该州获得一席之地而失败所缓和。

paras.en: "A Talarico win would mean so much," he said. "I haven't been keen on wanting to stay in Texas. And if the government were to change, it could give me a reason."
paras.zh: “塔拉里科的胜利意义重大，”他说。“我一直不想留在德克萨斯州。如果政府要改变，它可以给我一个理由。”

paras.en: For Republicans, a Democratic win in Texas would have a very different meaning.
paras.zh: 对于共和党人来说，民主党在德克萨斯州的胜利将具有非常不同的含义。

paras.en: At roughly the same time Talarico was addressing his supporters in the Fiesta Center, Trump â alongside the Republican Party's Senate candidate Ken Paxton â was just a few miles away, in a venue twice the size.
paras.zh: 大约在塔拉里科在嘉年华中心向他的支持者发表讲话的同时，特朗普与共和党参议员候选人肯·帕克斯顿（ Ken Paxton ）就在几英里之外，场地面积是原来的两倍。

paras.en: "If you go out and vote, we're going to have a tremendous win in Texas," the president told the crowd.
paras.zh: “如果你出去投票，我们将在德克萨斯州取得巨大的胜利，”总统告诉人群。

paras.en: Trump's visit to reliably-Republican Lubbock suggests the party is concerned about turnout even in the most conservative portions of the state. It is a worry that has been echoed by other Texas Republicans.
paras.zh: 特朗普对可靠的共和党人拉伯克的访问表明，即使在该州最保守的地区，该党也担心投票率。这是德克萨斯州其他共和党人的担忧。

paras.en: "Understand, we could lose Texas," Texas Senator Ted Cruz said in his podcast on Friday. "The Democrats are massively out-turning-out the Republicans."
paras.zh: “理解，我们可能会失去德克萨斯州，”德克萨斯州参议员特德克鲁兹周五在他的播客中说。“民主党人正在大规模地击败共和党人。”

paras.en: Don Huffines, who is running for election as the state's chief financial officer, issued an even more dire warning. "Texas is the foundation of the Republican Party in America," he posted on X.
paras.zh: 正在竞选该州首席财务官的Don Huffines发出了更为严峻的警告。“德克萨斯州是美国共和党的基础，”他在X上发帖说。

paras.en: "When the foundation breaks, it all falls apart. When we lose Texas, we lose the USA."
paras.zh: “当基础破裂时，一切都会分崩离析。当我们失去德克萨斯州时，我们就失去了美国。”

paras.en: For weeks now, party leaders have been warning that a liberal breakthrough in the Lone Star State could have dire consequences.
paras.zh: 几周来，党的领导人一直警告说，孤星州的自由主义突破可能会产生可怕的后果。

paras.en: They fear a Talarico win would motivate more local Democrats to run for statewide and federal offices. Better quality candidates with more funding could lead to a snowball effect similar to the Democratic inroads seen in other southern states, such as Georgia, North Carolina and Virginia.
paras.zh: 他们担心Talarico的胜利会激励更多的地方民主党人竞选全州和联邦办公室。有了更多的资金，更高质量的候选人可能会产生类似于乔治亚州、北卡罗来纳州和弗吉尼亚州等其他南部州的民主党入侵的雪球效应。

paras.en: "I think that it's pretty clear that Republicans, especially candidates, consultants, operatives, and others who are active in the party, see that this is a real threat," said Steinhauser.
paras.zh: Steinhauser说： “我认为很明显，共和党人，特别是候选人、顾问、特工和其他活跃在党内的人，都认为这是一个真正的威胁。”

paras.en: "The days of waving this off and saying that Texas would never turn blue are over."
paras.zh: “挥舞着这句话，说德克萨斯永远不会变成蓝色的日子已经结束了。”

paras.en: For the Texas Senate race to come to the point where recent polls suggest Talarico has a slim but stable lead has required a unique confluence of events and political dynamics â a "perfect storm", in the words of Steinhauser.
paras.zh: 为了使德克萨斯州参议院的竞选达到最近的民意调查显示Talarico有一个微弱但稳定的领先优势，需要事件和政治动态的独特融合-用Steinhauser的话说是“完美风暴”。

paras.en: "Everything that could go well for the Democrats is going well," he said, "and everything that could go badly for the Republicans is going badly."
paras.zh: “对民主党人来说，一切可能顺利的事情都很顺利，”他说， “而对共和党人来说，一切可能不顺利的事情都很糟糕。

paras.en: But it is also a whirlwind that, in a significant part, has been sown over the past year by Trump himself.
paras.zh: 但这也是一场旋风，在很大程度上是由特朗普本人在过去一年中播下的。

paras.en: The national environment for Republicans is a harsh one.
paras.zh: 对于共和党人来说，国家环境是严峻的。

paras.en: Voters are frustrated with high consumer costs, including the price of petrol, and largely blame Trump's tariff policies and the Iran war.
paras.zh: 选民对包括汽油价格在内的高消费成本感到沮丧，并在很大程度上归咎于特朗普的关税政策和伊朗战争。

paras.en: Political corruption has become an issue of growing concern. Democrats, independents and many Republicans in a recent Cook political report poll identified "greedy billionaires and corporations" and politicians seeking "personal gain" as the ones to blame.
paras.zh: 政治腐败已成为一个日益令人担忧的问题。在最近的库克政治报告中，民主党人、独立人士和许多共和党人将“贪婪的亿万富翁和企业”以及寻求“个人利益”的政客列为罪魁祸首。

paras.en: Texas-specific issues have also contributed to a hostile climate for the in-power party.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯州的具体问题也助长了执政党的敌对气氛。

paras.en: Polling and recent special elections in Texas indicate that Hispanic voters â many of whom switched to Trump to help him win the White House in 2024 â have soured on the administration's immigration enforcement policies.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯州的民意调查和最近的特别选举表明，西班牙裔选民-其中许多人转向特朗普，以帮助他在2024年赢得白宫-对政府的移民执法政策感到不满。

paras.en: Hispanics make up nearly a third of the state's population - and in more than a week of early voting in Texas, they have been casting ballots in historically large numbers.
paras.zh: 西班牙裔占该州人口的近三分之一，在德克萨斯州提前投票一周多的时间里，他们一直在进行历史性的大量投票。

paras.en: Data centre construction, which Texas Republicans had touted as a welcome investment in the state, has drawn widespread criticism, particularly in rural areas that have traditionally been solidly conservative.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯州共和党人吹捧的数据中心建设是该州的一项受欢迎的投资，这引起了广泛的批评，特别是在传统上一直坚定保守的农村地区。

paras.en: Texas Governor Greg Abbott, in his own tight re-election race, recently announced a one-year moratorium on AI construction in the state â a reflection of how quickly the issue has become a political liability.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯州州长格雷格·阿博特（ Greg Abbott ）在自己的紧锣密鼓的连任竞选中，最近宣布在该州暂停一年的人工智能建设-这反映了这个问题迅速成为政治负担。

paras.en: "It's bad for Republicans," one Texas political strategist, who asked to remain anonymous, told the BBC. "We're asking a whole lot of the electorate at this point for us to continue to be the guys in charge."
paras.zh: “这对共和党人不利，”一位要求匿名的德克萨斯州政治战略家告诉英国广播公司。“我们现在要求很多选民让我们继续担任负责人。”

paras.en: Then there's the baggage that Paxton, who defeated longtime incumbent Senator John Cornyn in a contentious primary campaign earlier this year, brings to the race.
paras.zh: 帕克斯顿在今年早些时候的一次有争议的初选中击败了长期任职的参议员约翰·科宁（ John Cornyn ） ，给比赛带来了负担。

paras.en: The 63-year-old Republican successfully painted the 74-year-old Cornyn as too old and too out-of-touch with Texas conservatives. He received a late boost, just days before his run-off election victory over Cornyn, in the form of a Trump endorsement.
paras.zh: 这位63岁的共和党人成功地将这位74岁的科宁描绘得太老，太与德克萨斯州的保守派脱节。就在他第二轮选举战胜科宁的前几天，他以特朗普代言的形式获得了提振。

paras.en: "Ken Paxton has gone through a lot, in many cases, very unfairly, but he is a Fighter, and knows how to WIN," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Our Country needs Fighters, and also Loyalty to the Cause of Greatness."
paras.zh: “肯·帕克斯顿（ Ken Paxton ）经历了很多，在许多情况下，非常不公平，但他是一名斗士，知道如何获胜，”特朗普在Truth Social上写道。“我们的国家需要战士，也需要对伟大事业的忠诚。”

paras.en: The "a lot" the president referenced Paxton going through includes a 2015 federal indictment on charges of securities fraud â later dropped â and a 2023 impeachment by the Republican-controlled Texas House of Representatives on corruption, bribery and abuse of power charges.
paras.zh: 总统提到的帕克斯顿正在经历的“很多”包括2015年关于证券欺诈指控的联邦起诉书-后来被撤销-以及共和党控制的德克萨斯州众议院对腐败，贿赂和滥用权力指控的2023年弹劾。

paras.en: The Texas Senate would later acquit Paxton after Trump intervened to pressure state Republican leaders.
paras.zh: 在特朗普干预向州共和党领导人施压后，德克萨斯州参议院后来宣告帕克斯顿无罪。

paras.en: All of this has meant that Paxton has more than a few critics â and enemies - in Texas, including within his own party.
paras.zh: 所有这些都意味着帕克斯顿在德克萨斯州，包括在他自己的政党内，有不止一些批评者和敌人。

paras.en: Talarico, by contrast, has proven to be an effective candidate. The state legislator defeated a well-known opponent, Dallas Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett, in the Democratic primary.
paras.zh: 相比之下， Talarico已被证明是一个有效的候选人。州议员在民主党初选中击败了众所周知的对手达拉斯女议员贾斯敏·克罗克特（ Jasmine Crockett ）。

paras.en: Since earning the nomination, he has maintained his polling lead despite a withering onslaught of negative advertising - much of it funded by the world's richest man Elon Musk, whose SpaceX company is based in Texas.
paras.zh: 尽管负面广告肆虐，但自获得提名以来，他一直保持着民意调查的领先优势--其中大部分资金来自全球首富埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk) ，他的SpaceX公司总部位于德克萨斯州。

paras.en: Musk alone has funnelled more than $170m into the race. Trump's MAGA Inc. committee has chipped in $40m.
paras.zh: 仅马斯克就为比赛投入了超过1.7亿美元$。特朗普的MAGA Inc.委员会已经筹集了4000万美元$。

paras.en: While Paxton has proven to be an ineffective fundraiser, the third-party money spent on his behalf has blanketed the airwaves in the state â spilling over into sporting events involving Texas teams that air across the nation.
paras.zh: 虽然Paxton已被证明是一个无效的筹款活动，但代表他花费的第三方资金已经覆盖了该州的电波-蔓延到涉及德克萨斯州球队在全国范围内播出的体育赛事。

paras.en: They have targeted Talarico for his past comments supporting transgender people, for calling "radicalised white men" a domestic terrorism threat and for criticising the fossil fuel and beef industries â two powerful interests in the state.
paras.zh: 他们将Talarico作为目标，因为他过去的评论支持变性人，将“激进的白人”称为国内恐怖主义威胁，并批评化石燃料和牛肉产业-这是该州的两个强大利益。

paras.en: Talarico has distanced himself from some of those earlier comments, arguing many were taken out of context and "missed the mark" or were "deliberately provocative" or "cringy".
paras.zh: Talarico与早些时候的一些言论保持距离，认为许多言论被断章取义， “失误”或“故意挑衅”或“畏缩”。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the Texas Democrat has proven to be a historically successful fundraiser, amassing more than $140m in donations over the course of his campaign and setting a three-month fundraising record for a Senate candidate.
paras.zh: 与此同时，这位德克萨斯州民主党人已被证明是一位历史上成功的筹款人，他在竞选期间积累了超过1.4亿美元的捐款，并为参议院候选人创下了三个月的筹款记录。

paras.en: The funding has allowed Talarico to hit back at Paxton, highlighting his past controversies, and defending himself from Republican attacks.
paras.zh: 这笔资金使塔拉里科能够反击帕克斯顿，突出了他过去的争议，并保护自己免受共和党的攻击。

paras.en: He frequently leans into his religious upbringing â as the grandson of a Southern Baptist preacher who spent time in a seminary â leavening his stump speeches with biblical references.

And last-minute Republican appeals, as well as Trump's repeated campaign visits, could spur conservatives to turn out in greater numbers on election day, erasing any Democratic early voting advantages.

paras.en: Inside the tiny Democratic Party office at a Talarico rally in Amarillo on Tuesday, retired schoolteacher Terri Mills listened to the candidate's stump speech.

paras.en: Despite acknowledging the decades of Democratic futility and false dawns, she said she was allowing herself to hope for a Democratic victory once again.

Carlisle Brake & Friction has broken ground to expand its Chennai, India manufacturing operations in one of the world’s fastest-growing industrial regions. Having produced mechatronic products in the region for more than 15 years, Carlisle CBF will relocate to add production at a larger site for off-highway paper wet friction discs and steel separator plates. The new facility is scheduled to open in 2027.

The move to expanded space is designed to accommodate manufacturing capabilities needed to serve the growing demand across the agriculture, construction and especially mining industries in India and Southeast Asia. Carlisle Brake & Friction is establishing a state-of-the-art wet friction manufacturing facility on par with proven global manufacturing processes in the new Chennai plant, to build a more resilient regional platform. articles.title: One Game at a Time: Lessons from the Sports World for Auto Body Shops
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: You hear it all the time in sports: we’re taking it one game at a time. This week, we’re 1-0, and next week starts a new week, and we’re hoping to go 1-0 again.

Why are coaches and athletes so hyper-focused on the game at hand, not worrying about the last game or any future game? “Our focus is on [their next opponent’s team name].” If they lost the last game badly, not worrying about it but washing it away and wiping the slate clean. If they won the last game by a wide margin, not getting too proud of themselves lest they feel they’re invincible and give less effort the next game.

Sounds a little to me like “staying in the present” or staying in the moment. Which I think is a little different in that it relates to the philosophy of living. For example, I heard someone say a good way to slow down time is to stay in the present — something altogether different than what I was talking about with sports.

But I think this “one game a time” attitude in sports has some business lessons. Have a bad quarter profit-wise? Let’s kill it the next quarter. Last week’s vehicles have been delivered, and there were some hiccups. What can we do this week to avoid those same bumps in the road? Let’s not fixate on why Ms. McGillicuddy was fuming about her car last week but learn from our mistakes so we don’t make another customer mad. Not get too high over our successes or too low over our failures but plod ahead with the same workman-like attitude to do the best job we can. One vehicle at a time, one customer at a time, the highest quality job we can do each time.

articles.title: How Cam Designs Are Meeting More Specialized Demands
articles.author: Greg Jones

paras.en: Picking a camshaft used to involve a simple flip through a catalog to find a grind that matched your basic engine specs. Today, off-the-shelf cams still make sense for many applications, but more specialized engine combinations are pushing builders toward more custom solutions. Experts attribute this shift to a handful of factors.

Nick Norris of Callies says the move away from “one-size-fits-most” cams is largely due to combinations becoming too specialized. The same basic engine, he notes, can be naturally aspirated, turbocharged, positive-displacement supercharged, or run with nitrous, and each can require a very different approach to valve timing.

“Better EFI, data acquisition and simulation have also changed what we can evaluate,” Norris says. “We can look at boost, backpressure, converter behavior, engine acceleration, and other data and design around what the vehicle actually needs. Instead of asking only what cam will make the most power, we can ask where we need the torque and how we want that power delivered.”

All of this has changed how Norris and other top manufacturers look at valvetrain development. While cam specs and events have traditionally been referenced to what’s happening at the lobe, “for the past couple of years I’ve been retraining myself to think more about the events at the valve,” he says. “After all, that’s what the engine sees.”

That shift – from designing around the camshaft itself to designing around what the valve actually does – is a big part of where cam development is headed. It also helps explain why manufacturers are moving beyond basic specs like lobe separation angle (LSA) and taking a more complete, system-level approach to the valvetrain.

Why exactly is the market evolving this way? One important driver, according to Bobby Biancaniello of Cam Motion, is “the ability to have a camshaft spec’d for your exact build and ground and shipped to you in one week’s time.”

While Cam Motion’s off-the-shelf grinds will work for almost any late-model application, he notes, when you start changing things like runner lengths on intakes, incorporating power adders, or adding displacement by lengthening the stroke, “it’s easier to make them exactly what they need with a custom grind than having a catalog with thousands of options” that can just end up complicating the selection process.

Another reason for this changing dynamic is the role of modern technology and tuning. Nic Woods of Clay Smith Cams explains that until about 10-15 years ago, EFI was a major headache for cam manufacturers, and “there were only a few guys in the country who really knew how to dial in performance cams and get them tuned and mapped correctly for the air-fuel ratio at idle.”
But now, with the rapid evolution of ECU technology and how well these systems communicate with the O2 sensors, today’s self-learning systems can better accommodate more aggressive performance cams.

“We don’t really have to recommend cams differently for fuel-injected platforms anymore,” Woods says. “We can give them the right cam, and if the guy doesn’t know how to tune it, the fuel injection can self-learn and map the fuel correctly.”

Charlie Westcott of Militia Racing Products points to manufacturing technology and material advances as additional factors influencing the market. He says many traditional cam cores are designed to cover a wide range of applications, which can create challenges when they’re machined and heat-treated.

By comparison, tool-steel cores (like S7) are high-strength throughout and can be manufactured more efficiently without some of the heat-treating and coating steps that materials like 8620 or 9310 would require.

“I can make a camshaft – from a phone call to the finished product – in about three days,” Westcott says. “Those three days are only because I’m waiting for the heat treat to come back. Whereas if you’re doing these other cams, you have to send them out to get copper-coated, then send them out again for heat treatment after you mill them. It’s a big time suck. I prefer getting things done quickly for people.”

Of course, to get a custom camshaft recommendation, certain information must be collected. Norris says the engine’s cubic inches, rpm range, cylinder heads, and application will get the Callies team in the ballpark. But choosing the actual profiles requires more detail.

“We’ll look at the weights of the valvetrain components and the overall stiffness of the system based on things like pushrod dimensions, rocker ratios and material, and the rest of the valvetrain configuration,” Norris says.
The spring package is another big consideration. If a customer has one they’re happy with, Norris and his team will go over the specs to make sure it’s compatible with the profiles they’ve chosen.

“If we’re starting from scratch, the spring and lobe need to be considered together rather than treating the spring as something that gets selected after the cam,” he notes. “Ultimately, the basic engine information helps determine the valve events and general cam specifications, while the details of the valvetrain help determine how aggressive the lobe profiles can be and still maintain control through the intended rpm range.”

Biancaniello agrees that when deciding on the best camshaft for a particular application, “it’s important for the cam guy to know as much as possible about the setup.” That means customers need to be as clear and up front as possible about their goals and how they plan to use the vehicle. Why? Because two builds that look virtually the same can require two very different cams.

As an example, he points to a turbocharged LS 5.3L with a set of 62mm turbos. In one case, the engine is being used in a streetcar with a tight converter, air conditioning, power brakes, and no transbrake. This customer wants very quick spool-up, a broad powerband, a 6,500-rpm ceiling, and 700-plus horsepower.

“That setup will have much different specs than the identical engine/turbos going into a drag race-only application with a transbrake and a converter that flashes 6,200-plus rpm and gets run to 8,000 rpm max on much higher boost levels with a goal of 1,200-plus hp,” he says.
Norris offers a similar assessment, making note of pressure conditions and the fact that the same boost level with two different turbo systems can produce very different exhaust backpressure.

“That affects how I approach exhaust timing and overlap,” Norris explains. “The engine specifications may look nearly identical on paper, but what the vehicle needs from the engine can lead to two very different camshafts.”

Woods, too, leaves no stone unturned when gathering information, wanting to know the compression, what cylinder head is being used, the flow numbers, the type of intake manifold, components in the bottom end, and more.

“We need to have some idea of whose brand piston is in there so we can get a good estimate of how much valve clearance we have and how much camshaft we can actually put in before he has a problem,” Woods says.

Once the specs are covered, it’s time to discuss the vehicle and its intended use, which gives manufacturers an idea of rpm range and where a customer wants power and torque to occur. “Some of these conversations can take five minutes; some can take two hours,” Woods admits. “At the end of the day, the cam is the same price, but a company has to be willing to put in that extra time to make sure the customer gets the exact right cam for his application.”

Westcott, whose customers include Pro Line Racing and Noonan Race Engineering, among others, sees plenty of unorthodox projects as well. His work has covered everything from a one-of-a-kind 1969 455-style Pontiac engine with a single overhead cam to a four-valve-per-cylinder, small block Oldsmobile W-30 (one of only two ever made) to an inline six-cylinder Holden race engine from Australia and a set of John Deere tractor pulling cams. At this point, it’s safe to say almost nothing is out of bounds.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Even so, Westcott still gets calls where he has to steer people away from potential trouble. One of the most common mistakes he encounters is customers focusing too heavily on aggressive lobe profiles to try to maximize area under the curve.

“I always say, you can’t make an engine good with the camshaft,” he states. “The camshaft, in my mind, is like the conductor of the orchestra. You’ve got your cylinder heads and your manifold, and your induction system is probably the most important thing. It really sets the rpm band for the engine. The camshaft has to match that stuff, so the camshaft comes last in the party.”

In other words, a cam can’t compensate for an engine combo that won’t support the desired rpm or power level. “You can’t take a stock small-block Chevy 350 and change the cam and think you’re going to make power at 10,000 rpm,” he adds. “That’s just not going to do it.”
Instead, he says, builders should focus on getting the entire combination right rather than trying to make up for shortcomings with an overly aggressive camshaft.

“I have to talk guys out of trying to make aggressive lobes because they think they need to square up the lobes to make the engine good,” Westcott says. “I tell them, you need to fix your heads and make the cam smooth. That way you’re not beating up parts.”

An overly aggressive cam can create unnecessary stress throughout the valvetrain. “If you have to get so aggressive that you’re beating up stuff, that’s never good,” he says. “If you’ve got a jackhammer for an engine, you want the engine to be nice and smooth and not have any problems. Work on the induction system.”

Another common mistake is simply going too large on duration. “You’re better off being 5 degrees short than 5 degrees big,” he says. “Everybody wants to have the cam be too big, but they’ll typically run better if they’re smaller than if they’re bigger.”

For Biancaniello, the biggest sticking point is unquestionably LSA. He says engine builders will often request a cam with a specific LSA and little else, expecting him to fill in the blanks. He has to remind them that LSA is only one part of the equation.

“Duration and centerlines are equally important pieces to that puzzle,” he says. “We need to choose the correct valve timing the setup wants,” adding that he encourages builders to reference Cam Motion’s cam timing calculator to better understand how changes in cam specs affect the engine’s behavior.

“I can make a camshaft ‘work’ with the LSA you might think is ideal for the setup,” Biancaniello says, “but the more ideal approach would have been picking the best open and close timing and letting the duration/LSA and centerlines fall wherever they fall to make those events timed where you want them.”

Norris tabs a common mistake as choosing a cam primarily from duration at .050” lift. While he notes that’s an important number, “it doesn’t tell you where the valve events occur or how the valve gets from the seat to peak lift and back.”

He also warns against concentrating too much on duration and lobe separation and overlooking the individual valve events. Intake closing, exhaust opening and the amount and location of overlap can have a major effect on where the engine makes torque and how it responds.

“The valvetrain also has to be considered,” Norris adds. “A lobe may look ideal from an airflow standpoint but be too aggressive for the lifter, rocker, valve, and spring combination. Making the cam more aggressive doesn’t help if the valvetrain becomes unstable before the engine reaches its intended rpm.”

As racing classes and enthusiast segments continue to become more specialized, application-specific camshaft development will undoubtedly progress in kind. Biancaniello expects the industry to head “down a further rabbit hole of constant testing, R&D and real-world data” to keep pace with the seemingly endless introduction of new segments and rulebooks on the competition side.

Norris sees the next step as combining traditional cam design with more detailed analysis of the complete valvetrain. Duration, lift and valve events will always be important, he says, “but we’re increasingly able to evaluate velocity, acceleration, jerk, radius of curvature and frequency content along with actual valve motion from Spintron testing.”

The long-term goal, then, is to put that data to work earlier in the cycle. “The ability to predict if and when the valvetrain will become unstable in software, verify it through Spintron testing and ultimately validate it on the dyno would take the development process to the next level,” Norris states.

Woods raises an interesting point about the future, and something he would like to see become more commonplace in the market: moving toward validated systems to prevent premature failures, especially in high-end builds.

“You get into those specialty racing applications and you test your lobe designs on a Spintron,” he says. “You have this rocker arm, this spring, this retainer, this pushrod, and this head, and then you sell the cam by itself – how does that make sense? It’s almost like you can only buy this cam with what we tested it with.

“That’s something I think the industry is really lacking: telling the customer that these lobes are specific for drag-racing applications, and you have to have this rocker, this spring, this retainer, and this diameter pushrod with this wall thickness. Otherwise, the results may vary. When it gets to those levels of application, you have to have the system. If one piece of that system isn’t in place, the likelihood of premature failure is evident. It’s impossible for it not to be.”

The bottom line is that off-the-shelf camshafts certainly have their place, but the direction of the industry is clear. As engine combinations get more specialized and manufacturers zero in on what’s happening at the valve, the cam is becoming less of an isolated component and increasingly one piece in a complete valvetrain system.

articles.title: How OE Tire Fitments Influence Replacement Tire Sales
articles.author: Denise Koeth

paras.en: An original equipment (OE) tire fitment can influence a customer’s next tire purchase years after a vehicle leaves the factory. Aaron Neumann, head of the Nexen Tire America Technical Center, estimates that around 30% of drivers request the same tire or brand when shopping for replacements. Among luxury vehicle owners, he says more than half choose the same brand.

For tire dealers, that familiarity creates an opportunity to turn OE tire fitments into replacement sales. But making the right recommendation requires understanding why automakers select particular tires, which customers want to preserve their vehicle’s original performance and when another tire might better meet their needs.
Neumann explains how OE partnerships influence consumer purchasing decisions and what dealers should consider when recommending replacement tires.

An OE tire can begin taking shape two to three years before its intended vehicle even reaches the market. Tiremakers earn an OE fitment on a vehicle through a multi-year, collaborative engineering and testing process with the auto manufacturer long before the vehicle goes into production.

“There is a high bar to earning OE fitment,” says Aaron Neumann, head of Nexen Tire America Technical Center. “Technically, a tire manufacturer has to prove they have a highly controlled production process with robust quality systems that pass very stringent audits. They also must have the technical capability to meet performance targets at the leading edge of tire technology, which is generally only within reach for Tier 1 and 2 manufacturers. Commercially, they need to show a top-level financial rating and logistically, need to show a 100% on-time global supply chain.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Neumann says many Hyundai, Kia, Ram and Jeep vehicles in the United States feature Nexen tires.

“Two fitments we’re particularly excited about right now are the Jeep Wrangler and the new Jeep Recon,” he says. “We are also very proud of our Porsche Panamera and Cayenne fitments. Those programs are good examples of the range of capabilities required in OE development. The performance targets for a Porsche are different from those of a Jeep, but in both cases the tire has to be engineered as part of the vehicle rather than treated as an off-the-shelf component.”
For a tire manufacturer, the rigorous process is worth it for both the added business and increased brand awareness.
While Nexen does see an increase in replacement sales for sizes with OE fitments, quantifying brand awareness is a little more difficult, according to Neumann.

“There are so many new brands in the market, and customers only need to think about tires once every few years, but OE creates familiarity over the entire ownership period,” he says. “Someone may see Nexen on their own vehicle, on a neighbor’s SUV or a spare OE Nexen Roadian HTX2 on the back of a Jeep Wrangler during their morning commute every day. They may not consciously think about it at the time, but that exposure helps make the brand familiar. That recognition matters when it becomes time to replace tires.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: That tendency to stick with an OE tire varies by vehicle segment and by what customers expect from their replacement tires.

“Understandably, luxury or performance owners are more sensitive to maintaining the way the vehicle was engineered to drive, so they place more value on staying with the OE brand or specification,” he says. “At the other end of the market, a value-oriented consumer may be more willing to compare brands based on price, mileage or another practical need.”
How OE Tire Fitments Influence Replacement Sales

When recommending replacement tires, ask customers what performance characteristics they want from their vehicles. Ask whether customers liked their OE tires and what driving conditions they regularly face. Then determine whether the OE fitment or another product is the best choice.

For luxury and performance vehicle owners, Neumann suggests considering which characteristics the driver wants to preserve, including steering response, ride quality, noise levels, braking and handling.

“Enthusiasts can be similar, although they may also be more willing to move away from the exact OE tire if they are deliberately trying to change a particular performance characteristic,” he adds. “That’s where understanding the customer’s priorities becomes important.

“Generally, OE specification carries more weight as vehicles become more specialized and customers become more sensitive to how the vehicle performs. That can include luxury cars, sports cars, performance SUVs and increasingly EVs, where factors such as rolling resistance, noise, vehicle weight and range can all make tire selection more noticeable.”

However, Neumann explains that in these instances, OE is not automatically the best replacement choice simply because of the vehicle type or price point. “The better question is whether the customer wants to preserve the original balance of performance or change it,” he notes.
From a customer’s point of view, it depends less on the vehicle and more on what they need from their tires.

“If they are happy with the OE tire’s performance, then replace them like for like,” Neumann says. “If they live in snow country, then they should upgrade to a tire marked with a three-peak mountain snowflake symbol. Now, if they do a lot of miles and would like better treadwear, then look for tires with longer treadwear warranties. If they have a truck and want to upgrade the appearance, look for a more aggressive A/T or R/T tire.”

He explains that when the switch is made from OE tires to a different product, there will be a trade-off, “perhaps 2 mpg of fuel economy or a little bit more tire noise,” but that many people think these trade-offs are worth making.
“I’m an advocate for teaching consumers about tire performance and trade-offs so they can make educated decisions when buying tires,” Neumann says.

articles.title: Clarios Announces Plans to Acquire Ecobat
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: Clarios announced plans to acquire Ecobat, including the company’s three U.S. critical mineral recovery and processing facilities. Clarios manufactures low-voltage automotive batteries and advanced energy storage solutions. The proposed acquisition would preserve and strengthen domestic critical mineral processing and recovery capacity amid growing demand and supply chain concerns. By integrating these facilities into its circular supply network, Clarios aims to recover, process and return valuable materials to U.S. manufacturers.

paras.en: Clarios Acquisition Includes Three U.S. Facilities

The proposed acquisition includes three critical mineral recovery facilities in City of Industry, California; Indianapolis; and Middletown, New York. The transaction also includes Ecobat’s Dallas office. Together, these facilities currently process more than 40 million batteries annually, recovering lead, tin, antimony and other materials.
The companies expect to close the transaction by early 2027, pending customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.

“As a world leader in critical minerals processing and recovery, Clarios is uniquely positioned to strengthen this highly capable U.S. recycling operation supported by an experienced workforce,” said Clarios CEO Mark Wallace. “We see a significant opportunity to build on Ecobat’s foundation by evaluating opportunities for future investment in these operations and supporting the continued success of the business. Together, these facilities will strengthen domestic critical mineral recycling capacity, enhance supply chain security, and support the U.S. manufacturing base for years to come.”

Clarios operates closed-loop battery processing and recovery systems. The company collects used batteries, recovers critical materials and manufactures new batteries using recycled content. The proposed acquisition would strengthen Clarios’ closed-loop model, expand access to critical materials and improve domestic battery supply chain resilience.

The transaction also represents an investment in the U.S. industrial base and workforce while supporting domestic supply chain independence. Recycled lead batteries represent the country’s largest domestic source of recovered critical minerals. These include antimony, lead and tin, which support defense and advanced technology applications.
Investment Supports U.S. Manufacturing Strategy

The investment advances Clarios’ broader $6 billion U.S. Energy Manufacturing Strategy. That strategy includes a $1.9 billion commitment to strengthen domestic critical mineral recycling and processing capabilities.

The proposed acquisition would preserve existing recycling infrastructure while creating opportunities for future expansion. Clarios will continue evaluating opportunities to expand its capabilities across the United States.
Ecobat Completes Portfolio Transformation

The sale marks the final step in a portfolio transformation Ecobat began in 2025. Over approximately 16 months, the company completed 10 divestitures spanning 17 sites across six countries. These transactions included the sale of its European operations. The proposed sale of its North American platform to Clarios would conclude that transformation.

articles.title: BendPak Introduces Two Double-Wide Parking Lifts
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: BendPak announced that it’s new PL-12000KDS and PL-12000KDT double-wide parking lifts accommodate four vehicles in two parking spots. Their narrow footprints also allow facilities to accommodate more lifts. The PL-12000KDS/KDT lifts join the BendPak PL-12000 tandem lift lineup, which features the company’s patent-pending independent platform design.
BendPak Lifts Feature Independent Platforms

Traditional double-wide parking lifts require operators to remove all vehicles parked below before lowering the upper platforms. However, BendPak’s PL-12000 platforms operate independently, allowing operators to lower one platform while the other remains stationary.
That means operators must move only one vehicle to access a vehicle parked above. The platform design also provides double-car-width open front access, improving entry and exit efficiency.
With commercial and residential development costs continuing to rise, maximizing vehicle capacity within existing space can reduce costs.

“Our new PL-12000KDS and PL-12000KDT tandem parking lifts feature a narrower footprint than our original PL-12000 models for customers who want to maximize the number of lifts they can fit in their parking facility,” said Jeff Kritzer, BendPak president and CEO. “Reducing the width by 15.5 inches, from 221.5 to 206 inches, allows more vehicles to be stored in a facility without expanding the building space. When filling a warehouse, saving just a few inches per lift means 20 lifts can be installed instead of 19 or fewer — that’s space to accommodate at least four more cars.”
