articles.title: Madagascar's Giant Bats Seem to Be Shrinking. After Measuring 121 Specimens, Scientists Suggest Hunting by Humans Is to Blame

paras.en: With wingspans up to five feet, Malagasy flying foxes—among the biggest fruit bats in the world—dominate Madagascar’s skies. But new research suggests that these massive, airborne mammals may not be the behemoths they once were.
paras.zh: 马达加斯加的狐狸是世界上最大的果蝠之一，它们的翅膀长达5英尺，是马达加斯加天空的主角。但新的研究表明，这些巨大的空中哺乳动物可能不再是它们曾经的庞然大物。

paras.en: In a study published in the Journal of Mammalogy on Thursday, scientists found that Madagascar’s flying foxes (Pteropus rufus) may be shrinking in size. The team compared skeleton measurements of modern bats to specimens in various museum collections dating back 150 years. The result: Modern flying fox skulls are noticeably smaller than skulls of their historical counterparts—and human hunting may be to blame.
paras.zh: 在周四发表在《哺乳动物学杂志》上的一项研究中，科学家们发现马达加斯加的飞狐（ Pteropus rufus ）体型可能正在缩小。该团队将现代蝙蝠的骨骼测量结果与150年前的各种博物馆藏品中的标本进行了比较。结果是：现代飞行狐狸的头骨明显小于其历史同行的头骨，而人类狩猎可能是罪魁祸首。

paras.en: The project began in 2021, when Field Museum post-doctoral researcher Emily Cornelius Ruhs, the paper’s lead author, heard a colleague say that the flying fox skeletons in the museum’s collection seemed bigger than the bats she was encountering in the field. Intrigued, Ruhs proposed digitizing the Field Museum’s records to analyze how the mammals’ size might have changed.
paras.zh: 该项目始于2021年，当时该论文的主要作者、菲尔德博物馆博士后研究员艾米丽·科尼利厄斯·鲁斯（ Emily Cornelius Ruhs ）听到一位同事说，博物馆收藏的飞狐骨骼似乎比她在田野里遇到的蝙蝠更大。有趣的是， Ruhs建议将菲尔德博物馆的记录数字化，以分析哺乳动物的大小可能发生的变化。

paras.en: “Then, Steven Goodman, who’s the actual field biologist on the project, was like, ‘I can do better than that,’” Ruhs recounts. He suggested visiting other museums, too, and assessing the size of specimens in person, which would be more precise than studying the records they had on file. Comparing modern and historical skeletons would “actually test whether or not the skull and the dental measurements are changing in size through time,’” Ruhs adds.

Goodman, a field scientist at the Field Museum and a co-author of the study, examined 121 Malagasy flying fox specimens housed across nine museums in both the United States and Europe. He took measurements of 12 different features of the bats’ skulls and teeth, and Ruhs then analyzed the results.

They noticed a significant shift in size around the 1980s: Bats collected prior to that date had skulls an average of 6 percent longer than those collected after, Jake Buehler reports for Science News. Ruhs says this lines up with the beginning of commercial hunting of flying foxes, which are a food source in Madagascar.

Before the 1980s, flying foxes were hunted and eaten on a small scale—to feed a family or local village, she says. But the rise of commercial hunting saw the bats “brought to market and being more readily available on things like restaurant menus in certain locations.” It’s “not this big conglomeration that you’re seeing in the U.S. of food being shipped everywhere,” she explains, but it still put pressure on the animals’ population.
Climate change or deforestation may have also played a role in the shrinkage, but Ruhs says the timing points to hunting as the culprit.

The work doesn’t prove that hunting has made the bats smaller. But Ruhs says it’s likely that hunters are targeting the bigger, more mature bats, which offer more meat. So far, the team isn’t sure if there is a genetic component to the change or whether the largest bats are just hunted and removed from the forests prematurely, before they can effectively reproduce—or end up in museum collections.

Malagasy flying foxes are currently considered a “vulnerable” species. In the early 2000s, Madagascar was home to an estimated 300,000 flying foxes—a number researchers estimate has since dropped by two-thirds, Science News reports. Flying foxes often only bear a single pup per year. So, given the slow reproduction rate, Ruhs says there can be real impacts when the species’ largest, most sexually viable members are taken out of the genetic pool.

“We’re removing these sexually mature and reproductively active bats from the population,” Ruhs says, “which of course has sort of trickle-down effects for what we call population viability: how well the population can maintain and be stable through time.”

The state of the flying foxes has impacts that stretch beyond the bats themselves. Vincent Florens, an ecologist at the University of Mauritius who was not involved in the research, says this fruit bat is a keystone species, or a species that has an outsized impact on its habitat compared to its overall population size. It feeds on large fruits like figs and disperses the seeds throughout the surrounding environment.

“It has a big ecological role, because the dissemination of seeds is extremely important for the reproduction of plants and also for the regeneration of forests,” Florens says. “Once you have the forest, you have everything that lives inside. There’s that cascading effect.”

Christian Vincenot, an engineer at the University of Luxembourg who has conducted prior research with Florens on the state of Mauritian flying foxes, says these bats’ changing size and physiology may affect their ability to fill their seed-dispersing role.

“If also there is an impact on the morphology of the mouth, [the flying foxes] could end up not being able to process as large of fruits and seeds as they used to,” says Vincenot, who was not involved with the new study. “Fruit bats eat a large variety of fruit from many different native plants, but also exotic plants and trees. So, if the population decreases, there [could] be an impact on seed dispersal.”

Given what this study reveals about how hunting pressures are impacting the Malagasy flying fox population, Florens says focusing on the protection and conservation of these animals should be the immediate next step. But, he adds, it’s not as easy as simply banning hunting.

“For us, we want to go to the restaurant, we go to an ATM, we get the money out, we go to the restaurant,” he says. “But for many people [in Madagascar], the ATM is the forest. They are hungry, they go out there, they fish something, they get cash [for] an animal, and they can have dinner.”

Ruhs recognizes this problem: Flying foxes, she says, are “an important food source for a lot of people, and we’re not saying we should stop hunting across the board. But I think it does call into question how much should this be regulated, and who’s in the position to keep these populations safe for the future.”

articles.title: A Dog Left a Paw Print on This Mud Brick 4,000 Years Ago. Archaeologists Discovered It in the Rubble of a Bronze Age House

paras.en: The house collapsed in a fire during the Bronze Age. Archaeologists know that much from excavating its ruins, which were found in modern-day Turkey.
paras.zh: 这座房子在青铜时代的一场大火中倒塌了。考古学家通过挖掘在现代土耳其发现的遗迹了解了这一点。

paras.en: The stories of the humans who built the structure have been lost to history. But one of the mud bricks unearthed in the rubble features an intriguing clue: a dog’s paw print, which survived undisturbed for 4,000 years.
paras.zh: 建造这座建筑的人类的故事已经消失在历史之中。但是在瓦砾中出土的一块泥砖有一个有趣的线索：一只狗的爪印，它可以不受干扰地存活4000年。

paras.en: The house is located at Tavsanli Hoyuk, an archaeological site in western Turkey. Archaeologists from Bilecik Seyh Edebali University have been conducting excavations there since 2021.
paras.zh: 这栋房子位于土耳其西部的考古遗址Tavsanli Hoyuk。自2021年以来， Bilecik Seyh Edebali大学的考古学家一直在那里进行挖掘。

paras.en: “At Tavsanli Hoyuk, one of the largest Bronze Age settlements in Western Anatolia, we are uncovering not only structures and artifacts but also such small and unexpected traces of life,” Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, Turkey’s minister of culture and tourism, says in a social media post, per a translation by the Daily Sabah.
paras.zh: 土耳其文化和旅游部长穆罕默德·努里·埃尔索伊（ Mehmet Nuri Ersoy ）在一篇社交媒体帖子中说： “在安纳托利亚西部最大的青铜时代定居点之一Tavsanli Hoyuk ，我们不仅发现了建筑和文物，还发现了这些意想不到的小生命痕迹。”

paras.en: Tavsanli Hoyuk began as a village some 8,000 years ago. Flooding later covered the land, but settlers returned in roughly 3200 B.C.E., at the beginning of the Bronze Age. Humans inhabited the site continuously for the 1,500 years that followed. But then, around 1700 B.C.E., attackers appear to have burned it down.
paras.zh: Tavsanli Hoyuk起源于大约8000年前的一个村庄。洪水后来淹没了这片土地，但在青铜时代开始时，定居者大约在公元前3200年返回。在接下来的1500年里，人类一直居住在这个地方。但在公元前1700年左右，袭击者似乎烧毁了它。

paras.en: Archaeologists have unearthed spearheads, arrowheads and daggers dating to this period. Previous excavations also revealed the remains of two victims of the attack, who were found beneath the ruins of a house. Officials announced the discovery of the brick marked by a paw print on October 26.
paras.zh: 考古学家出土了可以追溯到这一时期的矛头、箭头和匕首。先前的挖掘工作还发现了两名袭击受害者的遗骸，他们被发现在一所房屋的废墟下。官员于10月26日宣布发现了标有爪印的砖块。

paras.en: During the Bronze Age, workers made mud bricks by mixing water, soil and straw, according to a statement from Bilecik Seyh Edebali University. Workers would have poured this mixture into a mold, which then hardened in the sun. As this particular brick dried, a dog left a distinctive imprint featuring four round toe pads.
paras.zh: 根据Bilecik Seyh Edebali大学的一份声明，在青铜时代，工人们通过混合水、土壤和稻草来制造泥砖。工人会将这种混合物倒入模具中，然后在阳光下硬化。随着这块特别的砖块干涸，一只狗留下了一个独特的印记，上面有四个圆形脚趾垫。

paras.en: “Dogs have a very long history in Anatolia,” Erkan Fidan, the excavation director at Tavsanli Hoyuk, tells IFLScience’s Tom Hale. “By the Bronze Age, dogs were already a familiar part of everyday life in Anatolian settlements. The approximately 4,000-year-old paw prints discovered at Tavsanli Hoyuk provide a particularly direct and touching glimpse of this relationship.”
paras.zh: Tavsanli Hoyuk的挖掘总监Erkan Fidan告诉IFLScience的Tom Hale ： “狗在安纳托利亚有着悠久的历史。” “到青铜时代，狗已经成为安纳托利亚定居点日常生活中熟悉的一部分。在Tavsanli Hoyuk发现的大约4000年前的爪印为这种关系提供了特别直接和感人的一瞥。”

paras.en: Earlier this year, a study published in the journal Nature found genetic evidence of a domesticated dog that lived in what is now Turkey 15,800 years ago. Fidan points to this study, explaining that humans in the region have had a close relationship with dogs for thousands of years.
paras.zh: 今年早些时候，发表在《自然》杂志上的一项研究发现了15800年前生活在现在的土耳其的一只家养狗的遗传证据。Fidan指出了这项研究，解释说该地区的人类与狗有着数千年的密切关系。

paras.en: Quick facts: The oldest domesticated dogs
paras.zh: 简介：最古老的家养狗

paras.en: - In March 2026, two studies with overlapping authors revealed the “first definitive genetic evidence that dogs existed during the Paleolithic period, before humans developed agriculture,” according to the New York Times’ Emily Anthes.
paras.zh: -根据《纽约时报》的艾米丽·安斯（ Emily Anthes ）的说法， 2026年3月，两项作者重叠的研究揭示了“第一个明确的遗传证据，证明狗在人类发展农业之前的旧石器时代就存在了”。

paras.en: - Previously, the earliest genetic evidence of domesticated dogs had been about 10,900 years old.
paras.zh: -以前，最早的驯养狗的遗传证据大约有10900年的历史。

paras.en: “Of course, we cannot determine whether this particular dog was kept as a pet in the modern sense,” Fidan tells IFLScience. “But the discovery offers a small yet remarkable connection to everyday life four millennia ago.”
paras.zh: “当然，我们无法确定这只狗是否是现代意义上的宠物，” Fidan告诉IFLScience。“但这一发现为四千年前的日常生活提供了一个小而非凡的联系。”

paras.en: Paw prints have provided archaeologists with whimsical windows into history across thousands of years. One 15th-century Flemish manuscript features inky cat paw prints preserved on parchment. Archaeologists in Jerusalem found another cat paw print on pottery made more than 1,000 years ago—perhaps the earliest known evidence of a cat kneading (a behavior also known as “making biscuits”).
paras.zh: 爪印为考古学家提供了数千年历史的异想天开的窗口。一本15世纪的佛兰德手稿在羊皮纸上保存了漆黑的猫爪印花。耶路撒冷的考古学家在1000多年前的陶器上发现了另一个猫爪印，这可能是猫揉捏的最早已知证据（这种行为也被称为“制作饼干” ）。

paras.en: Researchers know very little about the dog that stepped on a brick. Did humans witness the act? If so, how did they respond? As Gizmodo’s Gayoung Lee writes, “I have a hunch that the interaction probably ended with the human scoffing and giving the furry troublemaker an affectionate tousle.”
paras.zh: 研究人员对踩到砖头的狗知之甚少。人类目睹了这一行为吗？如果是，他们如何回应？正如Gizmodo的Gayoung Lee所写的那样， “我有一种预感，这种互动可能以人类的嘲笑结束，并给毛茸茸的麻烦制造者带来深情的混乱。”

articles.title: Crafted From Bone, This 2,800-Year-Old Flute Unearthed in Troy May Have Been Played Around the Time That Homer Composed 'The Iliad' and 'The Odyssey'

paras.en: Archaeologists started excavating the ruins of Troy, the ancient city immortalized by the Greek poet Homer, in 1870.
paras.zh: 考古学家于1870年开始挖掘特洛伊遗址，这是一座由希腊诗人荷马永垂不朽的古城。

paras.en: In the century and a half since, digs at the site in northwestern Turkey have unearthed a pair of gold diadems, more than 100 two-handled wine goblets, and arrowheads and weapons dated to the Late Bronze Age, among other artifacts. Now, researchers have added another intriguing object to the mix: a 2,800-year-old bone flute that is thought to be the first musical instrument ever discovered at Troy.
paras.zh: 在此后的一个半世纪里，在土耳其西北部的遗址发掘了一对金冠、100多个双手柄葡萄酒酒杯、可追溯到青铜时代晚期的箭头和武器，以及其他文物。现在，研究人员在组合中添加了另一个有趣的物体：一支有2800年历史的骨笛，被认为是在特洛伊发现的第一件乐器。

paras.en: Turkey’s culture and tourism minister, Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, announced the find on social media last week, noting that the flute provides the first direct archaeological evidence of Troy’s musical culture. Although ancient texts and excavations elsewhere in Anatolia suggest that music “played an important role in [Trojan] religious rituals, as well as social and public life,” no physical traces of such performances had surfaced until now, the Hürriyet Daily News reports.
paras.zh: 土耳其文化和旅游部长穆罕默德·努里·埃尔索伊（ Mehmet Nuri Ersoy ）上周在社交媒体上宣布了这一发现，并指出长笛为特洛伊的音乐文化提供了第一个直接的考古证据。尽管安纳托利亚其他地方的古代文献和发掘表明，音乐“在[特洛伊]宗教仪式以及社会和公共生活中发挥了重要作用” ，但Hürriyet每日新闻报道，直到现在还没有出现过这种表演的物理痕迹。

paras.en: Troya’nın binlerce yıllık kültür ve sanat tarihine iki yeni keşifle katkı sunuyoruz. Bakanlığımızın izin ve destekleriyle Geleceğe Miras Projemiz kapsamında sürdürdüğümüz 2026 yılı kazılarında, yaklaşık 2.800 yıllık kemik flüt ile 4.500 yıllık insan biçimli bir idol başını gün ışığına çıkardık. Arkaik Dönem’e ait kemik flüt, 160 yılı aşkın Troya kazıları tarihinde bugüne kadar bulunan ilk ve tek müzik aleti. Bu keşifle, Troya’daki müzik kültürüne ilişkin doğrudan bir arkeolojik kanıta ulaştık. Troya II kent kapısı çevresinde bulunan idol başıyla da Erken Tunç Çağı’nın sembolik dünyasını ve Batı Anadolu’daki kültürel etkileşimleri anlamamıza katkı sağlayacak yeni bir eseri günümüze kazandırdık. Troya’nın farklı dönemlerini belgeleyen bu buluntuları bilimsel yöntemlerle araştırarak korumaya ve gelecek kuşaklara aktarmaya devam edeceğiz. Kazı ekibimize, Kültür Varlıkları ve Müzeler Genel Müdürlüğümüzün ekiplerine ve çalışmalara katkı sunan tüm mesai arkadaşlarıma teşekkür ediyorum.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: — Mehmet Nuri Ersoy (@MehmetNuriErsoy) October 22, 2026
paras.zh: — Mehmet Nuri Ersoy （ @ MehmetNuriErsoy ） 2026年10月22日

paras.en: Experts discovered the flute in an archaeological layer dating to the eighth century B.C.E., around the time that Homer composed The Iliad and The Odyssey. (Troy’s ruins are divided into nine layers, each corresponding with a different era in the city’s history.) Scholars once thought that Troy was all but abandoned during this period, but more recent research has identified clear evidence of habitation in the area.
paras.zh: 专家们在可追溯到公元前八世纪的考古层中发现了长笛，大约在荷马创作《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》的时候。（特洛伊的遗址分为九层，每层都对应着城市历史上不同的时代。）学者们曾经认为特洛伊在此期间几乎被遗弃，但最近的研究已经确定了该地区居住的明确证据。

paras.en: - The Iliad tells the story of the Trojan War, a legendary conflict between the ancient Greeks and the Trojans. It focuses on the actions of the Greek hero Achilles during the final year of the war.
paras.zh: -《伊利亚特》讲述了特洛伊战争的故事，这是一场古希腊人和特洛伊人之间的传奇冲突。它侧重于希腊英雄阿喀琉斯在战争最后一年的行动。

paras.en: - The Odyssey, meanwhile, chronicles the journey of Odysseus, king of Ithaca, as he tries to return home to his wife and son after the war.
paras.zh: -与此同时，《奥德赛》记录了伊萨卡国王奥德修斯在战后试图回到妻子和儿子身边的旅程。

paras.en: As Rüstem Aslan, head of the excavation team at Troy, tells the state-run Anadolu Agency, the timing of the find is noteworthy: Earlier this year, composer Ludwig Göransson used a similar instrument to create the siren song featured in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster film adaptation of The Odyssey. Played on a replica of an aulos, a double-reeded wind instrument popular in ancient Greece, the tune is one “of longing and sorrow that makes you share, briefly but profoundly, Odysseus’ feelings as he hears the sirens,” Joshua Barone wrote for the New York Times in July.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: To find a flute that might date to Homer’s lifetime, in the same year that The Odyssey loomed so large in the popular imagination, “is an interesting coincidence from the perspective of excavation history,” Aslan says, per a translation by A News.
paras.zh: 阿斯兰说，在《奥德赛》在大众想象中如此庞大的同一年，要找到可以追溯到荷马一生的长笛， “从挖掘历史的角度来看，这是一个有趣的巧合”。

paras.en: In addition to the flute, archaeologists at Troy uncovered the 4,500-year-old head of an anthropomorphic figure that was likely used for religious or ritual purposes. “This find is particularly noteworthy because there are only three to five similar finds during the … history of Troy excavations,” Aslan says, according to Heritage Daily’s Mark Milligan. The object was found near the city gate of Troy II, an Early Bronze Age settlement that was destroyed by fire around 2300 B.C.E.
paras.zh: 除了长笛，特洛伊的考古学家还发现了一个有4500年历史的拟人化头像，可能用于宗教或仪式目的。“这一发现特别值得注意，因为在特洛伊挖掘的历史中，只有三到五个类似的发现，”阿斯兰说，根据传统日报的马克·米利根。该物体是在特洛伊二世城门附近发现的，特洛伊二世是一个青铜时代早期的定居点，在公元前2300年左右被大火摧毁。

paras.en: When the German businessman and amateur archaeologist Heinrich Schliemann first identified the ruins of Troy in the 1870s, he assumed that the layer now known as Troy II dated to the time of the Trojan War. In fact, the objects discovered by Schliemann—including a cache of gold, silver and copper artifacts popularly dubbed “Priam’s treasure,” after the mythical king of Troy—date to about a millennium before the Trojan War, which scholars typically trace to the Late Bronze Age, in the 13th or early 12th century B.C.E.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Ironically, the trench that Schliemann dug while carelessly searching for evidence of Homeric Troy inadvertently damaged the very layers that held these ruins. “If you look on excavation maps, there’s a gap in the middle where it says, ‘Palace removed by Schliemann,’” Eric H. Cline, co-author of the book Digging for Troy: From Homer to Hisarlik, told the Guardian’s Naomi Larsson Piñeda in 2016. “He got Priam’s palace and then threw it away. He found Troy, but he also destroyed Troy.”
paras.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，施里曼在漫不经心地寻找荷马特洛伊的证据时挖掘的战壕无意中损坏了这些废墟的底层。《挖掘特洛伊：从荷马到希萨里克》（ Digging for Troy: From Homer to Hisarlik ）一书的合著者埃里克· H ·克莱恩（ Eric H. Cline ）在2016年告诉《卫报》的纳奥米·拉尔森·皮涅达（ Naomi Larsson Piñeda ）。“他拿了普里阿摩斯的宫殿，然后把它扔了。他找到了特洛伊，但他也摧毁了特洛伊。”

articles.title: How a Contractor’s Claude Agent Got Into the Pentagon
articles.author: Brian Barrett, Zoë Schiffer, Leah Feiger

paras.en: This week on Uncanny Valley, Brian Barrett, Leah Feiger, and Zoë Schiffer dive into our scoop on how a defense contractor connected Claude Code to a secure Department of Defense system. We also discuss the green, yellow, and red flags we see in Anthropic’s IPO filing—and why it’s a test not just for the AI industry but for the entire US economy—and how volunteers nationwide are preparing for ICE agents potentially showing up at polling sites in the midterms.
paras.zh: 本周，在《恐怖谷》节目中，Brian Barrett、Leah Feiger 和 Zoë Schiffer 深入探讨了国防承包商如何将 Claude Code 连接到安全的国防部系统。我们还讨论了 Anthropic 的 IPO 文件中看到的绿色、黄色和红色信号，以及为什么这不仅是对人工智能行业的考验，也是对整个美国经济的考验，以及全国志愿者如何为中期选举中可能出现在投票站的 ICE 特工做准备。

paras.en: - A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
paras.zh: - 一家国防承包商允许他们的个人人工智能代理访问安全的五角大楼系统

paras.en: - The Anthropic S-1 Filing Is Also an AI Doomsday Primer
paras.zh: - Anthropic S-1 文件也是人工智能世界末日入门书

paras.en: - What’s Worth More Than Cash in San Francisco Real Estate? Anthropic Stock
paras.zh: - 旧金山房地产有什么比现金更值钱的？人择库存

paras.en: - Massive Groups of Volunteers Are Ready to Face Down ICE at the Polls
paras.zh: - 大批志愿者准备在投票站对抗 ICE

paras.en: You can follow Brian Barrett on Bluesky at @brbarrett, Zoë Schiffer on Bluesky at @zoeschiffer, and Leah Feiger on Bluesky at @leahfeiger. Write to us at [email protected].
paras.zh: 您可以通过 @brbarrett 关注 Bluesky 上的 Brian Barrett，通过 @zoeschiffer 关注 Bluesky 上的 Zoë Schiffer，以及通过 @leahfeiger 关注 Bluesky 上的 Leah Feiger。请通过 [email protected] 给我们写信。

paras.en: If you’re on an iPhone or iPad, open the app called Podcasts, or just tap this link. You can also download an app like Overcast or Pocket Casts and search for “uncanny valley.” We’re on Spotify too.
paras.zh: 如果您使用的是 iPhone 或 iPad，请打开名为“播客”的应用程序，或者只需点击此链接。您还可以下载 Overcast 或 Pocket Casts 等应用程序，然后搜索“恐怖谷”。我们也在 Spotify 上。

paras.en: Note: This is an automated transcript, which may contain errors.
paras.zh: 注意：这是自动记录，可能包含错误。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: Welcome to the WIRED’s Uncanny Valley. I’m Brian Barrett, executive editor.
paras.zh: 布莱恩·巴雷特：欢迎来到《连线》杂志的恐怖谷。我是布莱恩·巴雷特，执行主编。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: I’m Zoë Schiffer, contributing editor.
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer：我是 Zoë Schiffer，特约编辑。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: And I’m Leah Feiger, director of politics and science.
paras.zh: 利亚·费格：我是政治和科学主任利亚·费格。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: This week, Anthropic has officially filed to go public. There is a lot going on in the hundreds of pages that the company submitted as part of its S-1 filing, from staggering earnings and losses, to warnings of AI’s existential threat. Obviously, we’re talking about Anthropic here. We’ll discuss our key takeaways and why this IPO is kind of high stakes, not just for the AI industry, but honestly the entire US economy.
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer：本周，Anthropic 已正式申请上市。该公司作为 S-1 文件的一部分提交的数百页内容中包含了很多内容，从令人震惊的收益和亏损，到对人工智能的生存威胁的警告。显然，我们在这里谈论的是人择。我们将讨论我们的关键要点，以及为什么这次 IPO 的风险很高，不仅对人工智能行业，而且对整个美国经济来说都是如此。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: We’re also bringing you a scoop about how a defense contractor plugged Anthropic’s Claude into a secure Department of Defense system, in what’s really one of the most outlandish uses of AI in the government we’ve seen so far.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：我们还为您带来了有关国防承包商如何将 Anthropic 的 Claude 插入安全的国防部系统的独家新闻，这实际上是我们迄今为止在政府中看到的最奇怪的人工智能应用之一。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: And the midterms are right around the corner, just a few days away. Massive groups of volunteers all over the country are already getting ready to protect their communities from the potential that ICE officers show up at the polls. We’ll get into how grassroots efforts like these are a reflection of a deeply uncertain election cycle.
paras.zh: 布莱恩·巴雷特（Brian Barrett）： 期中选举即将来临，仅剩几天时间。全国各地的大量志愿者团体已经做好准备，保护他们的社区免受 ICE 官员出现在投票站的影响。我们将探讨像这样的基层努力如何反映了高度不确定的选举周期。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: So on Monday, we learned that Anthropic finally pulled the trigger and publicly filed for its IPO. This has been highly anticipated for a bunch of reasons. Anthropic is expected to raise more money in its IPO than any company in history, and it would be the first major US company focused solely on building AI software to go public. To give you a sense of the scale that we’re talking about, the company’s valuation went from $183 billion a little over a year ago to $965 billion in its most recent round, and some expect that it could be worth close to $2 trillion once it starts trading. So the filing basically gives us the first real look inside Anthropic’s business because it’s a private company right now. It doesn’t have to report a bunch of stuff. And the numbers are pretty extreme in both directions, billions of dollars in revenue and even more billions in losses, and hundreds of billions that the company has already committed to compute. Because there’s a ton to unpack in this paperwork, I thought it would be fun to divide it into green flags, yellow flags, and red flags that we saw from the filing. What do you guys think?
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer：周一，我们得知 Anthropic 终于扣动扳机并公开申请 IPO。出于多种原因，人们对此寄予厚望。 Anthropic 预计在 IPO 中筹集的资金将超过历史上任何一家公司，这将是第一家专注于构建人工智能软件的美国大型公司上市。为了让您了解我们正在谈论的规模，该公司的估值从一年多前的 1830 亿美元增至最近一轮的 9650 亿美元，一些人预计一旦开始交易，其价值可能接近 2 万亿美元。因此，这份文件基本上让我们第一次真正了解了 Anthropic 的业务，因为它现在是一家私营公司。它不必报告一堆东西。而且这些数字在两个方向上都相当极端，收入数十亿美元，损失甚至更多，而该公司已经承诺计算数千亿美元。因为这份文件中有大量内容需要解开，所以我认为将其分为我们从文件中看到的绿旗、黄旗和红旗会很有趣。你们觉得怎么样？

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I’m astounded by how much money is at play here. This is, yes.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：我对这里有多少钱感到震惊。这是，是的。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: What flag, Leah? What flag is that?
paras.zh: 布莱恩·巴雷特：莉亚，什么旗子？那是什么旗？

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: For the sake of the economy, it’s green.
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer：为了经济，它是绿色的。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: For the sake of the economy, it’s green. This is so much money, guys. Sue me, but the only thing I can think of right now is that article that WIRED ran a couple of months ago about how people were selling their homes in the Bay Area with the promise of Anthropic stock post-IPO. And I remember at the time I was like, "How close are we to this?" And Zoe said, "Oh, they’re going to make so much money."
paras.zh: Leah Feiger：为了经济，它是绿色的。这是这么多钱，伙计们。告我吧，但我现在唯一能想到的就是《连线》几个月前发表的那篇文章，内容是关于人们如何在首次公开募股后承诺 Anthropic 股票的情况下出售湾区的房屋。我记得当时我就想，“我们离这还有多远？”佐伊说：“哦，他们会赚很多钱的。”

paras.en: Brian Barrett: Is it fair to say, Zoë, I feel like having the financials out there, yes, they’re losing money hand over fist, but the financials I think are better than people were expecting maybe. At least, it feels like they put a lot of concerns to rest, not all of them, but this is a real business. This is a business that is growing. It’s doing all the things you would want a business to do.
paras.zh: Brian Barrett ：公平地说， Zoë ，我觉得财务状况很好，是的，他们正在赔钱，但我认为财务状况可能比人们预期的要好。至少，感觉他们解决了很多问题，但不是所有问题，但这是一项真正的业务。这是一项正在成长的业务。它正在做你想让企业做的所有事情。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: Yes, I think absolutely. So its revenue hit $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, and it’s grown more than 14 fold from the same period last year. I think we have to go back to 2022 and remember that when ChatGPT came on the scene, it wasn’t even apparent that AI would have a real enterprise application. This was a consumer app that didn’t have really any business case for it. And it wasn’t until Anthropic came on the scene years later, it rolled out Claude Code that we started to really see like, oh no, there’s a viable business and actually the majority of the money is going to come from other businesses using their coding product. This is also, I think, a key difference that you hear from insiders between Dario and Sam. People very close to Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, will say he wakes up every single day and says, "Enterprise code." That is the thing he cares about. And that’s because that’s the thing that makes money for these businesses. Whereas I think the perception from some is that OpenAI is a little more scattered and all over the place. And I think you can see that in the numbers.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Brian Barrett: So they are leaning in. They have Claude code, huge success, enterprise code, huge success. I will say, to introduce a yellow flag, of that revenue that you talked about, very impressive revenue over $60 billion, nearly half of it came from three tech companies cloud marketplaces. So they are pretty heavily reliant on a small number of companies which are also competitors. It is this sort of tangled nest of reliances in this industry that feels, I think Anthropic didn’t put it as one of its major risk factors. We can talk about the risk factors in a second because that was my favorite section, but it does feel like, where’s the moat? Is there enough of one given how much they’re relying on a handful of companies that are also developing their own AI, other AI products are getting better, open source products, open weight products are out there. How yellow is that flag?
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: I think it’s yellow. It’s not surprising that a polyamorous worker cooperative would be incestuous in its business dealings. I was not shocked by that information. And it’s not unusual for a small percentage of spenders to have an out-sized impact on a company’s revenue. I think there was another number that Ramp put out recently, 80 percent of revenue for both Anthropic and OpenAI comes from about the top 1 percent of AI spenders. So the companies that are spending the most account for the vast majority of the company’s revenues. But it is a vulnerability, because if there’s a pullback and those companies start spending less, Anthropic is exposed. But another, I don’t know where to put this flag. I think it’s green. They were transparent about some of the risks involved in the IPO, some of the existential risks of AI generally. This is probably my favorite part in the whole thing. “Concerns have been raised ... That sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed and safeguarded appropriately, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.”
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer：我认为它是黄色的。一个多角恋的工人合作社在其业务往来中出现乱伦也就不足为奇了。我对这个信息并不感到震惊。一小部分消费者对公司收入产生巨大影响的情况并不罕见。我认为 Ramp 最近发布的另一个数字是，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 80% 的收入来自大约 1% 的 AI 消费者。因此，支出最多的公司占公司收入的绝大多数。但这是一个漏洞，因为如果出现回调并且这些公司开始减少支出，Anthropic 就会面临风险。但另一个，我不知道该把这个标志放在哪里。我认为它是绿色的。他们对 IPO 涉及的一些风险以及人工智能普遍存在的一些风险保持透明。这可能是整个事情中我最喜欢的部分。 “人们担心......足够先进的人工智能系统如果没有得到适当的开发和保护，可能会给人类带来灾难性或生存风险。”

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: The use of the passive voice in this S-1, concerns have been raised by Dario to be so for real.
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer：达里奥（Dario）对 S-1 中被动语态的使用提出了担忧，认为这是真的。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: Internally by Anthropic, I will say too, the phrase existential risk comes up three times. It’s twice existential risk to humanity, once existential risk to society. So in that scenario, presumably there are still humans, they have just abandoned any semblance of a social contract.
paras.zh: Brian Barrett ：在Anthropic的内部，我也会说，存在风险这个词出现了三次。这对人类来说是两次生存风险，对社会来说是两次生存风险。因此，在这种情况下，大概仍然有人类，他们刚刚放弃了任何表面上的社会契约。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: Zoë, I love that this was a green flag for you, the fact that they’re so openly-
paras.zh: 布莱恩·巴雷特：佐伊，我喜欢这对你来说是一面绿色的旗帜，因为他们是如此公开--

paras.en: Brian Barrett: And to be clear, they have been shouting this since they started that AI could kill everybody. This is not new for them. What I thought was interesting, and I’ll call it a red flag, red flag for humanity, yellow flag for Anthropic, green flag for me because I love to talk about it. So the same thing that they cite as most likely to cause the end of human life on earth, is the thing that they also cite as one of their primary competitive advantages. And that is recursive self-improvement. So that’s where an AI model can improve itself. And they’re saying on the one hand, if AI models keep getting better at improving themselves, and can eventually improve themselves to the point where humans don’t even need to look at it, closing the loop where AI just gets better, and makes AI better, and makes AI better to the point where we don’t even understand what AI is doing anymore, but gosh, it’s good and it’s making a lot of money, that’s the scenario in which AI is powerful enough to maybe end the world. But it’s also, Anthropic notes also we’re really good at that. We’re investing a lot of money in that. That’s how we’re going to get ahead.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: And how relatable is that? Who among us doesn’t have a shadow side that is equally augmented by the power that that shadow side gives you?
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer：这有多相关？我们当中谁没有阴影面，而阴影面赋予你的力量同样增强了它？

paras.en: Leah Feiger: To be clear, and WIRED covered this, as did basically everyone. When former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned and said it was because Anthropic could bring about the end of the world, he specifically cited curbing RSI at the top of his list. This is the whole ballgame.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：说清楚，有线电视覆盖了这一点，基本上每个人都是这样。当前人类学研究员雅各布·考克森（ Jacob Coxon ）辞职并表示这是因为人类可以带来世界末日时，他特别提到了抑制RSI。这就是整个球赛。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: Yes. And then the industry in general is very ... I think this is probably too extreme, but Bernie Sanders has a bill out there, and Ro Khanna has a separate bill that say, "Hey, let’s just ban recursive self-improvement. Let’s just say we’re not doing that." I will say one little note is that the risk factors is the longest section of the prospectus. It’s 94 pages, I believe. So they could have just said, "We have a shadow side and saved everybody.
paras.zh: Brian Barrett ：是的。然后整个行业都非常...我认为这可能太极端了，但是Bernie Sanders有一个法案， Ro Khanna有一个单独的法案说， “嘿，让我们禁止递归自我提升。假设我们没有这样做。“我要说的一点是，风险因素是招股说明书中最长的部分。我相信是94页。所以他们本可以说， “我们有阴影的一面，拯救了所有人。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Can we talk about a red flag that I haven’t gotten a great answer on yet, and I kind of need you to explain this to me like I’m a toddler? The compute bill, all of this technology costs so much money. I don’t personally feel like I have an understanding of where the limit is, how you do not spend enough to use all of your money and also spend enough to not put yourself out of business and end your technology forever. Perhaps I do not understand compute in its entirety or where it comes from, but all of this together, this is just so much. Tell me.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: It is so much. I’m not going to pretend that I understand it. The scale of what we’re talking about is, again, totally unprecedented. You get a lot of railroad analogies when you start talking about this stuff, but I will say that one key difference is that unlike the railroad companies, which were operating on slightly thinner margins, these are still very well-funded and rich companies. And so yes, they’re investing a ton in compute, and they expect that that compute will be needed. So far it is, and they expect that to continue to rise. I personally think that that is a viable argument, but of course the flip side is like, well, if growth starts to seriously slow down, and they’re left holding the bill for all of this compute that they’ve committed to, a lot of the contracts that Anthropic has signed, they can’t get out of. That’s going to be really bad, and it’s going to be bad not just for Anthropic, but for the entire US economy.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Leah Feiger: They call it their most significant operating cost, in quotes.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：他们称之为最重要的运营成本。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: I think significant too, that unlike say SpaceX, unlike Meta, other companies that are heavily invested in AI, a lot of what Anthropic is doing is basically leasing compute. They are not building as much. They are contracting out. So on the one hand, that maybe frees them from long-term obligations on these massive properties. On the other hand, obviously it’s sort of, to Zoë’s point, they’re contracts they can’t get out of. They are committed to these contracts, and they don’t really control their own destiny in that regard, especially when the compute is very competitive now. Getting access to compute has been really, really hard. It’s getting harder, especially as finance companies are less inclined to provide the debt, to support the debt to pay for all these infrastructure costs. One thing I wanted to add really quick is that they do say in the prospectus, I just need to call this out, that the company needs to make forward investments that will seem, "irresponsibly large," at first, which if Zoë found the shadow self relatable, I found this relatable because it’s what I tell my family every time I order DoorDash.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Brian Barrett: It’s going to be irresponsibly large at first glance.
paras.zh: 布莱恩·巴雷特：乍一看，它会变得不负责任地大。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: But will pay off eventually.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：但最终还是会有回报的。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I want to move us over to talk about a massive story that WIRED published today that also has to do with Anthropic’s Claude. WIRED’s Victoria Elliot reported today all about a security incident at the Department of Defense caused by a contractor who connected a secure centralized system, one used by multiple intelligence agencies, to their personal account for Claude Code, Anthropic’s commercial AI coding agent. The contractor works for the global consulting firm Accenture, and according to sources, the agent sent information about the DOD system along with login credentials, to a high-risk third-party website. And it ran inside the DOD network sources tell us for two months before anyone caught on.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Really to start us off, and I want to get into these details and everyone should go read this on wired.com, but I think the overarching thing that I really want to get across here is we have not seen this before. This is a massive, massive example of an AI agent in theory wreaking havoc, or even just having access to government systems without people’s knowledge of that.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：真的是为了让我们开始，我想深入了解这些细节，每个人都应该在wired.com上阅读这个，但我认为我真正想在这里传达的最重要的事情是我们以前从未见过这个。这是人工智能代理在理论上造成严重破坏，甚至只是在人们不知道的情况下访问政府系统的一个巨大而巨大的例子。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: First of all, huge scoop by Tori. Major credit to her. Really, really well done. I’m surprised there was not a system in place to catch this. I’m surprised that it was allowed to happen in the first place. It feels like there are multiple levels of failings here, and I think speaks to just sort of this is the DoD, this is happening, I assume, at all kinds of organizations as people become more reliant on agents to do literally whatever for them.
paras.zh: Brian Barrett ：首先， Tori的超级独家新闻。主要归功于她。真的，真的做得很好。我很惊讶没有一个系统来捕捉这个。我很惊讶它一开始就被允许发生。感觉这里有多层次的失败，我认为这就是国防部，我认为，随着人们越来越依赖代理人为他们做任何事情，这种情况正在各种组织中发生。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: Yeah. God, those people. Leah, my question for you, and then I want to give my take, is that we don’t know that anything nefarious was going on. This contractor was trying to use Claude to write code and deploy it.
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer ：是的，天哪，那些人。莉娅，我想问你，然后我想说的是，我们不知道发生了什么邪恶的事情。该承包商试图使用Claude编写代码并部署它。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Yes. So this isn’t a massive hacking attempt.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：是的，所以这不是一次大规模的黑客攻击。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: I think that’s more interesting though.
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer ：我认为这更有趣。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I agree. I agree. It’s the idea that there was access at all.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：我同意。我同意。这个想法是有访问权限的。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: Yeah. The thing that it reminds me of is a really popular product in Silicon Valley, maybe everywhere right now, is this recording tool and transcription tool called Granola. Basically, it’s this thing that connects to your calendar. When you have a meeting, it automatically starts recording. The result of that is that in many states, you’re illegally recording people all the time. And it’s become such a norm in Silicon Valley that everyone’s just thrown up their hands and been like, "Whatever. I guess this is just what we’re doing now." And this reminds me of that. I think that people are so used to having agents do things for them, or using Claude Code where they would’ve previously written and deployed code by hand, that they’re not as aware that what they’re doing is breaking norms, rules, laws.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Brian Barrett: I just want to quickly confirm, because I Googled it just now, California is a two-party consent state. If that’s useful to anyone out there who’s using Granola.
paras.zh: Brian Barrett ：我只是想快速确认一下，因为我刚刚在谷歌上搜索过，加利福尼亚州是一个两方同意的州。如果这对使用格兰诺拉麦片的人有用的话。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: It’s fully illegal. It’s fully illegal.
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer ：这是完全违法的。这是完全违法的。

paras.en: Brian Barrett: It’s fully illegal. You are breaking the law.
paras.zh: Brian Barrett ：这是完全违法的。你违反了法律。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: I really wish that you could see my slack-jawed open-faced right now, the fact that that exists. But back to the Accenture of it all, back to the DoD of it all, this system that this Claude agent had access to, the centralized system contains controlled unclassified information. So it’s CUI, it’s considered to be sensitive, but not to be released to the public without review. The issue though is that the way that different pieces of this information from this system and other parts that the system has access to, can be combined to create classified information. Does that make sense?
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Leah Feiger: To spell this out a little bit more, this can include information about critical infrastructure across the US, nuclear submarine propulsion, vulnerabilities to chemical and biological terrorism. This is not casual stuff that they had access to. The source aware of the incident who requested anonymity to speak to Tori said to her, "It puts all the data that’s in there at risk. If the third party software was compromised, there could be somebody out there with the ability to log into a secure environment without anyone knowing. It’s 100 percent a national security threat and could cause irreparable harm." This is serious. So the Accenture employee who was alleged to have connected this secure production environment to their personal Claude account to allow this agent to write and deploy code is also breaking another rule technically, because Claude is currently barred from being used by DoD staff.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Ever so young. This is a Mad Lib story. This is a Mad Lib story, to automate the process the contractor gave their login credentials. The agent wasn’t just writing code, but committing it, meaning that it was saving the code to the system on the employee’s behalf. And also they had to connect to the internet, so some of these things were air-gapped.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：非常年轻。这是一个疯狂自由的故事。这是一个Mad Lib的故事，为了自动化承包商给他们的登录凭据的过程。代理不仅仅是编写代码，而是提交代码，这意味着它代表员工将代码保存到系统中。而且他们还必须连接到互联网，所以其中一些东西是气隙的。

paras.en: Zoë Schiffer: Do we know what accountability looks like here? What has happened to the employee, what Accenture or the DoD are doing in the wake of this?
paras.zh: Zoë Schiffer ：我们知道这里的问责制是什么样的吗？员工发生了什么事，埃森哲或国防部在这之后做了什么？

paras.en: Leah Feiger: That is a great question. Despite the security risks, sources told WIRED that Accenture employees did not really treat the incident as super severe or urgent.
paras.zh: Leah Feiger ：这是一个很好的问题。尽管存在安全风险，但消息人士告诉WIRED ，埃森哲员工并没有真正将事件视为超级严重或紧急。

paras.en: Leah Feiger: Yep. Good, good, good. So when we reached out to the Department of Defense, a spokesperson there told us that, "The department does not comment on the status of its networks or systems." And on Accenture’s end, their spokesperson said that they "take all concerns seriously. These allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit. We fully complied with our legal and contractual obligations." When pressed though, Accenture didn’t offer clarification on who conducted the investigation, or dispute that there had been what could be characterized as an incident. I have to say, this isn’t the first time that Accenture has had a bit of an issue recently. Earlier this month, the FBI found that an Accenture contractor did not patch a vulnerability that led to the hacking group Shiny Hunters getting access to all of the FBI data. I don’t know if you guys remember that fun story. So lots of things happening here. So many different questions, for me at least, brought up about the use of personal AI agents when it comes to the workspace, contractors and government and what they have access to, what they have to reveal to the government at what time. There’s a lot here that fell in the cracks, and like I said earlier, Mad Libs, Mad Libs of a bad situation just really gone awry.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Brian Barrett: It feels like the use of AI agents in general, it’s a shortcut. It’s like I want to take a shortcut to whatever it is I’m doing. Sometimes that’s for great reasons. Zoë, you’ve given over 80 percent of your life to agents and you’re thriving, but there are some situations where you really shouldn’t take any kind of shortcut, especially not a shortcut that you can’t really control that’s going to be touching sensitive documents. Yeah, it’s inexcusable. I assume not the last time we’re going to hear about something like this. Well, in other news, the midterms are officially a week away and early voting already underway in lots of states. You may have already voted as you’re listening to this, power to you if so. One of the questions hanging over these elections though has nothing to do with who’s on the ballot. It’s who’s going to be at the polling stations. For the last six months, President Trump and his allies have declined to rule out the possible deployment of ICE agents to voting sites during the midterms, even though that would be illegal under federal law, has not really stopped him before in various scenarios. This week, WIRED’s David Gilbert spoke to a dozen people or so taking part in a nationwide effort to get ready for that possibility. They’re in towns and cities across the country, and they are people who see the presence of ICE at the polls as an existential threat to democracy. They’ve built massive networks of people to do a couple different things. The overall goal though is to A, document what ICE is doing and B, spread the word about rights to voters. So if you do go to the polls and you see ICE there, you know how to respond and react. Great that people are planning for this. Leah, I’m curious, how much of a likelihood or inevitability do you think this is going to be? ICE showing up at the polls and kind of disrupting ... I guess their very presence is disruptive, right? I think so it’s really just how likely do you think it is that they actually show up?
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Leah Feiger: A really good question and one that I’m honestly changing my mind on every few days. Recently, the Trump administration has indicated that they will not be sending ICE to the polls. Like you said, the last couple of months have been the exact opposite of that. And then you also have DHS and other random government accounts posting about how they are apprehending illegal voters as we speak. So there’s some mixed messaging that’s clearly happening right now. And in the middle of that, these organizations have stepped in to say, "OK, here’s our plan should this happen." Simultaneously, I think there’s just a lot of fear. Do I think that every single polling station is going to have that? No. Do I think that fear about it is probably going to dissuade some people from voting? Yeah. Yeah, I do. This isn’t forcing you to stand in a line for hours on end, which to be clear, also bad. This is the threat that you are going to be thrown in a facility and never see your family or your home ever again. This is massive. This is what ICE tactics have been in the past. So applying it to this situation, very, very scary. Will it happen? I think we’re probably going to see some of it. But the possibility for misinformation, I say misinformation, not disinformation, because people are just going to be spreading things around that they haven’t perhaps verified because of fear, because of what the Trump administration has been promising and has done in so many communities across the US over this past year, is very real and very scary.

articles.title: Google Pixel Watch 5 Sale: Its Lowest Price Yet (2026)
articles.author: Boutayna Chokrane

paras.en: If you’ve been waiting for a good deal on Google’s latest smartwatch before you commit, you're in luck. The Google Pixel Watch 5 (the 41-mm model with Wi-Fi) is currently $300, down from $400, marking its lowest price yet. (The larger 45-mm model is also discounted, from $430 to $330.)
paras.zh: 如果您在购买之前一直在等待谷歌最新智能手表的优惠，那么您很幸运。 Google Pixel Watch 5（带 Wi-Fi 的 41 毫米型号）目前售价从 400 美元降至 300 美元，创下迄今为止的最低价格。 （较大的 45 毫米型号也有折扣，从 430 美元降至 330 美元。）

paras.en: This early Black Friday sale means you don’t have to wait until the late-November holiday to score the worthwhile discount—and we recommend you don’t. Amazon, Best Buy, and the Google Store are all offering the 25 percent off deal, but I don’t know for how much longer. In other words, now is a great time to score this smartwatch for less.
paras.zh: 黑色星期五提前促销意味着您不必等到 11 月下旬的假期才能获得物有所值的折扣，我们建议您不要这样做。亚马逊、百思买和谷歌商店都提供 25% 的折扣，但我不知道能持续多久。换句话说，现在正是以更低的价格购买这款智能手表的好时机。

paras.en: The Pixel Watch 5 is one of the best smartwatches available for Android users. It’s a refinement of an already brilliant wearable, with double the RAM and storage, plus an upgraded Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 processor that makes this edition 20 percent faster than its predecessor. The domed display is gorgeous, comfortable, and easy to read during workouts, and it provides meaningful upgrades for health and fitness tracking.
paras.zh: Pixel Watch 5 是 Android 用户可用的最佳智能手表之一。它是对已经非常出色的可穿戴设备的改进，具有双倍的 RAM 和存储空间，再加上升级的 Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 处理器，使该版本比其前身快 20%。圆顶显示屏华丽、舒适，并且在锻炼期间易于阅读，并且它为健康和健身跟踪提供了有意义的升级。

paras.en: Beyond being able to track weights and reps, the new Strength Training experience includes a workout builder, audio cues, and rest times. You can build a custom routine in the Google Health app and have the watch guide you through each exercise, and incorporate Gemini AI by asking it to generate a workout based on a photo of your gym equipment. Speaking of Gemini, the Pixel Watch 5 supports certain offline tasks, such as starting a workout, which is nice if you like to leave your watch at home while you exercise.
paras.zh: 除了能够跟踪体重和次数之外，新的力量训练体验还包括锻炼生成器、音频提示和休息时间。您可以在 Google Health 应用程序中建立自定义例程，让手表指导您完成每项锻炼，并通过要求它根据健身器材的照片生成锻炼项目来整合 Gemini AI。说到 Gemini，Pixel Watch 5 支持某些离线任务，例如开始锻炼，如果您想在锻炼时将手表留在家里，这会很好。

paras.en: Google’s new Health Guardian tools include features for monitoring insulin resistance trends, blood pressure trends, breathing emergencies (available only in select countries), and sleep breathing quality. The watch also retains useful features like ECG, skin temperature tracking, and loss-of-pulse detection. It comes with upgraded sleep tracking, too, with Google claiming 15 percent greater accuracy than the Pixel Watch 4.
paras.zh: 谷歌的新健康卫士工具包括监测胰岛素抵抗趋势、血压趋势、呼吸紧急情况（仅在部分国家/地区提供）和睡眠呼吸质量的功能。该手表还保留了心电图、皮肤温度跟踪和脉搏丢失检测等有用功能。它还配备了升级的睡眠跟踪功能，谷歌声称其准确度比 Pixel Watch 4 高出 15%。

paras.en: Google estimates up to 40 hours of battery life, but mine only got to around 36 hours in testing before conking out. Fast charging is the real standout, though; just 15 minutes on the charger delivers up to 15 hours of use. If you’re like me and only remember to charge your watch 20 minutes before leaving the house, this is a lifesaver.
paras.zh: 谷歌估计电池续航时间可达 40 小时，但我的测试仅达到 36 小时左右就崩溃了。不过，快速充电才是真正的亮点。只需充电 15 分钟即可使用长达 15 小时。如果您像我一样只记得在出门前 20 分钟给手表充电，那么这就是您的救星。

paras.en: At its original $400 price, the Pixel Watch 5 is a pricey recommendation, especially since many of its software upgrades will also make their way to the previous generation. But at $300, it’s cheaper than the latest Apple Watch Series 12 and other high-end smartwatches. This is the lowest price I’ve seen for the Pixel Watch 5, so if you’ve been eyeing it, there’s little reason to wait for Black Friday.
paras.zh: 以 400 美元的原价计算，Pixel Watch 5 是一款昂贵的推荐产品，特别是因为它的许多软件升级也将延续到上一代产品。但它的售价为 300 美元，比最新的 Apple Watch Series 12 和其他高端智能手表便宜。这是我见过的 Pixel Watch 5 的最低价格，所以如果你一直在关注它，就没有理由等待黑色星期五。

articles.title: Former patient sues Sen. Roger Marshall for charging illegal interest

paras.en: Oct. 30 (UPI) -- U.S. Sen. Roger Marshall was sued Thursday by a patient of his former medical clinic who accuses him of charging illegal interest rates on unpaid medical bills.
paras.zh: 10月30日（合众社）——周四，美国参议员罗杰·马歇尔被他以前的诊所的一名病人起诉，指控他对未付的医疗费用收取非法利率。

paras.en: Marshall, R-Kan., has sued more than 700 patients over medical debt in his 25 years as an obstetrician-gynecologist, The New York Times reported.
paras.zh: 据《纽约时报》报道，堪萨斯州共和党人马歇尔在 25 年的妇产科医生生涯中，因医疗债务起诉了 700 多名患者。

paras.en: Some 81 of those patients were arrested for missing court dates.
paras.zh: 其中约 81 名患者因缺席法庭日期而被捕。

paras.en: One of those patients, Meischa Zimmerman, is now a lead plaintiff in the case. The class action lawsuit accuses Marshall of charging patients up to 18% annual interest, exceeding the state's limit of 15%.
paras.zh: 其中一名患者梅莎·齐默尔曼 (Meischa Zimmerman) 现在是该案的主要原告。集体诉讼指控 Marshall 向患者收取高达 18% 的年利息，超过了该州 15% 的限制。

paras.en: Zimmerman alleges the senator's clinic, Heartland Regional OBGYN, would often target low-income and uninsured mothers in "callous and predatory" debt collection schemes.
paras.zh: 齐默尔曼声称，参议员的诊所“哈特兰地区妇产科”经常会针对低收入和没有保险的母亲实施“冷酷和掠夺性”的收债计划。

paras.en: "Obviously, I think a jury will place a dollar value on our complaint over charging 18% usury rate on medical debt, but I will let the legal document speak for itself," attorney Kent Roth told NPR-affiliate KCUR.
paras.zh: 律师肯特·罗斯 (Kent Roth) 告诉 NPR 附属机构 KCUR：“显然，我认为陪审团会对我们对医疗债务收取 18% 高利贷的投诉进行评估，但我会让法律文件说明一切。”

paras.en: The lawyer who sued patients on Marshall's behalf, Steven Johnson, told The Times that collection efforts were "pretty much the way it works in the state of Kansas."
paras.zh: 代表马歇尔起诉患者的律师史蒂文·约翰逊告诉《泰晤士报》，催收工作“与堪萨斯州的运作方式几乎一样”。

paras.en: "Generally, at the time of services for all our clients if they were not paid up front, the Debtor agreed to an 18 percent interest rate," Johnson told the newspaper.
paras.zh: “一般来说，在为我们所有客户提供服务时，如果没有预先付款，债务人同意 18% 的利率，”约翰逊告诉该报。

paras.en: Marshall is running for reelection against Democrat Adam Hamilton, a Methodist minister.
paras.zh: 马歇尔正在竞选连任，对手是卫理公会牧师、民主党人亚当·汉密尔顿。

articles.title: Ill. man pleads guilty in $227M COVID-19 scheme to defraud Medicare

paras.en: Oct. 30 (UPI) -- An Illinois man pleaded guilty Friday to running a $227 million Medicare fraud scheme that used personal information purchased from a company in Pakistan to bill the government for COVID-19 tests that patients never received.
paras.zh: 10 月 30 日 (合众国际社)——周五，一名伊利诺伊州男子承认实施了价值 2.27 亿美元的医疗保险欺诈计划，该计划利用从巴基斯坦一家公司购买的个人信息向政府收取患者从未接受过的 COVID-19 检测费用。

paras.en: Syed Murtuza Kablazada, 36, an Indian national living in Des Plaines, Ill., pleaded guilty in federal court to two counts of healthcare fraud.
paras.zh: 赛义德·穆尔图扎·卡布拉扎达 (Syed Murtuza Kablazada)，36 岁，居住在伊利诺伊州德斯普兰斯市的印度国民，在联邦法院承认两项医疗保健欺诈罪。

paras.en: Prosecutors said Kablazada and his associates purchased three medical laboratories in the Chicago area between January and June 2023.
paras.zh: 检察官表示，卡布拉扎达及其同伙于 2023 年 1 月至 6 月期间在芝加哥地区购买了三个医学实验室。

paras.en: The laboratories -- Chicago Care, V Care and Al-Ameer -- were then used to submit fraudulent claims to Medicare for COVID-19 test kits.
paras.zh: 随后，Chicago Care、V Care 和 Al-Ameer 等实验室被用来向 Medicare 提交欺诈性的 COVID-19 检测试剂盒索赔。

paras.en: Kablazada paid approximately $11 million to a company in Pakistan that claimed to provide telemarketing services. In exchange, he received personal information belonging to hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries.
paras.zh: Kablazada 向一家声称提供电话营销服务的巴基斯坦公司支付了约 1100 万美元。作为交换，他收到了属于数十万医疗保险受益人的个人信息。

paras.en: Prosecutors said the information was used to bill Medicare for tests that patients had neither requested nor received.
paras.zh: 检察官表示，这些信息被用来向医疗保险收取患者既没有要求也没有接受的测试的费用。

paras.en: The laboratories submitted approximately $227 million in fraudulent claims over six months, with Medicare paying out about $136 million.
paras.zh: 这些实验室在六个月内提交了约 2.27 亿美元的欺诈索赔，其中医疗保险支付了约 1.36 亿美元。

paras.en: To conceal the scheme, Kablazada and his associates moved money through overseas transfers and unlicensed financial intermediaries.
paras.zh: 为了掩盖这一计划，卡布拉扎达和他的同伙通过海外转账和未经许可的金融中介机构转移资金。

paras.en: Some of the money was used to purchase luxury vehicles, according to the Justice Department.
paras.zh: 据司法部称，其中一些钱被用来购买豪华车。

paras.en: As part of his plea agreement, Kablazada agreed to forfeit more than $46 million seized by federal investigators from 10 bank accounts.
paras.zh: 作为认罪协议的一部分，卡布拉扎达同意没收联邦调查人员从 10 个银行账户中扣押的超过 4600 万美元。

articles.title: Paul Anthony Kelly grateful Ryan Murphy cast him as Satan after JFK Jr.

paras.en: NEW YORK, Oct. 30 (UPI) -- Paul Anthony Kelly says he was grateful writer-producer Ryan Murphy cast him as Satan in American Horror Story: 13 after giving him the role of John F. Kennedy Jr. in Love Story.
paras.zh: 纽约，10 月 30 日（合众国际社）——保罗·安东尼·凯利表示，他很感谢编剧兼制片人瑞恩·墨菲在《爱情故事》中让他扮演小约翰·肯尼迪一角后，让他在《美国恐怖故事：13》中扮演撒旦。

paras.en: "It was definitely a wild ride, for sure," Kelly, 38, told UPI in a Zoom interview this week.
paras.zh: “这确实是一次疯狂的旅程，”38 岁的凯利本周在 Zoom 采访中告诉合众国际社。

paras.en: "Playing JFK Jr. in Love Story was very much within the box. Playing a historical figure has to be historically accurate and there were a few things that I lent myself to. I definitely took it and tried to make it my own," he recalled.
paras.zh: “在《爱情故事》中扮演小肯尼迪是非常有条理的。扮演一个历史人物必须符合历史，有一些事情是我自己做的。我确实接受了它，并试图把它变成我自己的，”他回忆道。

paras.en: "But, then, being cast in Horror Story as Satan, essentially, it couldn't be more opposite and, then, there is no box to play within. It was very free rain, which I think was a wonderful acting exercise and character-building exercise and I got to work with absolute legends within the craft -- Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson, John Waters. The list is so long, so I'm very, very grateful and very fortunate to be in that position."
paras.zh: “但是，在《恐怖故事》中扮演撒旦，从本质上来说，它是非常对立的，然后，没有任何盒子可以玩。那是一场非常自由的雨，我认为这是一次很棒的表演练习和角色塑造练习，我必须与业内绝对的传奇人物一起工作——杰西卡·兰格、莎拉·保尔森、约翰·沃特斯。名单很长，所以我非常非常感激，非常幸运能够担任这个职位。”

paras.en: Kelly plays his handsome devil with a realism that makes him all the more dangerous since people naturally gravitate to him.
paras.zh: 凯利以现实主义的方式扮演他英俊的魔鬼，这使他变得更加危险，因为人们自然而然地被他吸引。

paras.en: "He was written as this charming, charismatic, but devilish individual. So, I really kind of tried to stay in that realm of old Hollywood, old money," he explained. "Compassion from an evil individual can almost be the scariest thing."
paras.zh: “他被写成一个迷人的、有魅力的，但邪恶的人。所以，我真的试图留在老好莱坞、老钱的王国里，”他解释道。 “来自邪恶之人的同情几乎是最可怕的事情。”

paras.en: This season of the anthology series wrapped up Thursday night with a coven of New Orleans witches, including ones played by Lange and Paulson, defeating Satan and banishing him to spend eternity in Leonardo da Vinci's painting, "The Last Supper."
paras.zh: 本季选集系列于周四晚上结束，在列奥纳多·达·芬奇的画作《最后的晚餐》中，一群新奥尔良女巫（包括兰格和保尔森扮演的女巫）击败了撒旦并将其驱逐到永恒。

paras.en: "It really was a fitting end. I think it was very, almost full-circle and certainly the way that humanity sees him. Now he's imprisoned within 'The Last Supper' as Judas the thirteenth -- there's so many thirteens in this show -- guest," Kelly said.
paras.zh: “这确实是一个合适的结局。我认为这几乎是一个圆满的结局，当然也是人类看待他的方式。现在他被囚禁在《最后的晚餐》中，作为第十三代犹大——这部剧中有很多十三个人——客串，”凯利说。

paras.en: "He's the traitor, so, it's kind of ironic, but I think very valid to be imprisoned within that position in the painting, but who knows if he's imprisoned for long."
paras.zh: “他是叛徒，所以，这有点讽刺，但我认为被囚禁在画中的那个位置是很合理的，但谁知道他是否会被囚禁很长时间。”

paras.en: Waters played Mr. Phibes, Satan's minion whom he beheads in the season finale.
paras.zh: 沃特斯扮演菲比斯先生，他是撒旦的爪牙，在本季大结局中被他斩首。

paras.en: "I was so spoiled in this season to work with absolute legends. But, john was just something else. He and I had a lot of fun on set. He's just such kooky fun."
paras.zh: “这一季我被宠坏了，能和绝对的传奇人物一起工作。但是，约翰就是另外一回事。他和我在片场玩得很开心。他真是太有趣了。”

paras.en: As for having to kill Mr. Phibes? Kelly was thrilled.
paras.zh: 至于必须杀死菲比斯先生？凯利很兴奋。

paras.en: "It's cool. I got to kill John Waters. A lot of the stuff I got to do within the show, I was like, 'Wow, this is incredible that I'm allowed to do this,'" he said. "I took a photo with [the head] before we chopped it off and picked it off the ground. But it's uncanny, the prosthetics that they used on this show and all of the effects were just top-notch."
paras.zh: “这很酷。我必须杀死约翰·沃特斯。我在剧中要做的很多事情，我当时想，‘哇，我被允许这样做真是难以置信，’”他说。 “我和[头部]拍了一张照片，然后我们把它砍下来，把它从地上捡起来。但不可思议的是，他们在这个节目中使用的假肢和所有效果都是一流的。”

paras.en: Kelly is already working on his next project -- The Housemaid's Secret -- the sequel to 2025's hit thriller, The Housemaid, which is based on Freida McFadden's best-selling novel.
paras.zh: 凯利已经开始着手他的下一个项目——《女仆的秘密》——2025 年热门惊悚片《女仆》的续集，该片改编自芙蕾达·麦克法登的畅销小说。

paras.en: "The first one was such a hit and so fun. I mean, the moment that he locks the door, it's just like, 'Oh, boy, it's going down,'" the actor said, noting he is excited to work with director Paul Feig.
paras.zh: “第一部非常受欢迎，也很有趣。我的意思是，当他锁上门的那一刻，就像是，‘哦，天哪，它正在下降，’”这位演员说，并指出他很高兴能与导演保罗·费格合作。

paras.en: "To be a part of the second one, is such an honor and it's so much fun and my character is not who you think he is. And, then, I get to play with Sydney Sweeney and Kirsten Dunst," he added.
paras.zh: “能够成为第二部的一部分，是一种荣幸，也很有趣，我的角色不是你想象的那样。然后，我可以和西德尼·斯威尼和克尔斯滕·邓斯特一起玩，”他补充道。

paras.en: "Michele Morrone is back. Stephen Kalyn's in it. Brittany Snow, I work with. She's phenomenal. It's really just a great script, great working experience. I think it's going to be a really fun, fantastic film."
paras.zh: “米歇尔·莫罗尼回来了。史蒂芬·卡林也在其中。布列塔尼·斯诺，我和她一起工作。她非常出色。这真的是一个很棒的剧本，很棒的工作经验。我认为这将是一部非常有趣、精彩的电影。”

paras.zh: NCAA 橄榄球赛以名人出镜而闻名，因此很可能会有许多著名男女演员和唱片艺术家出席。过去曾出现在比赛中的艺术家包括 Bulldogs 球迷 André 3000 和 Outkast 的 Big Boi、Samuel L. Jackson、Quavo、Luke Bryan 等。
