articles.title: What’s the scariest thing in the universe?

paras.en: Ah, autumn. Leaves are falling, days are shortening, and there’s a chill in the air.
paras.zh: 啊，秋天。树叶纷纷落下，白天日渐缩短，空气中弥漫着寒意。

paras.en: But is that just a result of the approaching winter as Earth’s northern axis begins to tip away from the sun? Or is it caused by some other cosmic horror, a cold finger of dread running down your spine as you contemplate the legion of nightmares lurking in the universe all around us?
paras.zh: 但这仅仅是冬季即将来临、地球北轴开始偏离太阳的结果吗？或者是由其他宇宙恐怖引起的，当你思考潜伏在我们周围宇宙中的大量噩梦时，恐惧的冰冷手指顺着你的脊椎流下来？

paras.en: Space is a scary place. Certainly, many objects in it appear scary to our human brains, and we interpret their shapes as witches and skulls and fiery jack-o’-lanterns. These are in reality relatively harmless illusions whose specific structures only remind us of dreaded visions.
paras.zh: 太空是一个可怕的地方。当然，其中的许多物体对我们人类的大脑来说似乎很可怕，我们将它们的形状解释为女巫、头骨和火热的南瓜灯。这些实际上是相对无害的幻觉，其特定结构只会让我们想起可怕的幻象。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: But there are actual terrifying objects in space, entities operating on a scale that crush our minds and reduce our human experience to a mote of dust floating in the dark.
paras.zh: 但太空中确实存在一些可怕的物体，这些实体的运作规模足以摧毁我们的思想，并将我们的人类经验简化为漂浮在黑暗中的一粒尘埃。

paras.en: I’m an astronomer, and I’ve studied and written about many of these objects for decades. What, you might wonder, in that vast cosmos, scares me?
paras.zh: 我是一名天文学家，几十年来我研究并撰写了许多此类物体的文章。你可能想知道，在那浩瀚的宇宙中，什么让我害怕？

paras.en: (But first, an aside: While cosmophobia—the dread of space—is not an officially recognized medical condition, I know some folks for whom this is a very real fear. I by no means am trying to enflame anyone’s actual terror, so let me state clearly: while real, the objects and events below are either so far away from us that even the most powerful has less effect on us than a whisper in a hurricane or are so rare that the odds of them occurring in a human lifetime—or even over eons—is so small as to be essentially zero. After all, how many people whom you know have been killed by a supermassive black hole merger?)
paras.zh: （但首先，顺便说一句：虽然宇宙恐惧症——对太空的恐惧——并不是一种官方认可的医学病症，但我知道对一些人来说，这是一种非常真实的恐惧。我绝不是试图激起任何人真正的恐惧，所以让我明确地说：虽然真实，下面的物体和事件要么离我们太远，以至于即使是最强大的对我们的影响也比飓风中的低语要小，要么太罕见，以至于它们在人的一生中发生的可能性——甚至超过毕竟，你认识的人中有多少人因超大质量黑洞合并而丧生？）

paras.en: So here, let me show you what gives me a preternatural frisson down my back.
paras.zh: 所以在这里，让我向你展示是什么让我的背部感到异常颤抖。

paras.en: Even the tiniest of stars is humbling on a human scale. TRAPPIST-1, an ultracool red dwarf barely massive enough to ignite nuclear fusion in its core, still releases the equivalent energy as the detonation of more than 50 million one-megaton nuclear bombs every second.
paras.zh: 即使是最小的恒星，在人类的尺度上也显得卑微。 TRAPPIST-1 是一颗超冷红矮星，其质量勉强足以在其核心引发核聚变，但它每秒释放的能量仍相当于超过 5000 万枚百万吨级核弹的爆炸能量。

paras.en: These are called Wolf-Rayet stars, and they’re so massive that the pressures and temperatures in their cores are almost beyond comprehension. They fuse hydrogen and helium into heavier elements at such fantastic rates that they blow out truly soul-searing amounts of energy.
paras.zh: 这些被称为沃尔夫-拉叶星，它们的质量如此之大，以至于其核心的压力和温度几乎难以理解。它们以惊人的速度将氢和氦融合成更重的元素，从而释放出真正灼烧灵魂的能量。

paras.en: R136a1 is just such a star, the most massive star known, at several hundred times the sun’s bulk. It is something like seven million times more luminous than the sun, a number that leaves me somewhat mentally paralyzed. Replace our sun with R136a1, and I fear Earth wouldn’t last long as a solid object. Happily, the star is actually in another galaxy, so distant it’s not even visible to the naked eye. And while there are many Wolf-Rayet stars in our own Milky Way galaxy, they are all still too far to damage us and in fact are fun to study, producing spectacular and gorgeous displays as they live—dangerously.
paras.zh: R136a1 就是这样一颗恒星，它是已知质量最大的恒星，质量是太阳的数百倍。它的亮度大约是太阳的七百万倍，这个数字让我有点精神瘫痪。用 R136a1 取代我们的太阳，我担心地球作为固体物体不会持续太久。令人高兴的是，这颗恒星实际上位于另一个星系，距离很远，甚至肉眼都看不见。尽管我们的银河系中有许多沃尔夫-拉叶星，但它们距离我们仍然太远，无法对我们造成伤害，而且事实上，研究它们很有趣，它们在危险的状态下会产生壮观而华丽的展示。

paras.en: Neutron stars are boggling objects all by themselves. A neutron star is the leftover core of a massive star that exploded as a supernova, and its every property reads like a comic book headline. Containing the mass of a star squeezed down into a ball the size of a city, they are so dense a single cubic centimeter weighs several hundred million tons, equivalent to all the cars in the U.S. compressed down to the size of a sugar cube. The gravity on the surface can be several billion times Earth’s, and a typical neutron star’s magnetic field is billions of times stronger than Earth’s as well.
paras.zh: 中子星本身就是令人难以置信的物体。中子星是一颗大质量恒星作为超新星爆炸后剩下的核心，它的每一个属性读起来就像漫画书的标题。它们含有一颗恒星的质量，被压缩成一个城市大小的球体，密度非常大，一立方厘米重达数亿吨，相当于美国所有汽车被压缩到方糖大小。表面的重力可能是地球的数十亿倍，典型的中子星的磁场也比地球强数十亿倍。

paras.en: But there is a subclass of neutron stars that are more powerful yet: the aptly-named magnetars, with magnetic fields that can be more than a quadrillion times stronger than that of our own planet. Their magnetic field is tied to their crusts, the thin shell of “normal” matter surrounding the more exotic interior. If there is a starquake, a sudden shift in the neutron star crust, the magnetic field gets shaken violently. This creates a truly enormous explosion of energy that barrels into the galaxy at large like a tsunami.
paras.zh: 但中子星的一个子类却更强大：名副其实的磁星，其磁场可能比我们星球的磁场强四亿倍以上。它们的磁场与地壳有关，地壳是“正常”物质的薄壳，包围着更奇特的内部。如果发生星震，中子星地壳突然发生移动，磁场就会剧烈震动。这会产生真正巨大的能量爆炸，像海啸一样冲入整个星系。

paras.en: In December 2004 such a wave swept over Earth, causing some havoc. It hit with such force that it compressed our planet’s magnetosphere, overloaded satellites and even partially ionized our atmosphere. While the damage was minor, this was all caused by the magnetar SGR 1806-20, which is 50,000 light-years away, halfway across our galaxy.
paras.zh: 2004年12月，这样的波浪席卷了地球，造成了一些破坏。它的撞击力如此之大，以至于压缩了我们星球的磁层，使卫星超载，甚至部分电离了我们的大气层。虽然损害很小，但这都是由磁星 SGR 1806-20 造成的，它距离我们 50,000 光年，横跨我们银河系的一半。

paras.en: Happily, magnetars are rare, and only a few known are closer to us, all less powerful than SGR 1806-20. I’d hate to think there’s another one like it out there but nearer to us, just waiting to blow off some magnetic steam.
paras.zh: 令人高兴的是，磁星很罕见，只有少数已知的磁星距离我们较近，它们的威力均不如 SGR 1806-20。我不愿想象还有另一个类似的东西存在，但离我们更近，只是等待释放一些磁力蒸汽。

paras.en: Speaking of neutron stars, if one can be a problem, what happens if there are two of them orbiting each other?
paras.zh: 说到中子星，如果其中一颗可能成为问题，那么如果其中两颗相互绕转会发生什么？

paras.en: Over time, the orbit of the pair can decay, the duo slowly approaching one another. Eventually the inevitability of gravity brings them close enough to suddenly merge, sending out a tremendous blast of matter and energy that can outshine the sun by a factor of many billions, though just for the briefest fraction of a second. Because of the high-energy photons they fling out and their milliseconds-long duration, these are called short gamma-ray bursts.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，两人的轨道会衰减，两人慢慢地相互接近。最终，引力不可避免地使它们足够接近，突然合并，发出巨大的物质和能量爆炸，其亮度可以比太阳高出数十亿倍，尽管只是在最短的一秒钟内。由于它们发射出高能光子且持续时间长达毫秒，因此被称为短伽马射线暴。

paras.en: Such explosions are rare because binary neutron stars are rare. While no burst has ever been seen in our galaxy, a handful of local binary systems are known. The good news is they’re likely too far away to damage us in the eventuality of their merging. Those don’t concern me.
paras.zh: 这种爆炸很少见，因为双中子星很罕见。虽然我们的银河系从未见过爆发，但已知有一些本地双星系统。好消息是，它们可能距离太远，无法在它们合并时对我们造成伤害。那些与我无关。

paras.en: What does, however, is the possibility of a pair of neutron stars much closer to us, hidden from our view because of their extreme age, cooling over the eons until they are cold enough to be invisible to our telescopes. Massive, dark and in a mad whirl around each other, they will announce their demise in an eruption of energy powerful enough to dwarf the effects of a magnetar.
paras.zh: 然而，真正重要的是，有可能存在一对距离我们更近的中子星，它们由于年龄极大而隐藏在我们的视野之外，经过亿万年的冷却，直到它们冷到足以被我们的望远镜看不见。它们巨大、黑暗，相互疯狂旋转，它们将在爆发的能量中宣告它们的灭亡，其强度足以使磁星的影响相形见绌。

paras.en: The odds of this are extremely low, so I don’t think there are any that close. I’m pretty sure. Probably.
paras.zh: 这种可能性非常低，所以我认为没有那么接近。我很确定。大概。

paras.en: But if I had to pick one thing out of the cosmic menagerie that gives me astronomical heebie-jeebies, it’s merging supermassive black holes.
paras.zh: 但如果我必须从宇宙动物园中选出一件让我感到天文惊慌的东西，那就是超大质量黑洞的合并。

paras.en: These are black holes on a galactic scale, with millions or billions of times the mass of the sun. They can come in pairs, coupled after two galaxies collide, the monsters in their hearts brought together in the merger. Over billions of years, they slide ever closer together until finally they eat each other to form a single, even more Brobdingnagian beast.
paras.zh: 这些是银河系规模的黑洞，质量是太阳的数百万或数十亿倍。他们可以成对出现，两个星系碰撞后耦合在一起，他们心中的怪物在合并中聚集在一起。数十亿年来，它们的距离越来越近，直到最后它们互相吞噬，形成一个更加庞大的巨兽。

paras.en: But not all their mass gets glommed together to form the final black hole boss. Instead a significant fraction is converted into energy in the form of gravitational waves, a literal shaking of the fabric of the universe, sending out incomprehensibly powerful ripples like an angry god shaking the crumbs off an Olympian tablecloth.
paras.zh: 但并不是所有的质量都聚集在一起形成最终的黑洞老板。相反，很大一部分以引力波的形式转化为能量，宇宙结构的真正震动，发出难以理解的强大涟漪，就像愤怒的神抖掉奥林匹亚桌布上的面包屑一样。

paras.en: How powerful? The merger’s gravitational roar in a fraction of second is equivalent to the amount of energy our sun emits in over a billion trillion years. It’s more powerful than the combined might of every single star in the observable universe.
paras.zh: 有多强大？这次合并在几分之一秒内产生的引力轰鸣相当于太阳在超过十亿万亿年中释放的能量。它比可观测宇宙中每一颗恒星的力量总和还要强大。

paras.en: Amazingly, the explosion is entirely dark; not a single photon of light is generated—all the energy goes into invisible gravitational waves. Also, these happen, on average, billions of light-years from us, so the energy is dissipated to far less than that of the beat of a bat’s wing on Earth. The gravitational burst is immense, but the vast distance between us wins.
paras.zh: 令人惊奇的是，爆炸时一片漆黑。没有产生任何一个光子——所有的能量都变成了看不见的引力波。此外，这些事件平均发生在距离我们数十亿光年的地方，因此能量消散的程度远低于地球上蝙蝠翅膀拍动的能量。引力爆发是巨大的，但我们之间的巨大距离获胜。

paras.en: Still, the very idea of such a thing freezes my brain, locking it into a mental feedback loop that’s the equivalent of running around in a tight circle flapping my arms wildly and screaming. Nothing should be that energetic. Nothing. Yet, as far as we know, the universe makes these all the time.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，这种事情的想法还是冻结了我的大脑，将其锁定在一个心理反馈循环中，这相当于在一个紧密的圈子里跑来跑去，疯狂地拍打我的手臂并尖叫。没有什么应该那么充满活力。没有什么。然而，据我们所知，宇宙一直在制造这些。

paras.en: So as you go trick-or-treating this holiday, be safe. Watch out for traffic and other costumed celebrants—but also keep a part of your attention on the sky. It’s pretty scary up there, too.
paras.zh: 所以，当你在这个假期玩“不给糖就捣蛋”的游戏时，一定要注意安全。留意交通和其他盛装庆祝者，但也要将一部分注意力集中在天空上。那里也很可怕。

articles.title: The world’s biggest cities are sinking. Is yours one of them?

paras.en: Major cities across the world—including hotspots such as New Orleans, Mexico City, Jakarta and Rome—are sinking by up to several inches every year.
paras.zh: 世界各地的主要城市，包括新奥尔良、墨西哥城、雅加达和罗马等热点地区，每年都会下沉数英寸。

paras.en: Those are the findings of an exhaustive new survey published in Nature Cities, in which researchers used satellite radar to track 465 urban areas of more than a million people from 2014 to 2023. The results, displayed in an interactive map, shows that sinking isn’t just “a local curiosity” for a small handful of cities, but “a global urban problem,” says study coauthor Guoquan Wang, a geophysicist at the University of Houston.
paras.zh: 这些是《自然城市》杂志上发表的一项详尽的新调查的结果，其中研究人员使用卫星雷达跟踪了 2014 年至 2023 年人口超过 100 万的 465 个城市地区。结果显示在交互式地图上，表明下沉不仅是少数城市的“当地好奇心”，而且是“全球城市问题”，该研究的合著者、休斯敦大学地球物理学家王国权说。

paras.en: Satellites can measure the land’s gradual sinking, called subsidence, by taking radar images of the same area over time to determine the shift in the radar signal’s travel—even a change of mere millimeters (twenty-fifths of an inch) of ground can result in a signal taking slightly longer to return than the past. The new work, which examined small chunks of land—just a few houses wide—all over the world, is “the most comprehensive and systematic exploration of subsidence in urban cities,” says Roland Bürgmann, a geophysicist at the University of California, Berkeley, who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: 卫星可以测量陆地逐渐下沉（称为沉降）的情况，方法是拍摄同一区域随时间变化的雷达图像，以确定雷达信号传播的变化——即使地面仅发生毫米（二十分之一英寸）的变化，也可能导致信号返回的时间比过去稍长。加州大学伯克利分校地球物理学家罗兰·布尔格曼（Roland Bürgmann）并未参与这项研究，他说，这项新研究研究了世界各地的小块土地（只有几栋房子那么宽），是“对城市沉降最全面、最系统的探索”。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Sinking was most severe in Southeast Asia, West and Central Asia and North America, but it also turned up in South America and Africa, both of which are generally less studied in regards to land subsidence; For almost half the cities in the dataset, no satellite radar study had ever been done before.
paras.zh: 东南亚、西亚、中亚和北美的下沉最为严重，但南美洲和非洲也出现了下沉现象，而这两个国家对地面沉降的研究普遍较少；对于数据集中几乎一半的城市，以前从未进行过卫星雷达研究。

paras.en: Different factors can contribute to urban subsidence. In New York City, for instance, the weight of buildings compresses the region’s soft soils. But the biggest driver is usually water utilities, industries and other groups pumping out water from under the ground. Groundwater helps hold up the soil like air in a cushion: pump it out, and the ground slowly sags.
paras.zh: 不同的因素会导致城市沉降。例如，在纽约市，建筑物的重量压缩了该地区的软土。但最大的推动因素通常是自来水公司、工业和其他从地下抽水的团体。地下水有助于支撑土壤，就像垫子中的空气一样：将其抽出，地面就会慢慢下陷。

paras.en: And the real danger is uneven sinking. “If the whole city were to smoothly subside altogether by an inch or so, it wouldn’t be that big of a problem,” Bürgmann says. But when one neighborhood drops faster than the next, the strain builds.
paras.zh: 真正的危险是不均匀下沉。 “如果整个城市平稳地完全沉降一英寸左右，那就不是什么大问题了，”布尔格曼说。但当一个社区的下降速度快于另一个社区时，压力就会加剧。

paras.en: Over time such strain can crack foundations, break sewer lines, damage subway systems and worsen flooding. In Jakarta, the sinking and flooding has become so severe that Indonesia is building a brand-new capital city on the island of Borneo.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，这种压力可能会导致地基破裂、下水道管道破裂、地铁系统受损并加剧洪水泛滥。在雅加达，下沉和洪水变得如此严重，以至于印度尼西亚正在婆罗洲岛上建造一座全新的首都。

paras.en: Once it happens, sinking is “cumulative and largely irreversible,” Wang says, but cities have successfully stopped continued subsidence before. Tokyo once sank “way faster than many cities today,” says Manoochehr Shirzaei, a geoscientist at Virginia Tech, who was a peer reviewer for the study, until officials drew up policies to halt it. These included regulations around groundwater pumping and a shift toward alternative surface water sources. In China, Beijing and the nearby city of Tianjin “stopped pumping groundwater and replaced it with surface water” piped from the Yangtze River basin, Wang says, and sinking has since halted in parts of the region.
paras.zh: 王说，一旦发生，下沉是“累积的并且基本上是不可逆转的”，但城市之前已经成功地阻止了持续的下沉。弗吉尼亚理工大学的地球科学家、该研究的同行评审员 Manoochehr Shirzaei 表示，东京曾经的下沉速度“比今天的许多城市都要快”，直到官员们制定了政策来阻止东京的下沉。其中包括有关地下水抽水和转向替代地表水源的法规。王说，在中国，北京和附近的天津市“停止抽取地下水，并用从长江流域输送的地表水取而代之”，此后该地区部分地区的下沉已经停止。

paras.en: “In most places, we have plenty of time to react,” Shirzaei says, “but we have to do it.”
paras.zh: “在大多数地方，我们有足够的时间做出反应，”希尔扎伊说，“但我们必须这样做。”

articles.title: Math Puzzle: Mysterious pyramid

paras.en: The nine cells of the triangle contain nine zeros. Try to change the numbers, with any number of moves, so that they become nine consecutive positive integers, the smallest of which is a. The arrangement of these nine numbers in the triangle is irrelevant. A move is the increase or decrease by 1 of the two numbers occupying two adjacent cells, where adjacent cells share a side. For which values of a is the problem solvable?
paras.zh: 三角形的九个方格包含九个零。尝试用任意次数的移动来改变数字，使它们成为九个连续的正整数，其中最小的是a。这九个数字在三角形中的排列是无关紧要的。移动是指占据两个相邻单元格的两个数字增加或减少 1，其中相邻单元格共享一条边。对于哪些 a 值，问题可以解决？

paras.en: A pair of adjacent cells always consists of one orange and one black triangle. Initially, the sum r of the numbers on the orange cells is equal to the sum b of the numbers on the black cells, namely, 0. A move does not change this equilibrium r = b. At the end, the nine numbers of the triangle should be a , a + 1, ..., and a + 8. Thus, because b is the sum of six of the numbers, b ≥ a + (a + 1) + (a + 2) + (a + 3) + (a + 4) + (a + 5) = 6a + 15, and because r is the sum of three of the numbers, r ≤ (a + 6) + (a + 7) + (a + 8) = 3a + 21. Because b = r, 6a + 15 ≤ 3a + 21, or a ≤ 2. Furthermore, r = b means that r + b = 2r, so r + b must be an even number. For a = 1, the sum of the nine numbers 1 + 2 + ... + 9 = 45, which is odd. Therefore, if there is a solution to the problem at all, it is only for a = 2.
paras.zh: 一对相邻的单元格总是由一个橙色和一个黑色三角形组成。最初，橙色方格上的数字之和 r 等于黑色方格上的数字之和 b，即 0。移动不会改变这种平衡 r = b。最后，三角形的九个数字应该是 a 、 a + 1、...、a + 8。因此，因为 b 是六个数字的和，所以 b ≥ a + (a + 1) + (a + 2) + (a + 3) + (a + 4) + (a + 5) = 6a + 15，并且因为 r 是三个数字的和，所以 r ≤ (a + 6) + (a + 7) + (a + 8) = 3a + 21。因为 b = r，所以 6a + 15 ≤ 3a + 21，或 a ≤ 2。此外，r = b 意味着 r + b = 2r，所以 r + b 必须是偶数。对于 a = 1，九个数 1 + 2 + ... + 9 = 45 之和是奇数。因此，如果问题有解的话，也只是针对a = 2。

paras.en: Instead of increasing the numbers on the same pair of cells by 1 n times, one can directly increase both numbers by n. This does not change the problem in any way. The order of the individual moves also plays no role. The image shows in three steps that there is indeed a solution for a = 2.
paras.zh: 无需将同一对单元上的数字增加 1 n 倍，而是可以直接将两个数字都增加 n 倍。这不会以任何方式改变问题。各个动作的顺序也不起作用。该图分三步显示，确实存在 a = 2 的解。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: We’d love to hear from you! E-mail us at games@sciam.com to share your experience.
paras.zh: 我们很乐意听取您的意见！请发送电子邮件至 games@sciam.com 与我们分享您的经验。

paras.en: This puzzle originally appeared in Spektrum der Wissenschaft and was reproduced with permission. It was translated from the original German version with the assistance of artificial intelligence and reviewed by our editors.
paras.zh: 该谜题最初出现在 Spektrum der Wissenschaft 中，经许可转载。它是在人工智能的帮助下从德语原文翻译而来，并由我们的编辑审阅。

articles.title: Why do flamingos dance while they eat? This scientist found out
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: On a family trip to Atlanta, Víctor Ortega Jiménez spent time taking pictures and videos of flamingos as they fed in their pond. It wasn’t to admire their long legs or flamboyant pink color. Instead, he noticed the “beautiful” ripples spreading across the water as the birds ate under the surface. But he didn’t know why the waves were happening.
paras.zh: 在一次前往亚特兰大的家庭旅行中，维克多·奥尔特加·希门尼斯 (Víctor Ortega Jiménez) 花时间拍摄了火烈鸟在池塘里进食的照片和视频。这并不是为了欣赏他们的长腿或艳丽的粉色。相反，他注意到当鸟类在水面下进食时，“美丽”的涟漪在水面上蔓延。但他不知道为什么会出现波浪。

paras.en: It took “more than four years to answer that question,” says Ortega Jiménez, of the University of California, Berkeley. “But I think the answer was fascinating.”
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的奥尔特加·希门尼斯说，“花了四年多的时间才回答这个问题”。 “但我认为答案很有趣。”

paras.en: Ortega Jiménez’s focus is biomechanics, or the study of how mechanics applies to animal movement and structure. His goal is to understand how animal behaviors might lead to human-made engineering feats.
paras.zh: 奥尔特加·希门尼斯的研究重点是生物力学，即研究力学如何应用于动物运动和结构。他的目标是了解动物行为如何导致人造工程壮举。

paras.en: He discovered that, by retracting their heads, flamingos produce vortexlike traps with water to scoop up algae. They stomp around — or dance, if you will — amplifying the vortex. The series of motions brings the food to their crooked beaks. The beaks then filter in food, releasing silt and mud.
paras.zh: 他发现，通过缩回头部，火烈鸟会用水产生漩涡状的陷阱来舀起藻类。他们跺脚——或者跳舞，如果你愿意的话——放大了漩涡。这一系列动作将食物送到它们弯曲的嘴里。然后喙过滤食物，释放淤泥和泥土。

paras.en: The impressive process can weed out particles the size of a single cell. This kind of self-cleaning filter for extremely small particles can be applied to remove microplastics and so-called forever chemicals called PFAS from water, Ortega Jiménez says.
paras.zh: 这个令人印象深刻的过程可以清除单个细胞大小的颗粒。 Ortega Jiménez 表示，这种针对极小颗粒的自清洁过滤器可用于去除水中的微塑料和所谓的永久化学物质 PFAS。

paras.en: “Nature is always full of secrets,” he says. “And I think that’s the riddle that keeps me going, trying to understand nature. That’s my way to see science: by observation and trying to be inspired and trying to solve a problem.”
paras.zh: “大自然总是充满秘密，”他说。 “我认为这就是让我继续前进、努力理解自然的谜团。这就是我看待科学的方式：通过观察、试图受到启发并试图解决问题。”

articles.title: Three-quarters of NFL football players may end up with CTE
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: An estimated three-quarters of NFL players who died in a 16-year period had the devastating neurogenerative disease called CTE.
paras.zh: 据估计，在 16 年内死亡的 NFL 球员中有四分之三患有名为 CTE 的破坏性神经再生疾病。

paras.en: Back in 2017, researchers reported that an estimated 99 percent of former NFL players developed CTE, or chronic traumatic encephalopathy, from an analysis of donated brains. But the families who provided the donations may have done so because their football-playing relatives had symptoms related to CTE, which could skew the results. A new study, which accounts for this potential bias, estimates that nearly 75 percent of former NFL players have CTE at death. It’s the first population-level estimate for NFL players, researchers report October 28 in JAMA Network Open.
paras.zh: 早在 2017 年，研究人员就报告称，根据对捐赠大脑的分析，估计 99% 的前 NFL 球员患有 CTE（慢性创伤性脑病）。但提供捐款的家庭可能这样做是因为他们踢足球的亲戚有与 CTE 相关的症状，这可能会扭曲结果。一项新的研究解释了这种潜在的偏差，估计近 75% 的前 NFL 球员在死亡时患有 CTE。研究人员于 10 月 28 日在 JAMA Network Open 上报告称，这是对 NFL 球员的首次人口水平估计。

paras.en: The development of CTE is linked to repeated blows to the head over time. The disease can occur in people who play contact sports, experience intimate partner violence or engage in military combat. A study of American football players suggests that the longer the duration of repeated head trauma, the higher the risk of CTE and the more severe the condition. During life, people who are later diagnosed with CTE can experience symptoms including memory issues, difficulty concentrating, depression and poor impulse control.
paras.zh: CTE 的发生与头部反复受到打击有关。这种疾病可能发生在从事接触性运动、遭受亲密伴侣暴力或参加军事战斗的人身上。一项针对美国橄榄球运动员的研究表明，反复头部外伤的持续时间越长，发生 CTE 的风险就越高，病情也越严重。在生活中，后来被诊断出患有 CTE 的人可能会出现记忆问题、注意力难以集中、抑郁和冲动控制能力差等症状。

paras.en: A brain protein called tau, which usually helps nerve cells communicate and performs other jobs, goes awry in CTE. Brains with the disease are snarled with irregular, damaging clumps of the protein. The condition is diagnosed after death, during an autopsy, and has been identified most frequently among American football players.
paras.zh: 一种名为 tau 的大脑蛋白通常帮助神经细胞沟通并执行其他工作，但在 CTE 中却出现了问题。患有这种疾病的大脑中充满了不规则的、具有破坏性的蛋白质团块。这种情况是在死后尸检过程中被诊断出来的，并且在美国橄榄球运动员中最常见。

paras.en: The new study, by a Boston University research team, included all previous NFL players who passed away from January 2008 through December 2023. The more than 2,300 players included almost 400 with samples in the university’s UNITE Brain Bank, with the remainder identified from records in the U.S. National Death Index. The research team determined that families of NFL players who had CTE-related symptoms in life were five times more likely to donate their relative’s brain than families whose relative did not experience symptoms. Taking that into consideration, the team landed on a population-level CTE estimate for NFL players of 74.5 percent.
paras.zh: 波士顿大学研究小组进行的这项新研究涵盖了 2008 年 1 月至 2023 年 12 月期间去世的所有 NFL 球员。这 2,300 多名球员中包括近 400 名球员，样本保存在该大学的 UNITE 脑库中，其余的则从美国国家死亡指数的记录中确定。研究小组确定，在生活中出现 CTE 相关症状的 NFL 球员的家庭捐献其亲属大脑的可能性是其亲属没有出现症状的家庭的五倍。考虑到这一点，该团队对 NFL 球员的人口水平 CTE 估计为 74.5%。

paras.en: The research team notes that determining the true prevalence of CTE is important to understanding the public health impact of the disease.
paras.zh: 研究小组指出，确定 CTE 的真实患病率对于了解该疾病对公共健康的影响非常重要。

articles.title: A proof-of-concept test can spot bladder cancer in urine
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: A splash of pee could reveal bladder cancer.
paras.zh: 尿液飞溅可能会发现膀胱癌。

paras.en: Using a proof-of-concept urine test that decodes RNA molecules, it’s possible to pick out patients with the disease, scientists report October 2 in Nature Medicine. Because urine is in direct contact with bladder tumors, it’s “a very attractive fluid” to look for this type of cancer, says Stanford University oncologist Maximilian Diehn. The technology, still in its infancy, offers a glimpse of what future screening tests might entail.
paras.zh: 科学家于 10 月 2 日在《自然·医学》杂志上报告称，使用解码 RNA 分子的概念验证尿液测试，可以挑选出患有这种疾病的患者。斯坦福大学肿瘤学家马克西米利安·迪恩 (Maximilian Diehn) 表示，由于尿液与膀胱肿瘤直接接触，因此它是寻找此类癌症的“非常有吸引力的液体”。这项技术仍处于起步阶段，可以让我们了解未来筛查测试可能需要的内容。

paras.en: Today’s liquid biopsies for cancer, which examine bodily fluids rather than tissue samples, largely focus on finding DNA that tumors shed into the blood. Diehn’s lab sought a different stream of information. The researchers analyzed RNA, DNA’s molecular cousin. RNA isn’t as stable as DNA, so it hasn’t been researchers’ top target. But it carries info that DNA lacks, such as which genes are turned on. That’s important, Diehn says, “because it can tell you what the cancer is doing at any given moment.”
paras.zh: 如今的癌症液体活检主要检查的是体液而不是组织样本，主要侧重于寻找肿瘤脱落到血液中的 DNA。迪恩的实验室寻求不同的信息流。研究人员分析了 DNA 的近亲分子 RNA。 RNA 不如 DNA 稳定，因此它并不是研究人员的首要目标。但它携带 DNA 所缺乏的信息，例如哪些基因被打开。迪恩说，这很重要，“因为它可以告诉你癌症在任何特定时刻正在做什么。”

paras.en: Diehn and his colleagues previously developed a technique to analyze dribs of RNA floating in blood. In samples from people with lung cancer, the team could read RNA signatures of the disease. Now, the researchers have shown that their technique is a whiz at detecting cancer in urine. The team tested their technique using samples from 515 cancer patients and healthy people. It was sensitive enough to identify 95 out of 100 people with bladder cancer — even at early stages of disease. What’s more, the test also offered hints about cancer biology, such as the type of tumor and risk of recurrence. Those details could help doctors make decisions about treatments, Diehn says.
paras.zh: Diehn 和他的同事之前开发了一种技术来分析血液中漂浮的 RNA 颗粒。在肺癌患者的样本中，研究小组可以读取该疾病的 RNA 特征。现在，研究人员已经证明他们的技术在检测尿液中的癌症方面非常出色。该团队使用 515 名癌症患者和健康人的样本测试了他们的技术。它的灵敏度足够高，即使在疾病的早期阶段，也能识别出 100 名膀胱癌患者中的 95 名。此外，该测试还提供了有关癌症生物学的提示，例如肿瘤类型和复发风险。迪恩说，这些细节可以帮助医生做出治疗决定。

paras.en: The researchers are now exploring their technique’s potential for picking up other cancers. Their evidence suggests that it can spot cancer in the kidney and prostate, organs also washed by urine. One day, Diehn says, he can imagine a multi-cancer urine test focused on tumors in the genitourinary tract. But there’s much to do before such a test makes it into clinics.
paras.zh: 研究人员现在正在探索他们的技术检测其他癌症的潜力。他们的证据表明，它可以发现肾脏和前列腺中的癌症，这些器官也被尿液清洗过。迪恩说，有一天，他可以想象一种针对泌尿生殖道肿瘤的多种癌症尿液检测。但在这种测试进入临床之前还有很多工作要做。

paras.en: Because the technology is so new, the jury’s still out on whether RNA-based testing will find use in cancer screening, Diehn says. “But absolutely, I think the field needs to investigate it.”
paras.zh: Diehn 表示，由于这项技术太新，基于 RNA 的检测是否能用于癌症筛查尚无定论。 “但绝对，我认为该领域需要对此进行调查。”

articles.title: Chernobyl's Dogs Are Genetically Different, And We May Finally Know Why
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: The world's worst nuclear disaster didn't only affect humans.
paras.zh: 世界上最严重的核灾难不仅影响人类。

paras.en: When the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant experienced a catastrophic explosion on 26 April 1986, radioactive fallout compelled Soviet authorities to abandon the area, declaring a giant exclusion zone that covered about 2,600 square kilometers (1,000 square miles).
paras.zh: 1986 年 4 月 26 日，切尔诺贝利核电站发生灾难性爆炸，放射性尘埃迫使苏联当局放弃该地区，宣布划定一个占地约 2,600 平方公里（1,000 平方英里）的巨大禁区。

paras.en: Studies have since shown that animals came to thrive in the abandoned Chernobyl Exclusion Zone (CEZ), free from the interference of living human populations.
paras.zh: 此后的研究表明，动物在废弃的切尔诺贝利禁区（CEZ）中繁衍生息，免受人类的干扰。

paras.en: At the time of the evacuation, many residents were forced to leave their pets behind, and 'liquidators' were subsequently sent in to destroy the remaining animals, along with livestock in the contaminated area.
paras.zh: 疏散时，许多居民被迫留下宠物，随后派出“清理者”消灭剩余的动物以及污染地区的牲畜。

paras.en: "It is unclear how many animals were able to evade the liquidators, but enough domestic dogs escaped this fate to establish persistent populations within the zone," researchers explain in a new paper in Genes, led by first author and population geneticist Megan Dillon from North Carolina State University.
paras.zh: 研究人员在《Genes》杂志上发表的一篇新论文中解释道：“目前尚不清楚有多少动物能够逃脱清算者的追捕，但有足够多的家犬逃脱了这种命运，并在该地区建立了持久的种群。”该论文由第一作者、北卡罗来纳州立大学群体遗传学家梅根·狄龙 (Megan Dillon) 领导。

paras.en: "Several hundred dogs are now estimated to inhabit the CEZ and are thought to descend, at least in part, from pets left behind after the disaster."
paras.zh: “现在估计有数百只狗居住在CEZ，并且被认为至少部分是灾难后留下的宠物的后代。”

paras.en: These dogs, now more than 30 canine generations removed from the disaster, offer a unique opportunity to study how decades of contamination might affect living organisms and their evolution.
paras.zh: 这些狗现已从这场灾难中逃脱了 30 多代，为研究数十年的污染可能如何影响生物体及其进化提供了独特的机会。

paras.en: In a study published in 2023, some of the same research team analyzed the dogs, finding that dogs that lived near the site of the abandoned nuclear power plant were genetically distinct from dogs that lived further away, leaving open the possibility that the genetic variations could be the result of mutations caused by lingering radiation.
paras.zh: 在 2023 年发表的一项研究中，同一研究小组的一些成员对这些狗进行了分析，发现生活在废弃核电站附近的狗在基因上与生活在更远的地方的狗不同，这表明基因变异可能是由挥之不去的辐射引起的突变的结果。

paras.en: A follow-up study in 2024 found no evidence that mutations were driving the genetic differentiations, so Dillon and fellow researchers kept investigating, in an attempt to solve the mystery.
paras.zh: 2024 年的一项后续研究没有发现任何证据表明突变正在驱动遗传分化，因此狄龙和其他研究人员继续调查，试图解开这个谜团。

paras.en: "This [new study] ties up some of the loose ends from our previous work, where in characterizing the population's genetic structure we found that while these two dog groups are geographically very close, they have a very high degree of genetic difference, and those differences aren't due to mutation," says Dillon.
paras.zh: “这项新研究解决了我们之前工作中的一些未解决的问题，在描述种群遗传结构的过程中，我们发现虽然这两个狗群在地理上非常接近，但它们具有非常高的遗传差异，而这些差异并不是由于突变造成的，”狄龙说。

paras.en: "With this work we wanted to explore two additional larger-scale evolutionary drivers – are the genetic differences due to selection, or are they due to genetic drift over time in an isolated population?"
paras.zh: “通过这项工作，我们希望探索另外两个更大规模的进化驱动因素——遗传差异是由于选择造成的，还是由于孤立群体中随着时间的推移而发生的遗传漂变？”

paras.en: In the new research, Dillon and team analyzed whole-genome sequence data collected from 106 dogs between 2018 and 2019, including animals from the Nuclear Power Plant (NPP) and from Chornobyl City (the Ukrainian spelling of Chernobyl), approximately 16 kilometers (10 miles) away.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，Dillon 和团队分析了 2018 年至 2019 年间从 106 只狗收集的全基因组序列数据，其中包括来自核电站 (NPP) 和约 16 公里（10 英里）外的切尔诺贝利市（切尔诺贝利的乌克兰语拼写）的动物。

paras.en: If mutations aren't responsible for the genetic differences seen in dogs living at the nuclear plant, natural selection could be an explanation, with existing genetic variants becoming more common if they improve an organism's chances of surviving and reproducing in a particular environment.
paras.zh: 如果突变不是生活在核电站的狗身上所见遗传差异的原因，那么自然选择可能是一种解释，如果现有的遗传变异提高了有机体在特定环境中生存和繁殖的机会，那么它们就会变得更加普遍。

paras.en: Alternatively, it's possible genetic drift could explain the result, in which genetic changes occur at random, not necessarily conferring any survival advantages.
paras.zh: 或者，遗传漂变可能可以解释这一结果，其中遗传变化是随机发生的，不一定会带来任何生存优势。

paras.en: In the case of the dogs living near the nuclear power plant, however, the differentiation doesn't seem to be down to chance alone.
paras.zh: 然而，对于生活在核电站附近的狗来说，这种差异似乎不仅仅是偶然的。

paras.en: The researchers found evidence of changes concentrated in specific genomic regions located near genes associated with cancer, cellular function and maintenance, infectious diseases, and immune response.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现变化的证据集中在位于与癌症、细胞功能和维持、传染病和免疫反应相关的基因附近的特定基因组区域。

paras.en: "While we can't say for certain whether what we've found can be directly confirmed as selection, we do find these genomic signatures suggestive of selection," Dillon says.
paras.zh: “虽然我们不能肯定地说我们的发现是否可以直接证实为选择，但我们确实发现这些基因组特征暗示了选择，”狄龙说。

paras.en: "When we dig deeper into those genomic regions, we find that these genes are involved in biologically relevant pathways that could allow them to overcome the effects of being exposed to toxicants in this environment."
paras.zh: “当我们深入研究这些基因组区域时，我们发现这些基因涉及生物学相关的途径，这些途径可以使它们克服在这种环境中暴露于有毒物质的影响。”

paras.en: We don't know for sure, and it will fall to future research to investigate further, but the researchers think it's plausible that in the wake of the disaster, some dogs may have had existing genetic advantages that protected them from cancer, or gave them better immune responses, or resistance to toxic exposures.
paras.zh: 我们不确定，这将由未来的研究来进一步调查，但研究人员认为，灾难发生后，一些狗可能拥有现有的遗传优势，可以保护它们免受癌症的侵害，或者赋予它们更好的免疫反应或对有毒物质的抵抗力，这是合理的。

paras.en: As time passed, those dogs may have bestowed survival advantages to their offspring, as did each successive generation, in a mode of natural selection called directional selection.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，这些狗可能会通过一种称为定向选择的自然选择模式，赋予它们的后代生存优势，就像每一代人一样。

paras.en: "When we consider the toxic environment around Chornobyl, I can see why most people would think, 'Surely there's got to have been some consequence of living in that environment,'" says geneticist Matthew Breen from North Carolina State University.
paras.zh: “当我们考虑切尔诺贝利周围的有毒环境时，我可以理解为什么大多数人会想，‘生活在那种环境中肯定会产生一些后果’，”北卡罗来纳州立大学的遗传学家马修·布林说。

paras.en: "But what we're saying is the consequence may not have gone as far as changing the dogs' genome in order to adapt, it could be the ones that were able to survive the initial exposures had this level of underlying genetic diversity and variants to offer a higher degree of fitness."
paras.zh: “但我们想说的是，结果可能不会达到改变狗的基因组以适应的程度，它可能是那些能够在最初的暴露中幸存下来的狗，具有这种水平的潜在遗传多样性和变异，以提供更高程度的适应性。”

paras.en: Editor's note: This article selectively uses the spelling "Chernobyl" to reflect the historical context of the 1986 disaster, when Ukraine was part of the Soviet Union and Russian transliterations were widely used. The Ukrainian spelling is "Chornobyl".
paras.zh: 编者注：本文选择性地使用“切尔诺贝利”这个拼写来反映1986年灾难的历史背景，当时乌克兰还是苏联的一部分，俄语音译被广泛使用。乌克兰语的拼写是“切尔诺贝利”。

articles.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Formula Kills Drug-Resistant Cancer Cells in The Lab
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: The most common form of esophageal cancer worldwide is notoriously difficult to treat, in part due to the scourge of drug resistance.
paras.zh: 众所周知，全球最常见的食管癌很难治疗，部分原因是耐药性的祸害。

paras.en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) – which is particularly common in Asia and developing nations – is often treated with the chemotherapy drug cisplatin, but tumors can develop resistance to the medication, making the deadly disease difficult to contain.
paras.zh: 食管鳞状细胞癌（ESCC）在亚洲和发展中国家尤其常见，通常使用化疗药物顺铂进行治疗，但肿瘤会对药物产生耐药性，从而使这种致命的疾病难以控制。

paras.en: "Once resistance develops, patients are more likely to experience reduced responses to subsequent treatment and unfavorable survival outcomes," researchers from Shaoxing University in China write in a new study published in Frontiers in Immunology.
paras.zh: 中国绍兴大学的研究人员在《免疫学前沿》上发表的一项新研究中写道：“一旦出现耐药性，患者更有可能对后续治疗反应减弱，并出现不利的生存结果。”

paras.en: "Deciphering the mechanistic drivers of cisplatin resistance and pioneering novel interventions to counteract it are critical and unmet imperatives for altering the therapeutic landscape for ESCC patients."
paras.zh: “破译顺铂耐药的机制驱动因素并开拓新的干预措施来抵消它对于改变 ESCC 患者的治疗前景至关重要且尚未得到满足。”

paras.en: In their study, the research team examined one such candidate to help us fight back against ESCC – but as far as novel interventions go, it's practically ancient.
paras.zh: 在他们的研究中，研究小组检查了这样一种候选药物，以帮助我们对抗食管鳞癌——但就新颖的干预措施而言，它实际上是古老的。

paras.en: Huayu Wan is a formulation of traditional Chinese medicine, containing 15 ingredients derived from two traditional remedies, the Taohong Siwu and Didang decoctions.
paras.zh: 化瘀丸是一种中药配方，含有源自两种传统药物（桃红四物汤和地当汤）的 15 种成分。

paras.en: In the past, Huayu Wan was used to treat abdominal masses and tumor-like conditions, and the formulation is still used in modern clinical settings in China to help treat tumors.
paras.zh: 过去，化瘀丸被用来治疗腹部肿块和肿瘤类疾病，该制剂在中国的现代临床环境中仍然用于帮助治疗肿瘤。

paras.en: Despite ongoing research involving Huayu Wan, much of it in animal models, there's still a lot we don't know about the molecular mechanisms underlying its antitumor effects.
paras.zh: 尽管有关化瘀丸的研究正在进行中，其中大部分是在动物模型中进行的，但我们对其抗肿瘤作用背后的分子机制仍有很多了解。

paras.en: In the new study, the researchers grew human and mouse esophageal cancer cells that were made resistant to cisplatin and exposed them to dosages of Huayu Wan.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，研究人员培养了对顺铂具有抗药性的人和小鼠食道癌细胞，并将它们暴露于一定剂量的化瘀丸中。

paras.en: Results showed that the medicinal formulation suppressed the activity and growth of the cancer cells, with greater antitumor effects seen with larger doses or after longer durations of exposure.
paras.zh: 结果表明，该药物制剂抑制了癌细胞的活性和生长，剂量越大或接触时间越长，抗肿瘤作用就越大。

paras.en: According to the researchers, Huayu Wan induces ferroptosis in cancer cells, a form of programmed cell death, in which iron contributes to a destructive buildup of oxidative damage to cell membranes.
paras.zh: 研究人员称，化瘀丸会诱导癌细胞铁死亡，这是一种程序性细胞死亡，其中铁会导致细胞膜氧化损伤的破坏性积累。

paras.en: The formulation appears to weaken cancer cells' ability to neutralize the damage, disrupting antioxidant defense mechanisms involving a chemical called glutathione and triggering cancer cells to free up their internal iron stores, which fuels greater oxidative damage.
paras.zh: 该配方似乎会削弱癌细胞中和损伤的能力，破坏涉及谷胱甘肽化学物质的抗氧化防御机制，并触发癌细胞释放其内部铁储备，从而加剧氧化损伤。

paras.en: "By coupling these two processes, Huayu Wan innovatively forces a breakdown of the cancer cells' redox defenses," the researchers explain.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说：“通过将这两个过程结合起来，化瘀丸创新地迫使癌细胞的氧化还原防御崩溃。”

paras.en: "It sparks uncontrolled lipid peroxidation while freeing iron from intracellular ferritin stores, which together drive robust ferroptotic cell death."
paras.zh: “它会引发不受控制的脂质过氧化，同时从细胞内铁蛋白储备中释放铁，这些铁蛋白共同驱动强大的铁死亡细胞。”

paras.en: In a separate experiment in mice, animals implanted with cisplatin-resistant esophageal cancer cells were treated with Huayu Wan, and the traditional medicine appeared to suppress tumor growth and reduce tumor weight, when compared to untreated mice.
paras.zh: 在另一项针对小鼠的单独实验中，用化瘀丸治疗植入顺铂耐药食管癌细胞的动物，与未经治疗的小鼠相比，这种传统药物似乎可以抑制肿瘤生长并减轻肿瘤重量。

paras.en: The researchers also found that tumors treated with Huayu Wan contained more immune cells called CD8+ T cells, suggesting the formulation might trigger an immune response that could help combat cancer cells, in addition to its direct effects on tumor suppression.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现，用化瘀丸治疗的肿瘤含有更多称为 CD8+ T 细胞的免疫细胞，这表明该制剂除了直接抑制肿瘤外，还可能引发有助于对抗癌细胞的免疫反应。

paras.en: When Huayu Wan was combined with an immunotherapy treatment called anti-PD–1, the combination produced a greater suppression of tumor growth and a greater reduction in tumor weight than either of the treatments did by themselves.
paras.zh: 当化瘀丸与一种名为抗PD-1的免疫疗法相结合时，与单独使用任何一种疗法相比，这种组合对肿瘤生长产生了更大的抑制作用，并更大程度地减轻了肿瘤重量。

paras.en: It's worth noting that the results seen here have only been demonstrated in cell lines and an animal model for now, so we'll need a lot more research before we can say that Huayu Wan would be clinically safe and similarly effective in human patients.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，这里看到的结果目前仅在细胞系和动物模型中得到证实，因此我们需要进行更多的研究才能说化瘀丸在临床上是安全的并且对人类患者同样有效。

paras.en: But based on the evidence here, there are some positive signs that this traditional Chinese medicine could be a potent tool in the future, and it's one we might very well need.
paras.zh: 但根据这里的证据，有一些积极的迹象表明这种传统中药未来可能成为一种有效的工具，而且是我们非常需要的工具。

paras.en: "Natural products are increasingly recognized for their potential to overcome chemotherapy resistance or increase drug sensitivity by modulating cancer cell survival pathways," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“天然产品因其通过调节癌细胞生存途径克服化疗耐药性或提高药物敏感性的潜力而得到越来越多的认可。”

paras.en: "These findings highlight the potential of Huayu Wan as an alternative therapeutic strategy for cisplatin-resistant ESCC and warrant further investigation of its ability to complement existing treatments."
paras.zh: “这些发现凸显了化瘀丸作为顺铂耐药性食管鳞癌替代治疗策略的潜力，并值得进一步研究其补充现有治疗的能力。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in Frontiers in Immunology.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《免疫学前沿》上。

articles.title: Scientists Have Built a Robot Dog Powered by Human Brain Cells
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: Using living neurons as the foundation of computer chips promises to bring significant advantages over conventional systems in terms of both energy efficiency and adaptability: As sophisticated as AI is, the human brain needs a lot less power to run and is still much better at dealing with the unfamiliar.
paras.zh: 使用活体神经元作为计算机芯片的基础，有望在能源效率和适应性方面比传统系统带来显着优势：尽管人工智能非常复杂，但人类大脑运行所需的能量要少得多，并且在处理不熟悉的事物方面仍然要好得多。

paras.en: The latest demonstration of this biological technology comes from scientists at Cortical Labs in Australia, who have fitted out a robotic dog with neurons grown in the lab that are able to direct it towards a target on a simple map.
paras.zh: 这种生物技术的最新演示来自澳大利亚皮质实验室的科学家，他们为一只机器狗配备了在实验室培养的神经元，能够将其引导到简单地图上的目标。

paras.en: By growing the neurons right on the chip, and fitting it with electrodes that provide two-way electrical signaling, the Cortical Labs team was able to translate activity in the small group of neurons into movement for the attached robot.
paras.zh: 通过在芯片上培养神经元，并为其安装提供双向电信号的电极，皮质实验室团队能够将一小群神经元的活动转化为所连接机器人的运动。

paras.en: "The robotic dog is a simple demonstration of how progress in biological systems can also be applied into the real world, but it helps make the opportunity tangible," says Brett Kagan, the co-founder and CEO of Cortical Labs.
paras.zh: Cortical Labs 联合创始人兼首席执行官布雷特·卡根 (Brett Kagan) 表示：“机器狗简单地展示了生物系统的进步如何应用于现实世界，但它有助于让机会变得切实可见。”

paras.en: "Longer term, this approach could support robots and autonomous systems that need to make decisions in unpredictable, real-world environments."
paras.zh: “从长远来看，这种方法可以支持需要在不可预测的现实环境中做出决策的机器人和自主系统。”

paras.en: We're still at the early stages of this technology – it's not particularly fast or efficient yet – but in the future, we could see neuron-controlled robots working in remote or hazardous conditions, or assisting humans with personalized responses that learn over time.
paras.zh: 我们仍处于这项技术的早期阶段——它还不是特别快或高效——但在未来，我们可以看到神经元控制的机器人在远程或危险的条件下工作，或者帮助人类做出随着时间的推移而学习的个性化反应。

paras.en: Cortical Labs has already demonstrated clusters of neurons completing computer tasks, including playing the games Pong and Doom, and now it's extending the idea into the physical world with robotics – and offering an alternative to traditional systems.
paras.zh: Cortical Labs 已经展示了完成计算机任务的神经元集群，包括玩 Pong 和 Doom 游戏，现在它正在通过机器人技术将这一想法扩展到物理世界，并提供传统系统的替代方案。

paras.en: "Robots that are becoming remarkably capable machines at their physical control, still struggle with the higher order control required to learn quickly or adapt when conditions change," says Kagan.
paras.zh: 卡根说：“机器人在物理控制方面正在成为功能非常强大的机器，但仍然难以实现快速学习或适应条件变化所需的高阶控制。”

paras.en: "Walking, running, and doing acrobatics is amazing, but determining where and when to do actions remains a challenge with traditional methods."
paras.zh: “步行、跑步和做杂技是令人惊奇的，但确定何时何地进行动作对于传统方法来说仍然是一个挑战。”

paras.en: A similar technology demonstration has also been run by Cortical Labs in partnership with Honda Research Institute Europe. In this demo, everything was run inside a virtual system, but again the aim was directing an agent around a basic grid in search of a reward.
paras.zh: Cortical Labs 与本田欧洲研究院合作也进行了类似的技术演示。在这个演示中，一切都在虚拟系统内运行，但目标还是引导代理围绕基本网格寻找奖励。

paras.en: The setup was the same, with electrical signals stimulating neurons on a chip, and the chip returning electrical messages of its own. By varying the characteristics of the electrical signal and supplying feedback on the moves of the agent, the researchers were able to train and interpret movement from the living chip.
paras.zh: 设置是相同的，电信号刺激芯片上的神经元，芯片返回自己的电信息。通过改变电信号的特征并提供有关代理动作的反馈，研究人员能够训练和解释活体芯片的动作。

paras.en: Over more than 4,000 hours of interactions with the chip and agent, the team was able to test almost 1,300 different signal combinations.
paras.zh: 经过 4,000 多个小时与芯片和代理的交互，该团队能够测试近 1,300 种不同的信号组合。

paras.en: "This research collaboration enables us to investigate fundamentally different approaches to intelligent agents," says Daniel Tanneberg, a Senior Scientist at Honda Research Institute Europe.
paras.zh: “这项研究合作使我们能够研究完全不同的智能代理方法，”本田欧洲研究所的高级科学家 Daniel Tanneberg 说。

paras.en: "Using living cells as the core computational substrate comes with many challenges but also offers great potential in terms of energy efficiency, robustness, and adaptation – potential that we can now begin to explore and evaluate."
paras.zh: “使用活细胞作为核心计算基质带来了许多挑战，但在能源效率、鲁棒性和适应性方面也提供了巨大的潜力——我们现在可以开始探索和评估这些潜力。”

paras.en: There was still a fair amount of trial and error here, and the next steps are to scale up these chips to tackle more complex tasks in a shorter time – as robots out in the real world are going to need to do much more than navigate around a simple grid.
paras.zh: 这里仍然存在大量的试验和错误，下一步是扩大这些芯片的规模，以在更短的时间内处理更复杂的任务——因为现实世界中的机器人需要做的不仅仅是在简单的网格中导航。

paras.en: Another aim for the researchers is to learn more about how these neuron-based chips retain information, and what kind of 'memory' feature they might have.
paras.zh: 研究人员的另一个目标是更多地了解这些基于神经元的芯片如何保留信息，以及它们可能具有什么样的“记忆”功能。

paras.en: "The challenge is not simply growing neurons on silicon: It is finding reliable ways to communicate with biological systems, train them and understand which approaches produce consistent results," says Johnson Zhou, a Research Software Engineer at Cortical Labs.
paras.zh: Cortical Labs 的研究软件工程师 Johnson Zhou 表示：“挑战不仅仅是在硅上生长神经元：它还在于找到与生物系统通信的可靠方法，训练它们并了解哪些方法会产生一致的结果。”

paras.en: "This research gives us a framework for testing those questions at scale. It establishes a foundation we can build on as biological computing moves towards practical applications."
paras.zh: “这项研究为我们提供了一个大规模测试这些问题的框架。它为我们在生物计算走向实际应用时奠定了基础。”

paras.en: The navigation research has yet to be peer-reviewed but has been presented at the NeurIPS 2026 conference and is available on arXiv.
paras.zh: 该导航研究尚未经过同行评审，但已在 NeurIPS 2026 会议上展示，并可在 arXiv 上获取。

articles.title: Scientists reveal a hidden snakebite crisis killing up to 513,000 people a year

paras.en: Scientists reveal a hidden snakebite crisis killing up to 513,000 people a year
paras.zh: 科学家揭示了隐藏的蛇咬伤危机，每年导致多达 513,000 人死亡

paras.en: - A startling new study suggests that venomous snakebites are killing far more people worldwide than official statistics indicate, with an estimated 274,000 to 513,000 deaths every year. Researchers found that as many as 7 million people could suffer snake envenoming annually, while more than 800,000 survivors are left with long-term disabilities.
paras.zh: - 一项令人震惊的新研究表明，全世界因毒蛇咬伤而死亡的人数远远多于官方统计数字，估计每年有 274,000 至 513,000 人死亡。研究人员发现，每年有多达 700 万人遭受蛇毒袭击，而超过 80 万幸存者会留下长期残疾。

paras.en: Not every snakebite injects venom. When venom enters the body, however, it can cause snake envenoming. This is a potentially fatal condition and it mostly affects poor rural communities across tropical and subtropical regions who don’t have easy access to medical care.
paras.zh: 并非每次被蛇咬伤都会注入毒液。然而，当毒液进入体内时，会导致蛇中毒。这是一种潜在的致命疾病，主要影响热带和亚热带地区的贫困农村社区，他们无法轻易获得医疗服务。

paras.en: As researchers with decades of combined experience in snakebite and tropical disease epidemiology, we came to realise that snake envenoming faces a data crisis. Over half of the countries where venomous snakes pose a threat don’t keep count of how many people are bitten or envenomed.
paras.zh: 作为在蛇咬伤和热带疾病流行病学方面拥有数十年综合经验的研究人员，我们逐渐意识到蛇中毒面临着数据危机。超过一半的毒蛇构成威胁的国家没有统计有多少人被咬或中毒。

paras.en: In rural sub-Saharan Africa and south Asia, many victims live hours away from the nearest clinic, lack transport, or seek care from traditional healers. As a result, their cases are never captured in national health statistics.
paras.zh: 在撒哈拉以南非洲和南亚的农村地区，许多受害者的住所距离最近的诊所只有几个小时的路程，缺乏交通工具，或者寻求传统治疗师的护理。因此，他们的病例从未被记录在国家卫生统计数据中。

paras.en: To bridge this massive gap, we conducted a study to map the global burden of snake envenoming and related deaths.
paras.zh: 为了弥补这一巨大差距，我们进行了一项研究，绘制了蛇中毒和相关死亡的全球负担。

paras.en: We looked at data from 79 countries by reviewing studies published up to March 31, 2025. This allowed us to update the findings from our milestone 2008 global burden study. To fill the remaining data gaps, we built a geostatistical model that combines real-world data with local environmental and socioeconomic factors. This allowed us to estimate envenoming and fatality rates.
paras.zh: 我们通过回顾截至 2025 年 3 月 31 日发布的研究来查看来自 79 个国家的数据。这使我们能够更新里程碑式的 2008 年全球负担研究的结果。为了填补剩余的数据空白，我们建立了一个地统计模型，将现实世界数据与当地环境和社会经济因素结合起来。这使我们能够估计中毒率和死亡率。

paras.en: We conclude from our findings that snake envenoming is a public health crisis on a far greater scale than official statistics have shown. Our results show that sub-Saharan Africa bears the heaviest toll.
paras.zh: 我们从我们的研究结果中得出结论，蛇中毒是一场公共卫生危机，其规模比官方统计数据显示的规模要大得多。我们的结果显示，撒哈拉以南非洲地区的死亡人数最为严重。

paras.en: The World Health Organization has set an ambitious target to halve snakebite mortality and disability by 2030. Mapping the problem at the country level is the first crucial step.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织制定了一个雄心勃勃的目标，即到 2030 年将蛇咬伤死亡率和残疾率降低一半。在国家层面上绘制问题地图是关键的第一步。

paras.en: To overcome the lack of reliable data, we turned to a model-based geostatistics framework.
paras.zh: 为了克服缺乏可靠数据的问题，我们转向基于模型的地质统计框架。

paras.en: To understand how this modelling works, think of it as predicting invisible patterns by combining known data points with environmental signals. Instead of assuming data for every region, this modelling uses statistical probability to calculate a range of likely outcomes based on environmental signals.
paras.zh: 要了解此建模的工作原理，请将其视为通过将已知数据点与环境信号相结合来预测不可见的模式。该模型没有假设每个区域的数据，而是使用统计概率根据环境信号计算一系列可能的结果。

paras.en: We fed our model with data including climate, snake species richness and socioeconomic indicators. The model then calculated the probability of snakebites occurring in specific locations, even where official health records were completely blank.
paras.zh: 我们为模型提供了气候、蛇物种丰富度和社会经济指标等数据。然后，该模型计算了特定地点发生蛇咬伤的概率，即使官方健康记录完全空白。

paras.en: By comparing different data sources (including hospital-reported data and regional statistics) against ground level community-survey data, our framework allowed us to account for unreported snake envenomings. It produced both a baseline floor and a potential upper ceiling for snake envenomings and fatalities.
paras.zh: 通过将不同的数据源（包括医院报告的数据和区域统计数据）与地面社区调查数据进行比较，我们的框架使我们能够解释未报告的蛇中毒事件。它为蛇中毒和死亡提供了底线和潜在的上限。

paras.en: Based on this, we estimate that at least 2.1 million people experience snake envenoming each year globally. The true number could be high as 7 million. Using our model, which adjusts for substantial under-reporting, annual deaths may range from 274,000 to 513,000.
paras.zh: 据此，我们估计全球每年至少有 210 万人遭受蛇毒袭击。真实数字可能高达700万。使用我们的模型（根据大量漏报情况进行调整），每年的死亡人数可能在 274,000 人到 513,000 人之间。

paras.en: The geographic distribution of this burden is uneven. Our research shows that sub-Saharan Africa alone accounts for 45% of all global envenomings and fatalities. That burden has likely been underestimated for decades. People in sub-Saharan Africa experience snake envenoming and death at nearly three times the rate seen in south Asia.
paras.zh: 这一负担的地理分布不均匀。我们的研究表明，仅撒哈拉以南非洲地区就占全球中毒事件和死亡人数的 45%。几十年来，这一负担可能一直被低估。撒哈拉以南非洲地区的人们遭受蛇中毒和死亡的比率几乎是南亚地区的三倍。

paras.en: Countries like Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Ethiopia face a high burden, driven by dense rural populations and high exposure in agricultural fields.
paras.zh: 由于农村人口密集和农业领域的高风险，尼日利亚、刚果民主共和国和埃塞俄比亚等国家面临着沉重的负担。

paras.en: The reasons sub-Saharan Africa suffers such disproportionate harm are structural rather than accidental.
paras.zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲地区遭受如此严重损害的原因是结构性的，而不是偶然的。

paras.en: Firstly, the continent hosts a rich diversity of medically important venomous species. These include saw-scaled vipers (Echis spp.), puff adders (Bitis arietans), African cobras (Naja spp.) and mambas (Dendroaspis spp.). They are responsible for substantial morbidity and mortality across the continent.
paras.zh: 首先，这片大陆拥有丰富多样的具有重要医学意义的有毒物种。其中包括锯鳞蝰蛇 (Echis spp.)、粉蝰 (Bitis arietans)、非洲眼镜蛇 (Naja spp.) 和曼巴蛇 (Dendroaspis spp.)。它们造成了整个非洲大陆的大量发病率和死亡率。

paras.en: Secondly, millions of rural agricultural workers labor in open fields without protective boots and walk on unlit footpaths at night. When a bite occurs, fragile health systems, long travel distances to regional facilities and the high cost or total absence of effective antivenom mean a treatable medical emergency can quickly become fatal. Similar conditions exist in parts of Asia.
paras.zh: 其次，数以百万计的农村农业工人在空旷的田野里劳作，没有穿防护靴，晚上走在没有灯光的小路上。当发生咬伤时，脆弱的卫生系统、到地区设施的长途旅行以及高昂的成本或完全缺乏有效的抗蛇毒血清意味着可治疗的医疗紧急情况可能很快就会致命。亚洲部分地区也存在类似情况。

paras.en: We estimate that over 800,000 survivors are left with long-term physical disabilities each year, including amputations and other permanent impairments. These disabilities can reduce household income, increase healthcare costs and push already vulnerable farming families deeper into poverty.
paras.zh: 我们估计，每年有超过 800,000 名幸存者留下长期身体残疾，包括截肢和其他永久性损伤。这些残疾会减少家庭收入，增加医疗费用，并使本已脆弱的农业家庭陷入更深的贫困。

paras.en: Meeting the World Health Organization’s goal requires moving away from guesswork and using spatial risk data to guide real-world policy.
paras.zh: 实现世界卫生组织的目标需要摆脱猜测，并使用空间风险数据来指导现实世界的政策。

paras.en: By identifying high-risk hotspots, governments and global health partners can strategically stockpile antivenom where it is needed most, train primary healthcare workers in high-burden rural zones and improve rapid transport infrastructure.
paras.zh: 通过识别高风险热点地区，各国政府和全球卫生合作伙伴可以在最需要的地方战略性地储备抗蛇毒血清，培训高负担农村地区的初级卫生保健人员，并改善快速交通基础设施。

paras.en: Snake envenoming has remained hidden for too long. Better data cannot solve the problem, but can help ensure that antivenom, healthcare services and prevention efforts reach the communities that need them most.
paras.zh: 蛇中毒已经隐藏太久了。更好的数据不能解决问题，但可以帮助确保抗蛇毒血清、医疗服务和预防工作到达最需要的社区。

paras.en: Materials provided by The Conversation. Original written by Dileepa Ediriweera, Health Data Scientist, Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由对话提供。原文由利物浦热带医学院健康数据科学家 Dileepa Ediriweera 撰写。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: Hubble reveals a stunning twist in how the universe emerged from darkness

paras.en: Hubble reveals a stunning twist in how the universe emerged from darkness
paras.zh: 哈勃揭示了宇宙如何从黑暗中出现的惊人转折

paras.en: - A surprising discovery by astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope is challenging a leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense fog of hydrogen roughly 13 billion years ago. Scientists once believed powerful winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape galaxies and clear that cosmic fog, but new observations reveal that these winds actually block radiation instead.
paras.zh: - 天文学家使用哈勃太空望远镜的一项令人惊讶的发现正在挑战关于早期宇宙如何从大约 130 亿年前的浓密氢雾中出现的主要解释。科学家们曾经相信，恒星爆炸产生的强大风有助于辐射逃离星系并清除宇宙迷雾，但新的观察结果表明，这些风实际上会阻挡辐射。

paras.en: A surprising discovery made with NASA's Hubble Space Telescope is challenging a leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from darkness. The findings suggest that powerful explosions from dying stars may have actually interfered with a process scientists once believed they helped drive.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局哈勃太空望远镜的一项令人惊讶的发现正在挑战关于早期宇宙如何从黑暗中出现的主要解释。研究结果表明，垂死恒星产生的强大爆炸实际上可能干扰了科学家曾经认为它们有助于驱动的过程。

paras.en: An international research team, including astronomers from the University of Michigan, found that powerful winds produced by exploding stars can prevent ultraviolet radiation from escaping galaxies. This is the opposite of what a widely accepted theory had predicted, and it could change how scientists understand one of the most important transformations in cosmic history.
paras.zh: 包括密歇根大学天文学家在内的一个国际研究小组发现，恒星爆炸产生的强大风可以阻止紫外线辐射逸出星系。这与广泛接受的理论的预测相反，它可能会改变科学家理解宇宙历史上最重要的转变之一的方式。

paras.en: The discovery, published in Nature Astronomy, offers new clues about how the universe became transparent to ultraviolet light roughly 13 billion years ago.
paras.zh: 这一发现发表在《自然天文学》上，为了解大约 130 亿年前宇宙如何对紫外线变得透明提供了新线索。

paras.en: How the Early Universe Emerged From Its Cosmic Fog
paras.zh: 早期宇宙如何从宇宙迷雾中出现

paras.en: During the first billion years after the Big Bang, vast amounts of neutral hydrogen filled the space between galaxies. This hydrogen formed a kind of cosmic fog that absorbed ultraviolet radiation, preventing that light from traveling freely across the universe.
paras.zh: 在大爆炸后的最初十亿年里，大量的中性氢充满了星系之间的空间。这种氢形成了一种吸收紫外线辐射的宇宙雾，阻止光线在宇宙中自由传播。

paras.en: That changed during a period known as reionization, which began approximately 13 billion years ago. Intense radiation from early galaxies gradually transformed the hydrogen by stripping electrons from its atoms, leaving behind positively charged protons and free electrons.
paras.zh: 这种情况在大约 130 亿年前开始的“再电离”时期发生了变化。来自早期星系的强烈辐射通过从原子中剥离电子来逐渐改变氢，留下带正电的质子和自由电子。

paras.en: As more hydrogen became ionized, ultraviolet light could travel much farther through intergalactic space. This transformation helped establish the relatively transparent universe that astronomers observe today.
paras.zh: 随着更多的氢被电离，紫外线可以在星际空间中传播更远的距离。这种转变帮助建立了天文学家今天观察到的相对透明的宇宙。

paras.en: "Eventually, when it ionized the majority of hydrogen filling intergalactic space, that was the end of reionization and we see the universe today," said Cody Carr, a postdoctoral researcher in the University of Michigan's Department of Astronomy. "We call reionization the last major phase transition of the universe."
paras.zh: 密歇根大学天文学系博士后研究员科迪·卡尔说：“最终，当它电离了星系际空间中的大部分氢时，再电离就结束了，我们看到了今天的宇宙。” “我们将再电离称为宇宙的最后一个主要相变。”

paras.en: Despite its enormous importance, astronomers still do not fully understand which objects supplied the radiation responsible for reionization or how enough of that radiation managed to escape from early galaxies.
paras.zh: 尽管它非常重要，但天文学家仍然不完全了解哪些物体提供了负责再电离的辐射，或者足够的辐射如何设法从早期星系中逃逸。

paras.en: "We don't know exactly what objects caused reionization or how it evolved," said Carr, who conducted and led the research while working as a postdoctoral scholar at Zhejiang University in China, before joining the University of Michigan. "We know that it took place, but we don't have complete answers to those questions."
paras.zh: 卡尔说：“我们不知道到底是什么物体引起了再电离，也不知道它是如何进化的。”在加入密歇根大学之前，卡尔在中国浙江大学担任博士后学者期间进行并领导了这项研究。 “我们知道它发生了，但我们没有这些问题的完整答案。”

paras.en: Hubble Challenges a Leading Theory About Exploding Stars
paras.zh: 哈勃挑战有关恒星爆炸的领先理论

paras.en: For years, one prominent explanation centered on supernovae, the powerful explosions that occur when certain stars reach the ends of their lives. These explosions can generate enormous winds that sweep through galaxies, pushing gas and other material outward.
paras.zh: 多年来，一个著名的解释集中在超新星上，超新星是某些恒星生命终结时发生的强烈爆炸。这些爆炸会产生席卷星系的巨大风，将气体和其他物质向外推。

paras.en: Scientists proposed that these winds cleared pathways through the gas surrounding young stars, allowing ultraviolet radiation to escape into the space between galaxies. Once outside, that radiation could help break apart the neutral hydrogen responsible for the universe's ancient fog.
paras.zh: 科学家提出，这些风清除了年轻恒星周围气体的通道，使紫外线辐射能够逃逸到星系之间的空间。一旦到了外面，这种辐射可能会帮助分解造成宇宙古老雾气的中性氢。

paras.en: However, new observations from Hubble suggest that this explanation may have the process backward.
paras.zh: 然而，哈勃的新观测表明，这种解释可能会导致过程倒退。

paras.en: Rather than opening routes for radiation to escape, the researchers found that stronger galactic winds were associated with less escaping ionizing radiation. The observations indicate that the winds generated by supernovae can actually make it harder for the radiation to leave a galaxy.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，更强的银河风并没有为辐射逃逸开辟通道，而是与逃逸的电离辐射减少有关。观测结果表明，超新星产生的风实际上会使辐射更难离开星系。

paras.en: "Basically, how these galaxies were leaking ionizing radiation isn't what we thought," Carr said.
paras.zh: “基本上，这些星系如何泄漏电离辐射并不是我们想象的那样，”卡尔说。

paras.en: The results lend support to a different possibility. Radiation from young, massive stars may escape their galaxies before those stars explode as supernovae and generate large winds that reshape the surrounding environment.
paras.zh: 结果支持了另一种可能性。年轻的大质量恒星的辐射可能会在这些恒星爆炸为超新星并产生重塑周围环境的强风之前逸出星系。

paras.en: "Our observations show that these photons are escaping before galactic winds form," Carr said.
paras.zh: “我们的观察表明，这些光子在银河风形成之前就已经逃逸，”卡尔说。

paras.en: Photons are individual packets of light energy. In this case, the researchers are interested in ultraviolet photons energetic enough to ionize hydrogen, making them essential to understanding how the early universe became transparent.
paras.zh: 光子是单独的光能包。在这种情况下，研究人员对能量足以电离氢的紫外光子感兴趣，这使得它们对于理解早期宇宙如何变得透明至关重要。

paras.en: What Hubble Discovered in Nearby Starburst Galaxies
paras.zh: 哈勃在附近的星爆星系中发现了什么

paras.en: To investigate how radiation escapes, the international team used the Hubble Space Telescope to examine nearby starburst galaxies. These are galaxies experiencing exceptionally intense periods of star formation, making them useful modern examples of the kinds of galaxies believed to have contributed to reionization.
paras.zh: 为了调查辐射如何逃逸，国际团队使用哈勃太空望远镜检查附近的星暴星系。这些星系经历了异常强烈的恒星形成时期，使它们成为被认为有助于再电离的星系的有用的现代例子。

paras.en: Hubble, a NASA mission launched with contributions from the European Space Agency, allowed researchers to study the light coming from these galaxies in detail.
paras.zh: 哈勃是美国宇航局在欧洲航天局的资助下启动的一项任务，它使研究人员能够详细研究来自这些星系的光。

paras.en: The team examined their spectra, which reveal how much light is present at different wavelengths. By studying the patterns in those spectra, astronomers can learn about the gas surrounding stars and determine how quickly it is moving.
paras.zh: 研究小组检查了它们的光谱，揭示了不同波长下存在多少光。通过研究这些光谱中的模式，天文学家可以了解恒星周围的气体并确定其移动速度。

paras.en: Gas absorbs particular wavelengths of light, creating recognizable dips in a galaxy's spectrum. The locations and shapes of these dips provide clues about the speed and movement of galactic winds.
paras.zh: 气体吸收特定波长的光，在星系光谱中产生可识别的凹陷。这些凹陷的位置和形状提供了有关银河风的速度和运动的线索。

paras.en: When the researchers compared wind speeds with the amount of ionizing radiation escaping from each galaxy, they uncovered a surprising relationship. Galaxies with the fastest winds allowed the smallest fraction of ionizing radiation to escape.
paras.zh: 当研究人员将风速与从每个星系逸出的电离辐射量进行比较时，他们发现了一种令人惊讶的关系。风速最快的星系允许逃逸的电离辐射比例最小。

paras.en: That result directly challenges the expectation that stronger winds should clear away more gas and make it easier for radiation to reach intergalactic space.
paras.zh: 这一结果直接挑战了更强的风应该清除更多气体并使辐射更容易到达星际空间的预期。

paras.en: "It appears that energy input from supernovae has stirred up the surroundings and increased, rather than decreased, the coverage of neutral gas and dust that suppresses ionizing radiation escape," said Stephan McCandliss, a senior author of the study and director of the Center for Astrophysical Sciences at Johns Hopkins University.
paras.zh: 该研究的资深作者、约翰·霍普金斯大学天体物理科学中心主任斯蒂芬·麦坎德利斯说：“超新星输入的能量似乎搅动了周围环境，增加了而不是减少了抑制电离辐射逃逸的中性气体和尘埃的覆盖范围。”

paras.en: In other words, instead of clearing a path for ultraviolet light, energy from exploding stars appears to redistribute gas and dust in ways that can block more of it.
paras.zh: 换句话说，恒星爆炸产生的能量似乎并没有为紫外线扫清道路，而是重新分配了气体和尘埃，从而阻挡了更多的气体和尘埃。

paras.en: Young Stars May Hold the Key to Cosmic Reionization
paras.zh: 年轻恒星可能掌握着宇宙再电离的关键

paras.en: Although large galactic winds appear to suppress escaping radiation, smaller winds and other activity around young stars could still help create openings in the surrounding gas.
paras.zh: 尽管大型银河风似乎抑制了逃逸的辐射，但年轻恒星周围较小的风和其他活动仍然有助于在周围的气体中形成开口。

paras.en: These processes may occur before the first supernova explosions, giving radiation a chance to escape while conditions are more favorable.
paras.zh: 这些过程可能发生在第一次超新星爆炸之前，使辐射有机会在条件更有利的情况下逃逸。

paras.en: The findings suggest that astronomers may need to pay greater attention to what happens during the earliest stages of star formation, rather than focusing primarily on the effects of exploding stars.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，天文学家可能需要更多地关注恒星形成的最早阶段发生的事情，而不是主要关注恒星爆炸的影响。

paras.en: Carr and his colleagues are seeking additional observing time with Hubble to examine more galaxies and investigate whether the same patterns appear elsewhere. More observations could help establish how important the activity of young stars is in allowing ionizing radiation to escape.
paras.zh: 卡尔和他的同事正在寻求哈勃望远镜的额外观测时间，以检查更多星系并调查其他地方是否出现相同的模式。更多的观测可以帮助确定年轻恒星的活动对于电离辐射逃逸的重要性。

paras.en: The results also have implications for computer simulations of the early universe. These simulations attempt to recreate how galaxies formed, how gas moved through them, and how radiation eventually transformed the hydrogen filling intergalactic space.
paras.zh: 研究结果对早期宇宙的计算机模拟也有影响。这些模拟试图重现星系是如何形成的，气体如何穿过星系，以及辐射如何最终改变充满氢的星系间空间。

paras.en: "Supernovae play a central role in cosmological hydrodynamic simulations that explain how ionizing radiation escapes from galaxies," said Renyue Cen, a senior author of the study and professor and director of the Center for Cosmology and Computational Astrophysics at Zhejiang University. "Our findings highlight the need to examine how radiation and winds from young stars shape the surrounding gas before the first supernovae explode."
paras.zh: 该研究的资深作者、浙江大学宇宙学与计算天体物理中心教授兼主任岑仁跃说：“超新星在解释电离辐射如何从星系逃逸的宇宙流体动力学模拟中发挥着核心作用。” “我们的发现强调需要研究年轻恒星的辐射和风在第一颗超新星爆炸之前如何塑造周围的气体。”

paras.en: By accounting more accurately for these early interactions between stars, radiation, and gas, researchers may be able to build better models of how reionization unfolded.
paras.zh: 通过更准确地解释恒星、辐射和气体之间的这些早期相互作用，研究人员也许能够建立更好的模型来解释再电离是如何展开的。

paras.en: The discovery does not yet settle the question of what caused the universe's last major phase transition. However, it provides an important new clue, suggesting that the radiation that helped lift the universe's ancient fog may have escaped galaxies before powerful stellar explosions began to alter their surroundings.
paras.zh: 这一发现尚未解决是什么导致了宇宙最后一次主要相变的问题。然而，它提供了一条重要的新线索，表明在强大的恒星爆炸开始改变星系周围环境之前，帮助解除宇宙古老迷雾的辐射可能已经逃离了星系。

paras.en: International Research Collaboration and Funding
paras.zh: 国际研究合作和资助

paras.en: The research brought together nearly 30 scientists from more than a dozen institutions around the world. Sally Oey, a professor of astronomy at the University of Michigan, also contributed to the study.
paras.zh: 这项研究汇集了来自全球十几家机构的近 30 名科学家。密歇根大学天文学教授 Sally Oey 也对这项研究做出了贡献。

paras.en: The project received additional financial support from Zhejiang University, the Zhejiang Provincial Top-Level Research Support Program, the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities in Spain, the European Regional Development Fund, and the European Union's Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Program.
paras.zh: 该项目得到了浙江大学、浙江省顶尖研究支撑计划、国家自然科学基金委、西班牙科学、创新和大学部、欧洲区域发展基金、欧盟地平线2020研究与创新计划的额外资助。

paras.en: The research was also supported in part by federal funding from NASA and the U.S. National Science Foundation. Additional support for the Hubble Space Telescope observations came through a grant administered by the Space Telescope Science Institute.
paras.zh: 这项研究还得到了美国宇航局和美国国家科学基金会的联邦资助的部分支持。对哈勃太空望远镜观测的额外支持来自太空望远镜科学研究所的拨款。

articles.title: A computer scientist breaks through a limit that stood since 1996

paras.en: A computer scientist breaks through a limit that stood since 1996
paras.zh: 一位计算机科学家突破了 1996 年以来的限制

paras.en: - Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar
paras.zh: - 印度甘地讷格尔理工学院

paras.en: - A computer scientist has achieved a breakthrough in a nearly 25-year-old problem involving how computers calculate distances across enormous networks. The new algorithm delivers more reliable estimates for closely connected points without sacrificing speed, overcoming a longstanding limitation of earlier methods. Its secret lies in a smarter way of sampling network connections at multiple scales.
paras.zh: - 一位计算机科学家在一个近 25 年的问题上取得了突破，该问题涉及计算机如何计算跨巨大网络的距离。新算法可以在不牺牲速度的情况下为紧密相连的点提供更可靠的估计，从而克服了早期方法长期存在的局限性。它的秘密在于以更智能的方式对多个尺度的网络连接进行采样。

paras.en: Finding the shortest route between two locations is something navigation apps like Google Maps do every day. Behind the scenes, sophisticated algorithms analyze networks of roads and intersections to identify efficient paths. But what if a computer needed to calculate the shortest distance between every possible pair of locations in an enormous network?
paras.zh: 寻找两个地点之间的最短路线是 Google 地图等导航应用每天都会做的事情。在幕后，复杂的算法分析道路和交叉路口网络，以确定有效的路径。但是，如果计算机需要计算庞大网络中每对可能的位置之间的最短距离怎么办？

paras.en: That challenge extends far beyond maps. Similar calculations are important for transportation systems, communication networks, and even biological structures involving proteins, neurons, or other interconnected components. As these networks grow, determining the shortest routes between all their points becomes increasingly difficult.
paras.zh: 这一挑战远远超出了地图的范围。类似的计算对于运输系统、通信网络，甚至涉及蛋白质、神经元或其他互连组件的生物结构都很重要。随着这些网络的发展，确定所有点之间的最短路线变得越来越困难。

paras.en: Computer scientists call this the All-Pairs Shortest Paths (APSP) problem. It involves finding the shortest distance between every pair of points in a graph. In this context, a 'graph' is simply a collection of points (called vertices) joined by connections (called edges). Those points might represent cities, PCs, subway stations, or organs, while the connections could stand for highways, cables, railway lines, or blood vessels.
paras.zh: 计算机科学家将此称为全对最短路径（APSP）问题。它涉及找到图中每对点之间的最短距离。在这种情况下，“图”只是由连接（称为边）连接的点（称为顶点）的集合。这些点可能代表城市、电脑、地铁站或器官，而连接可能代表高速公路、电缆、铁路线或血管。

paras.en: Why Calculating Shortest Paths Is So Difficult
paras.zh: 为什么计算最短路径如此困难

paras.en: Determining the exact shortest distances across a massive network can consume enormous amounts of computing time and memory. In densely connected networks, some conventional approaches require what mathematicians call cubic time. That means doubling the number of points can increase the computational workload by roughly eight times.
paras.zh: 确定大型网络中确切的最短距离可能会消耗大量的计算时间和内存。在密集连接的网络中，一些传统方法需要数学家所说的立方时间。这意味着点数加倍会使计算工作量增加大约八倍。

paras.en: Because the required computation (work) can grow much faster than the network itself, researchers have spent decades searching for more efficient methods. One promising solution is to use approximation algorithms, which calculate estimates rather than exact answers. The goal is to produce distances that are sufficiently accurate while dramatically reducing the amount of computation required.
paras.zh: 由于所需的计算（工作）的增长速度比网络本身快得多，因此研究人员花费了数十年的时间寻找更有效的方法。一种有前途的解决方案是使用近似算法，该算法计算估计值而不是精确答案。目标是产生足够准确的距离，同时显着减少所需的计算量。

paras.en: An important advance came in 1996, when researchers Dor, Halperin, and Zwick (DHZ) developed a method capable of producing distance estimates within twice the actual shortest distance for sufficiently distant points, while operating in nearly optimal time.
paras.zh: 1996 年取得了一项重要进展，当时研究人员 Dor、Halperin 和 Zwick (DHZ) 开发了一种方法，能够对足够远的点在两倍于实际最短距离的范围内生成距离估计，同时在几乎最佳的时间内运行。

paras.en: This level of accuracy is known as a "2‑approximation." For example, if the shortest possible route between two locations is 10 kilometers, an estimate satisfying this guarantee would fall between 10 and 20 kilometers.
paras.zh: 这种精度水平被称为“2 近似值”。例如，如果两个位置之间的最短可能路线为 10 公里，则满足此保证的估计值将在 10 到 20 公里之间。

paras.en: Rather than examining every possible route, the DHZ approach uses a relatively small selection of points from the network (referred to as sampled vertices). These strategically selected points serve as shortcuts that help the algorithm estimate distances more efficiently.
paras.zh: DHZ 方法不是检查每条可能的路线，而是使用网络中相对较小的点选择（称为采样顶点）。这些战略性选择的点作为捷径，帮助算法更有效地估计距离。

paras.en: A Clever Shortcut With a Hidden Weakness
paras.zh: 隐藏弱点的聪明捷径

paras.en: The approach works particularly well when the points being compared are far apart.
paras.zh: 当比较的点相距很远时，该方法尤其有效。

paras.en: Consider a journey between Delhi and Chennai. Because the cities are separated by a considerable distance, the algorithm can often find a sampled point close to the shortest route. This allows it to calculate an estimate that remains within the promised limit of twice the actual distance.
paras.zh: 考虑德里和钦奈之间的旅程。由于城市相距相当远，算法通常可以找到最接近最短路线的采样点。这使得它能够计算出一个估计值，该估计值保持在实际距离两倍的承诺限制内。

paras.en: However, the same strategy becomes less dependable when the two points are close together.
paras.zh: 然而，当两点接近时，相同的策略就变得不太可靠。

paras.en: Imagine calculating the shortest route between two neighborhoods in the Mumbai suburbs. The sampled points might be located too far from the most direct connection, forcing the algorithm to estimate a much longer route.
paras.zh: 想象一下计算孟买郊区两个街区之间的最短路线。采样点可能距离最直接的连接太远，迫使算法估计更长的路线。

paras.en: For example, two points might be connected by a path containing just two edges, yet the sampled route could contain five. Because five exceeds twice the true distance of two, the result violates the "at most twice" accuracy guarantee.
paras.zh: 例如，两个点可能通过仅包含两条边的路径连接，但采样的路线可能包含五个边。由于 5 超过 2 真实距离的两倍，因此结果违反了“最多两倍”的精度保证。

paras.en: This weakness meant that the original algorithm's mathematical guarantee applied only when the points were sufficiently far apart. For closer connections, the same level of accuracy could not always be assured.
paras.zh: 这一弱点意味着原始算法的数学保证仅在点相距足够远时才适用。对于更紧密的连接，无法始终保证相同水平的准确性。

paras.en: That limitation remained a challenge for nearly three decades.
paras.zh: 近三十年来，这一限制仍然是一个挑战。

paras.en: A New Algorithm Breaks Through a Decades-Old Limit
paras.zh: 一种新算法突破了几十年前的限制

paras.en: Now, Dr. Manoj Gupta, an Associate Professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar, has introduced a refinement that extends the accuracy guarantee to points much closer together than earlier methods allowed.
paras.zh: 现在，印度甘地讷格尔理工学院副教授 Manoj Gupta 博士引入了一项改进，将精度保证扩展到比早期方法允许的距离更近的点。

paras.en: Gupta presented his research at the 66th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS 2025) in a paper titled "Improved 2-Approximate Shortest Paths for close vertex pairs."
paras.zh: Gupta 在第 66 届计算机科学基础年度研讨会 (FOCS 2025) 上发表了一篇题为“Improved 2-Approximate Shortest Paths for close vertexpairs”的论文，展示了他的研究成果。

paras.en: The achievement is particularly significant because the improved algorithm preserves the overall runtime of the earlier approach while expanding the range of distances for which reliable estimates can be guaranteed.
paras.zh: 这一成就尤为重要，因为改进的算法保留了早期方法的整体运行时间，同时扩大了可以保证可靠估计的距离范围。

paras.en: The breakthrough comes from rethinking how points are sampled within the network.
paras.zh: 突破来自于重新思考网络内点的采样方式。

paras.en: Traditional methods depended on a collection of representative points to estimate distances. Gupta's approach instead introduces a multi-scale sampling strategy that organizes information about the network at several different levels.
paras.zh: 传统方法依赖于代表点的集合来估计距离。相反，古普塔的方法引入了一种多尺度采样策略，该策略在多个不同级别上组织有关网络的信息。

paras.en: By analyzing connections at multiple scales rather than relying on a single sampling layer, the algorithm can account for shorter routes that previous approaches might overlook.
paras.zh: 通过分析多个尺度的连接而不是依赖于单个采样层，该算法可以解释以前的方法可能忽略的较短路线。

paras.en: This more sophisticated sampling technique reduces the minimum distance required for the 2-approximation guarantee to hold, without increasing the algorithm's overall computational complexity.
paras.zh: 这种更复杂的采样技术减少了保持 2 近似保证所需的最小距离，而不会增加算法的整体计算复杂性。

paras.en: Returning to the transportation example, the original DHZ method could efficiently estimate sufficiently long journeys, such as the route between Delhi and Chennai. The improved approach extends that dependable accuracy to much shorter connections (such as Mumbai's suburbs).
paras.zh: 回到交通示例，最初的 DHZ 方法可以有效地估计足够长的旅程，例如德里和金奈之间的路线。改进的方法将可靠的准确性扩展到更短的连接（例如孟买的郊区）。

paras.en: The central achievement is not simply a new way to estimate distances. It is the ability to provide the same mathematical accuracy guarantee across a wider range of distances while maintaining computational efficiency.
paras.zh: 核心成就不仅仅是一种估计距离的新方法。它能够在更广泛的距离内提供相同的数学精度保证，同时保持计算效率。

paras.en: Why This Computer Science Breakthrough Matters
paras.zh: 为什么这一计算机科学突破很重要

paras.en: Massive networks are fundamental to modern technology. Internet infrastructure, transportation systems, social media platforms, and artificial intelligence applications all depend on analyzing complicated webs of interconnected information.
paras.zh: 大规模网络是现代技术的基础。互联网基础设施、交通系统、社交媒体平台和人工智能应用程序都依赖于分析复杂的互连信息网络。

paras.en: In many situations, obtaining a perfectly exact distance is less important than producing a dependable estimate quickly. When networks contain enormous numbers of connections, the ability to balance accuracy and speed becomes especially valuable.
paras.zh: 在许多情况下，获得完全精确的距离并不比快速生成可靠的估计更重要。当网络包含大量连接时，平衡准确性和速度的能力变得尤其有价值。

paras.en: Gupta's research strengthens the mathematical foundations of algorithms designed to handle these challenges. Although the findings are theoretical and do not establish immediate improvements to specific commercial systems, they offer a better way to approach distance calculations in large networks.
paras.zh: 古普塔的研究加强了旨在应对这些挑战的算法的数学基础。尽管这些发现是理论上的，并没有立即改进特定的商业系统，但它们提供了一种更好的方法来处理大型网络中的距离计算。

paras.en: The work also provides insight into how the overall structure of a network can be understood through carefully selected local connections. By improving how these relationships are sampled and analyzed, researchers can move closer to efficiently estimating distances between every pair of points in a massive system.
paras.zh: 这项工作还提供了如何通过精心选择的本地连接来理解网络整体结构的见解。通过改进这些关系的采样和分析方式，研究人员可以更有效地估计大型系统中每对点之间的距离。

paras.en: Progress in theoretical computer science often comes through incremental refinements rather than dramatic changes. Improving an influential result that dates back to 1996 therefore represents a meaningful advance.
paras.zh: 理论计算机科学的进步通常来自于渐进的改进，而不是巨大的变化。因此，改进一项可追溯到 1996 年的有影响力的结果代表着一项有意义的进步。

paras.en: By extending a longstanding accuracy guarantee without increasing overall runtime, the new algorithm pushes beyond an important mathematical boundary and strengthens the techniques underlying some of today's most complex connected systems.
paras.zh: 通过在不增加总体运行时间的情况下扩展长期的准确性保证，新算法突破了重要的数学边界，并增强了当今一些最复杂的互联系统的基础技术。

paras.en: Materials provided by Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由印度甘地讷格尔理工学院提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。
